t: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
The result: every practitioner who assesses a participant or writes a plan for us is confi
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: The result: every practitioner who assesses a participant or writes a plan for us is confirmed suitable by the Commission. Each is supervised by a suitable clinical supervisor and keeps their skills current. The Rules are applied in every plan, and restrictive practices are reduced and eliminated. This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-01 Behaviour Support in the NDIS Policy (Specialist Behaviour Support), commitments C1 to C15. "The Rules" in this procedure means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018. "The Commission" is the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.

t: Start this procedure when: we engage, employ or contract a practitioner or a clinical supe
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Start this procedure when: we engage, employ or contract a practitioner or a clinical supervisor a clinical supervision session is due a practitioner's suitability outcome changes or is due to be reconsidered a quarter ends, or the Rules change. Who acts: The Service Manager confirms suitability, names the clinical supervisor, releases the practitioner and keeps the dates. The clinical supervisor holds each session, checks the plans and reviews restrictive practices. The practitioner brings their work and tells us the same day of any change to their outcome. The Quality Manager checks for changes to the Rules. The Chief Executive reports to the governing body. In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole practitioner engages an external clinical supervisor and a substitute in writing (step 4). The external clinical supervisor does the Service Manager's checks on the sole practitioner's own work: steps 1 to 3, 8, 23, 24 and 26. Everything else the sole practitioner does themselves, including the register entries (step 22), the briefing (step 28) and the Quality Manager's and the Chief Executive's steps. The one exception is the decision whether an incident is reportable, which the external clinical supervisor makes with them. The independent contact for concerns, named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, reads and signs the quarterly summary (step 30). If one person is both Service Manager and clinical supervisor for a practitioner, the Chief Executive does steps 8 and 23 for them.

t: Our registration includes specialist behaviour support. Check the certificate of registrat
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Our registration includes specialist behaviour support. Check the certificate of registration. Without it, nobody assesses a participant or writes a plan (Practice Standards Rules, section 7(3)). You know the practitioner's name and the date they will start. You can open REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register, REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register. You have a blank FRM-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Clinical Supervision Record. Open one at step 1 for each new practitioner. For a session, you have the practitioner's caseload list by file number and the drafts or plans for checking. You also have the use data for each regulated restrictive practice and their development log. The practitioner sends these 2 business days before the session (our standard). You have a copy of the Rules and of the restrictive practice authorisation law of [state or territory]. You have the Commission's phone number, 1800 035 544, and the email address of its practitioner team, ndispractitioners@ndiscommission.gov.au.

t: A person who is not yet considered suitable must not do any part of an assessment or a pla
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: A person who is not yet considered suitable must not do any part of an assessment or a plan, even when supervised. The Rules say a practitioner must provide the specialist behaviour support services (section 17). A plan written by anyone else breaches our registration, and it may put a restrictive practice in place that no suitable person has checked. A supervisor below the level in Decision table 1 does not count as clinical supervision. The practitioner is then unsupervised in practice, whatever the diary says. Stop the session and use the substitute. A plan with a regulated restrictive practice that skips the check has never been tested against the Rules. It can be lodged with the Commissioner and relied on by the people who carry it out. A supervision record is not an incident report. The Commission's clock for a reportable incident runs from the day we become aware, and waiting for the next session loses days. A participant's name in a supervision record spreads private information to more readers. Use the file number only.

t: Steps
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)

t: Ask the practitioner for the Commission's written suitability outcome.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Ask the practitioner for the Commission's written suitability outcome. Service Manager Ask every new practitioner, whether employee, contractor or agency. Open FRM-SBS-01 for them. Copy from the outcome its date, the decision (suitable, with or without conditions), the pathway used (self-assessment or new entry-level) and any conditions. The outcome shows no capability level. The level comes from the practitioner's own self-assessment against the Positive Behaviour Support Capability Framework, endorsed by their clinical supervisor, and is recorded at step 4. For a new entry-level practitioner, ask for the Commission's reconsideration letter and copy its date and deadline. Check that the name matches their identity documents. Read the result with Decision table 2. You hold the outcome, or you know there is none. FRM-SBS-01 Q2, Q6, Q7 and Q8 Before the practitioner is given any participant (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support Rules, s 17 and s 18)

t: Confirm the outcome from the Commission's own evidence.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Confirm the outcome from the Commission's own evidence. the outcome is missing or unclear, or a new entry-level reconsideration deadline has passed with no decision from the Commission Service Manager The primary evidence is the outcome letter the practitioner downloads from the Commission's provider portal. Sight it and write the date you saw it. If it is missing or unclear, the practitioner asks the Commission's practitioner team by email and shows you the reply; write the date and any reference. The Commission runs no provider-facing confirmation service, so allow time. Do not accept the practitioner's word alone. You have seen the Commission's own evidence, or you know there is none. FRM-SBS-01 Q8 Before the practitioner is given any participant (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support Rules, s 17 and s 18)

t: Confirm the pre-engagement checks are complete.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Confirm the pre-engagement checks are complete. Worker screening, banning orders and professional registration keep people who must not do this work away from participants. A practitioner who has not cleared them is unsafe to allocate, even when the Commission considers them suitable. Service Manager For an employee, use PRO-HRM-01 Human Resource Management Procedure and FRM-HRM-01 Worker Screening and Credential Checklist. For a contractor or agency practitioner, use PRO-HRM-07 Contractor and External Provider Verification Procedure, which also sets their written agreement. The checks are a current worker screening clearance for this risk assessed role. They also include a search of the NDIS Provider Register for a banning order under every name the person has used. Check qualifications, and professional registration where the profession needs it. Every check is complete and in date, or the practitioner is not given any participant. FRM-SBS-01 Q9 Before the practitioner starts any work (Practice Standards (Worker Screening) Rules, s 13)

t: Name the clinical supervisor and a substitute.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Name the clinical supervisor and a substitute. Service Manager Use Decision table 1 for the level each must hold. Levels are read from each person's self-assessment against the Positive Behaviour Support Capability Framework, endorsed by their own clinical supervisor, never from the Commission's outcome. Record the practitioner's endorsed level, who endorsed it and the date at FRM-SBS-01 Q6. Each supervisor must be trained in clinical supervision and must not supervise anyone who supervises them. Each declares any conflict of interest on FRM-GOV-01 Conflict of Interest Declaration Form. If no one inside can do it, engage an outside clinical supervisor in writing. The agreement covers confidentiality, the NDIS Code of Conduct, how they raise a concern and who owns the records. For a new entry-level practitioner it is the supervisor agreement the Commission expects, and the supervisor is at proficient level or above. A sole practitioner engages the outside supervisor. Add an outside clinical supervisor to REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register as the holder of the position, with the substitute as first delegate. The practitioner has a named clinical supervisor and a named substitute who meet the standard. FRM-SBS-01 Q6 and Q10 to Q13, and REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register (position holder and first delegate) for an outside supervisor Before the start-up session (our standard)

t: Hold the start-up session with the practitioner.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Hold the start-up session with the practitioner. Clinical supervisor Agree how supervision will work. Cover how often (Decision table 1), how long and how it is held. Cover how the practitioner asks for an extra session and how they raise a disagreement. Say what stays confidential and its limits: duty of care, the law and audits. Record the answers on FRM-SBS-01 as a start-up session. Keep that record open until step 8. The practitioner and the clinical supervisor have a written arrangement. FRM-SBS-01 Q1, Q3 and Q14 Before the practitioner is given any participant (our standard)

t: Agree the practitioner's professional development plan.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Agree the practitioner's professional development plan. Clinical supervisor Set the hours from Decision table 1 for the next 12 months. Name the topics. At least half are on positive behaviour support or other evidence-informed behaviour support practice. Use the higher number if the practitioner's professional body asks for more. Supervision sessions do not count towards the hours. Agree the dates and who pays or allows the time. There is a dated plan the practitioner can follow. FRM-SBS-01 Q15 and REG-HRM-02 At the start-up session, then every 12 months (our standard)

t: Check that the practitioner understands the Rules.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Check that the practitioner understands the Rules. the practitioner is new to us, 12 months have passed since their last Rules check, or the Rules have changed Clinical supervisor The practitioner first completes training on the Rules. Then they show you they can explain and apply them, using a plan of theirs or a sample plan. They must cover the five kinds of regulated restrictive practice and the conditions in section 21. They must cover the plan deadlines, consultation and notice, the approved form and lodgement, and the duty to reduce and eliminate. They must also cover the duties of implementing providers, and the note for each state or territory where they work. This is the one annual knowledge check: it also serves POL-SBS-02 C2 and PRO-SBS-02 step 2, and is recorded once, on FRM-HRM-07 Training and Competency Assessment Record and in REG-HRM-02. If they do not meet it yet, agree what to learn and repeat the check. The practitioner has passed a recorded check on the Rules, or does not work alone. FRM-SBS-01 Q16 Before their first assessment or plan work, then every 12 months (our standard)

t: Release the practitioner by adding them to the suitable list.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Release the practitioner by adding them to the suitable list. Service Manager Release them only when steps 1 to 7 are recorded. Write the release date on FRM-SBS-01, with any limits from the conditions on the outcome. Then the clinical supervisor and the practitioner sign the start-up record, which is signed here and not at the end of the session. The practitioner then does only the work the conditions allow. Add them to the suitable list in REG-HRM-02, with their outcome date, pathway, endorsed level, conditions and any reconsideration letter date. Everyone who gives out assessment or plan work reads that list first. The practitioner is on the suitable list and can be given participants. FRM-SBS-01 Q17 The day the Rules check is passed (our standard)

t: Confirm that the practitioner's suitability is unchanged and that the supervision meets th
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Confirm that the practitioner's suitability is unchanged and that the supervision meets the standard. Clinical supervisor Ask the practitioner to confirm the date, the pathway and the conditions on their outcome, any reconsideration letter, and whether their endorsed self-assessment has changed. Compare them with the last record. If nothing has changed, record "No change" at Q7; Q6 to Q13 then stand as last recorded. Check that you still meet Decision table 1. Ask whether you or the practitioner have a conflict of interest with any participant on today's list. If anything has changed, use Decision table 2. If you do not meet the standard, stop and use the substitute. The record shows the practitioner's suitability and the supervisor's level on the day of the session. FRM-SBS-01 Q1, Q3, Q4, Q6, Q7 and Q10 to Q12 At the start of every session, no later than the longest gap in Decision table 1 after the last one (our standard)

t: Review the actions from the last session.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Review the actions from the last session. Clinical supervisor Go through each action and mark it done, open or overdue. For an overdue action, ask why and agree a new date. Never delete an earlier due date. Every earlier action has a status. FRM-SBS-01 Q5 At the start of every session (our standard)

t: Review each participant's work that the practitioner brought.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Review each participant's work that the practitioner brought. Clinical supervisor Use file numbers only, never names. For each, write the kind of work, the plan version and what you decided. Read each handover and training record (FRM-SBS-04) and review record (FRM-SBS-05) made since the last session. Then list every participant on the caseload who has not been discussed in the last 3 months. Put each one on this agenda if there is time, or fix a date. Every participant on the caseload has been discussed within 3 months, or has a date. FRM-SBS-01 Q18 and Q19 Every participant at least once every 3 months (our standard)

t: Check which plans and reviews are overdue or due soon.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Check which plans and reviews are overdue or due soon. Clinical supervisor Read the engagement dates and plan dates in REG-SBS-01. The Rules set these deadlines. After a regulated restrictive practice is used, the clocks start when we are engaged to write the plan. An interim plan is due within 1 month. A comprehensive plan is due within 6 months (section 19). A comprehensive plan that contains a regulated restrictive practice is reviewed at least every 12 months, and sooner after a change that needs the plan amended (section 22). For every other plan a 12-month review is our standard, and an interim plan's review date is the comprehensive plan's due date. A plan with a regulated restrictive practice is lodged with the Commissioner "as soon as practicable" (section 24(1)). The Rules use those words. Our working limit is 5 business days from the day the plan is finalised. List what is overdue or due in the next 4 weeks, with the action to meet each. Ask which plans you checked earlier have been lodged. No deadline is missed without someone knowing and acting. FRM-SBS-01 Q20 and Q21 At every session (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support Rules, s 19, s 22 and s 24(1))

t: Check that each plan was checked against the Rules before it was finalised.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Check that each plan was checked against the Rules before it was finalised. A plan with a regulated restrictive practice can limit a person's freedom for years. A plan that has not been checked against the Rules can break them and still be lodged and relied on. Clinical supervisor List each plan finalised or reviewed since the last session, and each draft waiting. A plan with a regulated restrictive practice has its own recorded test. Find the clinical supervisor's decision at FRM-SBS-02 Q28 and Q29, under PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). For a review, find the check on FRM-SBS-05, under PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure. The check must be dated before the plan was finalised. For any other plan that Decision table 1 names, test every row of Decision table 3 yourself. Approve a plan only when every row passes. Otherwise return it with the changes needed, or hold it. If a plan with a restrictive practice was finalised with no recorded check, tell the Service Manager the same day. Do the test now and raise an entry in REG-QMS-01. A plan you wrote is tested by a different clinical supervisor. If the practitioner disagrees with your decision, see "If it goes wrong". Each plan has a recorded check dated before it was finalised, or a gap that is being fixed. FRM-SBS-01 Q22 and Q23 At every session. A draft with no recorded check is tested within 5 business days of arriving, or 2 business days for an interim plan (our standard)

t: Review the regulated restrictive practices on the practitioner's caseload.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Review the regulated restrictive practices on the practitioner's caseload. Clinical supervisor For each practice, read the use data since the last session and the trend. Ask what reduction step was agreed, who takes it and by when. Ask whether any use was an emergency use, or was outside the plan or outside an authorisation, and what followed. Send any such use to the Service Manager the same day (Decision table 4). Do not accept "no change" as a default. Ask what must happen first and fix a date to look again. Each practice has a reduction step with an owner and a date, or a reason and a date to look again. FRM-SBS-01 Q24 to Q26 At every session (our standard)

t: Observe or read a sample of the practitioner's own work.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Observe or read a sample of the practitioner's own work. Clinical supervisor Choose one. Sit in on a consultation or an assessment visit. Watch a recorded session, with consent. Or read a full draft assessment, plan or data analysis. Pick work you have not seen before. Write what you saw and what you found. This shows that supervision looks at the work, and not only at the practitioner's account of it. The clinical supervisor has seen the practitioner's work first hand. FRM-SBS-01 Q27 At least once every 3 months (our standard)

t: Give the practitioner feedback on their work.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Give the practitioner feedback on their work. Clinical supervisor Name what they do well and what to build, with an example for each. Include comments from participants or their representatives. Seek those comments at least once every 12 months. Then ask what the practitioner thinks of their caseload and of this supervision, and write down their reply. Your feedback and the practitioner's views are on the record. FRM-SBS-01 Q28 and Q29 At every session (our standard)

t: Ask the practitioner about their wellbeing and any need for a debrief.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Ask the practitioner about their wellbeing and any need for a debrief. Clinical supervisor This work is hard. Always ask after a serious incident, a use of a restrictive practice or a distressing consultation. Offer a debrief and a referral to [employee assistance or other support]. Do not wait for the next session when the need is urgent. Wellbeing has been asked about and any support is agreed. FRM-SBS-01 Q30 At every session, and a debrief within 2 business days when asked for (our standard)

t: Record the professional development the practitioner has done.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Record the professional development the practitioner has done. Clinical supervisor Write each activity with its date, hours and topic since the last session. Add the total for this 12 months and compare it with Decision table 1. If the practitioner is behind, agree dated catch-up steps. Note any training they need, so the Service Manager can update their training plan in REG-HRM-02. The hours and progress are known, and training needs reach the training plan. FRM-SBS-01 Q31 and REG-HRM-02 At every session (our standard)

t: Start the process that Decision table 4 names.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Start the process that Decision table 4 names. A supervision record is not an incident report. Waiting for the next session to report a safety or reportable matter can make a notice to the Commission late. the session raised a safety, conduct, reportable or Rules compliance concern Clinical supervisor Phone the person the table names. Then write on FRM-SBS-01 what you did and give the number of the incident report, complaint or other record. The Quality Manager decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the Commission. The Commission's clock runs from the day we become aware: within 24 hours of becoming aware where the incident involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm; otherwise within 5 business days (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents Rules, s 20 and s 21). A worker must tell a supervisor or manager "as soon as possible" (section 19). Our standard is the same day. The concern is in the right process, and the record shows which. FRM-SBS-01 Q32 and Q33 The same day (our standard)

t: Agree the new actions and the next session date.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Agree the new actions and the next session date. Clinical supervisor Give each action one owner and a due date. Set the next date no later than the longest gap in Decision table 1. Put it in both diaries before the practitioner leaves. Everyone knows what happens next and when. FRM-SBS-01 Q34 and Q35 At the end of every session (our standard)

t: Sign the record.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Sign the record. Clinical supervisor and practitioner Each person signs, or confirms electronically with their name, date and time. Do not change a signed record. Add a correction as a new version, with the reason. The record is complete. FRM-SBS-01 Sign-off The same day, and no later than 1 business day after the session (our standard)

t: Enter the session in REG-HRM-02.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Enter the session in REG-HRM-02. Service Manager Enter the date, the supervisor and their endorsed level, the development hours and the next due date. Note whether the session was on time. Enter no participant names. File the signed record in the practitioner's supervision file. The register shows the session and the next due date. REG-HRM-02 2 business days after the record is signed (our standard)

t: Check each practitioner's dates in REG-HRM-02.
w: Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
x: Check each practitioner's dates in REG-HRM-02. Service Manager Read the suitable list and look for six things. First, a new entry-level reconsideration deadline within 3 months: ask what the practitioner has lodged with the Commission (the self-assessment and the endorsement tool), and look again every month. Second, an outcome the Commission has revoked, limited or questioned, or an endorsed self-assessment missing: use Decision table 2. Third, a session overdue past the longest gap in Decision table 1: see "If it goes wrong". Fourth, a Rules check due within 1 month: book step 7. Fifth, development hours behind the plan at 6 months or 12 months: ask the clinical supervisor to agree catch-up steps. Sixth, a supervisor or substitute who no longer meets Decision table 1. t: Restrictive Practices Policy (Specialist Behaviour Support)
This policy sets what [Provider name] commits to when a Behaviour Support Practitioner pro
x: This policy sets what [Provider name] commits to when a Behaviour Support Practitioner proposes a regulated restrictive practice for a participant's behaviour support plan. It is for participants, their families and advocates, our practitioners, the providers who carry out our plans, and the people who check our work.

t: Every Behaviour Support Practitioner and Clinical Supervisor at [Provider name], whether a
x: Every Behaviour Support Practitioner and Clinical Supervisor at [Provider name], whether an employee or a contractor. Every interim and comprehensive behaviour support plan we write or review that holds, or may come to hold, a regulated restrictive practice. Every state and territory where we work, and every setting where the participant lives or receives supports. Specialist behaviour support only. A provider that only carries out plans, or that also uses a practice itself, follows POL-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Policy for its own use. Its monthly reports follow POL-BSP-05 Monitoring and Reporting the Use of Regulated Restrictive Practices Policy. "The Behaviour Support Rules" in this policy means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018. A "practice" is a regulated restrictive practice, one of the five kinds in section 6 of those Rules.

x: We will write down, for every state and territory where we work, how a restrictive practice is authorised there. Each note names the authorising body, who must consent, the practices that are prohibited and the evidence to lodge. The Clinical Supervisor checks each note against its source at least every 6 months, and on any announced change to the law, the authorising body's process or its guidance.

t: We will make sure each Behaviour Support Practitioner knows the Behaviour Support Rules be
x: We will make sure each Behaviour Support Practitioner knows the Behaviour Support Rules before they propose a practice. They also know the note for each state or territory where they work. x: We will make sure each Behaviour Support Practitioner does learning on restrictive practices and their risks at least every 12 months. We record it in REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register.

x: We will ask each participant who they want involved before we contact anyone else. Where the participant refuses to involve a family member or carer, we record the refusal and the reasons as our evidence of all reasonable steps under section 20(3)(e) of the Behaviour Support Rules, and the Clinical Supervisor records whether any further step is reasonable. We offer an independent advocate and use the communication supports the participant needs.

t: We will give the participant and each person we must notify written notice of our intentio
x: We will give the participant and each person we must notify written notice of our intention to include a practice, in a format they can use. For a comprehensive plan we give it at least 5 business days before the Clinical Supervisor decides. For an interim plan we give it at the first meeting and at least 2 business days before the decision, so that the consultation fits inside the 1 month limit in section 19(2)(a). Where the risk is immediate, we give it before the plan is finalised and record why.

x: We will explain the risk of harm, the risks of the practice and the alternatives to each person we consult. We ask each person to say the risks back in their own way. We record every view and every objection in full.

x: We will build the strategies with the participant, their support network and each implementing provider. Changes to the environment, new skills and community activities come first. We apply them, or record why we cannot yet, before we rely on a practice.

x: We will put a practice in a plan only after the Clinical Supervisor has confirmed in writing that it meets every condition in the Behaviour Support Rules. It must be a last resort, the least restrictive response, in proportion to the risk of harm and used for the shortest possible time. A practitioner never decides on a practice they proposed. The Practitioner lodges every plan that holds a practice with the NDIS Commission within 5 business days of finalising it. We do this whether or not authorisation is needed or given.

x: We will never include a practice that the state or territory prohibits. We will not call a practice authorised until the authorising body has said so in writing. x: We will put a reduction and elimination strategy in every plan that holds a practice, interim plans included. It sets the steps, the measure, the end point and a review date. x: We will support each implementing provider to use a practice only within the plan and its authorisation. t: Behaviour Support Rules: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices a
x: Behaviour Support Rules: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018. Plan: an interim or a comprehensive behaviour support plan. Clinical Lead: the most senior Clinical Supervisor, who owns clinical practice at [Provider name] (POL-SBS-03 defines the role). In a sole practitioner provider, the outside Clinical Supervisor. Regulated restrictive practice (practice): one of five kinds named in section 6 of the Behaviour Support Rules. They are seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint and environmental restraint. Behaviour Support Practitioner: a person the Commissioner considers suitable to do behaviour support assessments and write plans that may hold a practice. Clinical Supervisor: the person who gives clinical supervision to our practitioners and decides whether a practice goes into a plan. Implementing provider: a provider that carries out a plan and may use the practice. Authorisation: the approval, consent or other process of a state or territory, however described, that must be met before a practice is used. Authorising body: the body, tribunal or officer that gives authorisation. Note: our one page record, kept in REG-QMS-03, of how a state or territory authorises practices. Last resort: used only in response to a risk of harm, and only after evidence-based, person-centred, proactive strategies have been explored and applied. Reduction and elimination strategy: the written steps, measure, end point and review date that lead to a practice being reduced and ended. Consultation record: FRM-SBS-02, the record of who we consulted about a practice and what we decided. High-risk practice: a practice the NDIS Commission's guidance says must never be in a behaviour support plan, such as prone or supine restraint, a pin-down or take-down, a restraint that restricts breathing or circulation, a punitive or aversive practice, over-correction or the seclusion of a child. State or territory authorisation never makes one acceptable. NDIS Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission. The Commissioner is its head. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

t: Control
Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
The result: a regulated restrictive practice goes into a participant's behaviour support p
x: The result: a regulated restrictive practice goes into a participant's behaviour support plan only after the participant and the people they choose have been consulted. They know the risks and the alternatives. The practice meets the Behaviour Support Rules and the authorisation process of the state or territory. The plan also holds a way to reduce the practice and end it. This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Policy (Specialist Behaviour Support), C1 to C15. "The Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018. A "practice" is a regulated restrictive practice, one of the five kinds in section 6 of those Rules. A "restrictive practice" in the wider sense is any practice or intervention that has the effect of restricting the rights or freedom of movement of a person with disability (NDIS Act 2013, section 9); a practice is regulated only if it meets section 6. A "plan" is an interim or a comprehensive behaviour support plan. A "high-risk practice" is one the NDIS Commission's guidance says must never be in a plan (POL-SBS-02 C15).

t: A signature is not an authorisation. The participant's, a guardian's and ours do not make
x: A signature is not an authorisation. The participant's, a guardian's and ours do not make a practice lawful. Only the authorisation process of the state or territory does. A practice used without it breaches the registration conditions and can be a reportable incident. Never include a practice the state or territory prohibits. Never include a high-risk practice the NDIS Commission says must never be in a plan: prone or supine restraint, a pin-down or take-down, a restraint that restricts breathing or circulation, a punitive or aversive practice, over-correction or the seclusion of a child. State or territory authorisation never makes one acceptable. Decision table 2 row 16 tests this first. Silence is not agreement, and being told is not understanding. We use data, observation and information about what sets it off and keeps it going. The Behaviour Support Rules call it a functional behavioural assessment. assessment report: the written record of the behaviour support assessment. We write it on FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template. plan: a behaviour support plan, interim or comprehensive. interim plan: a plan written quickly to reduce immediate risk while the assessment is done. comprehensive plan: the full plan that rests on the assessment. regulated restrictive practice: seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint or environmental restraint, as section 6 of the Behaviour Support Rules defines them. engagement date: the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used, whichever is earlier (ground rule 7). support network: the family, carers, friends and advocates the participant chooses. decision maker: a person with legal authority to decide for the participant, for example a guardian. engagement date: the earliest of the date we agree, in any form, to develop the plan, the date we first do assessment or plan work, and the date the service agreement starts; or the date a regulated restrictive practice is first used after the referral reaches us, if that is earlier. Ground rule 7 explains it. in force: a plan is in force from the date the Practitioner finalises and signs it. Commissioner: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commissioner. The Commission is the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Policy

t: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
w: Functional behaviour assessments and behaviour support plans

t: The result: every participant we assess gets an assessment that finds their unmet needs an
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: The result: every participant we assess gets an assessment that finds their unmet needs and the function of their behaviour. They get a plan written with them and with the people who carry it out. Those providers accept it, and a plan with a regulated restrictive practice reaches the Commissioner on time. This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Policy, C1 to C14. "Behaviour Support Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

t: Start this procedure when: we receive a referral for a behaviour support assessment or pla
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Start this procedure when: we receive a referral for a behaviour support assessment or plan we take over a participant from another specialist provider a review under PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure says a plan must change, or the assessment revisit date is within 30 days. Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this procedure. A provider that only carries out plans uses PRO-BSP-05 Supporting the Assessment and Development of Behaviour Support Plans Procedure. Who acts: The Service Manager logs the referral, sets the dates, allocates the people, prepares each lodgement and keeps the register. The Clinical Lead triages the risk. The Practitioner does every assessment, writes every plan and lodges it in the Commission's portal. The Clinical Supervisor checks each report and each plan. The Quality Manager and the Chief Executive check the register and receive anything late. The Quality Manager decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the Commission. In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole Practitioner holds the Service Manager, Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles, except that the decision whether an incident is reportable is made by the outside Clinical Supervisor with them. The Clinical Supervisor is always someone outside, is the Clinical Lead for this procedure, and does the Service Manager's checks on the sole Practitioner's own work. Where a step says to tell another role, a sole Practitioner writes it on the plan row and tells the Clinical Supervisor. Terms in this procedure: Practitioner: an NDIS behaviour support practitioner, a person the Commissioner considers suitable to assess behaviour and write plans (Behaviour Support Rules, section 5). plan: a behaviour support plan, interim or comprehensive. assessment report: the written record of the assessment, on FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template. cover sheet: the record of how a plan was checked, shared and lodged, on FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record. plan row: one line of REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register for one plan version. implementing provider: a provider that carries out the strategies in a plan. regulated restrictive practice: seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint or environmental restraint (Behaviour Support Rules, section 6). engagement date: the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used, whichever is earlier (POL-SBS-03 ground rule 7). Where that use was before the referral reached us, the date the referral reached us. A later date named in a service agreement never moves it. in force: a plan is in force from the date the Practitioner finalises and signs it.

t: You are a Practitioner the Commissioner considers suitable, or you are supporting one. You
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: You are a Practitioner the Commissioner considers suitable, or you are supporting one. You can open REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register. You have FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record, on paper or in the system. You have the participant's communication preferences: FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form. You know where FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form is kept. You know your Clinical Supervisor's name and how to reach them. You know the state or territory where the participant lives. Its law decides who can consent and which practices need authorisation.

t: If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. Tell the Service Manager after. A delay can cost a
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. Tell the Service Manager after. A delay can cost a life. Only a suitable Practitioner may assess or write. Anyone else doing it breaks a condition of our registration (Behaviour Support Rules, sections 17 and 18). No consent, no assessment. Gathering information without valid consent breaches the participant's privacy and their right to decide. Look for pain and illness first. A plan built on the wrong cause leaves the participant in pain and does not work. The clocks start at engagement. Where a regulated restrictive practice led to our engagement, missing the 1 month or the 6 month limit breaks a condition of registration (Behaviour Support Rules, section 19). A restrictive practice never enters through the back door. One that reaches a plan without consultation, notice and authorisation can be used on the participant unlawfully. Lodge whether or not the practice is authorised. The Rules ask for the plan either way (Behaviour Support Rules, section 24(2)). A plan nobody accepted may not be followed. Workers who have not seen it may respond in unsafe or uneven ways.

t: Steps
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure

t: Log the referral.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Log the referral. Service Manager Write down the date, who referred the participant and why, in the referrer's words. Say if we are taking over from another specialist provider. The referral is on record with its date. FRM-SBS-03 Q1, Q2 Same business day (our standard)

t: Triage the risk.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Triage the risk. A participant at immediate risk, or a regulated restrictive practice already in use, cannot wait for a full assessment. Delay leaves people unsafe and can break the 1 month limit. Clinical Lead, or a Practitioner the Clinical Lead names If anyone is in danger now, tell the referrer to call 000. Ask what has happened, whether a regulated restrictive practice has been used, who uses it, how often, and who is at risk. Choose the row in Decision table 1. If the row needs an interim plan, tell the Service Manager now and start PRO-SBS-06 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). Do not wait for the assessment. We know whether this is urgent and which plan is needed first. FRM-SBS-03 Q4 Within 1 business day of the referral (our standard)

t: Confirm we can take the referral.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Confirm we can take the referral. Service Manager Check that the participant chose us and that our registration covers specialist behaviour support. Check that a suitable Practitioner is free, their NDIS plan funds behaviour support and a service agreement is signed (AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template). Open the plan row in REG-SBS-01 and write the engagement date: the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used, whichever is earlier. Where that use was before the referral reached us, use the date the referral reached us. Starting assessment or plan work counts as agreeing to develop the plan. A later start date in the agreement never moves it. We have agreed to take the referral, the plan row is open and the engagement date is recorded. FRM-SBS-03 Q3; REG-SBS-01 col A Before any assessment work starts. The same day where risk is urgent (our standard)

t: Work out the due dates.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Work out the due dates. Service Manager Use Decision table 1, counting from the engagement date set at step 3 (the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used, whichever is earlier). Where a regulated restrictive practice was used and led to our engagement, the interim plan is due 1 month after the engagement date. The comprehensive plan is due 6 months after it. In every other case the comprehensive plan is due 84 days after it. The assessment report is always due 49 days after it. Put each date in the diary of the Practitioner and the Service Manager. Every due date is on the plan row and in two diaries. FRM-SBS-03 Q5 Same day as step 3 (our standard)

t: Allocate a Practitioner and a Clinical Supervisor.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Allocate a Practitioner and a Clinical Supervisor. An assessment or plan written by a person the Commissioner has not found suitable breaks a condition of our registration. Service Manager Confirm the Practitioner's suitability under PRO-SBS-01 Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). Check a contractor the same way. Do not allocate anyone who is still waiting for the Commissioner's decision. Name the Clinical Supervisor. A sole Practitioner names an outside Clinical Supervisor. A suitable Practitioner and a Clinical Supervisor are named on the plan row. FRM-SBS-03 Q6, Q7 Within 2 business days of step 3 (our standard)

t: Ask the participant for consent.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Ask the participant for consent. A family member, carer or provider cannot consent for an adult unless they hold legal authority. Collecting or sharing information without valid consent breaches the participant's privacy and their right to decide. Practitioner Meet the participant in the way that suits them. Use their communication preferences. Explain what the assessment is, what we will collect, from whom, who will see it, and that they can stop at any time. Use Decision table 2 to find who decides. Offer an independent advocate. Ask for consent to assess, to ask named people and services for information, and to share the report. Record each answer, including each no, on FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form. The participant has decided in their own way, and we know who we may ask and who we may tell. FRM-SBS-03 Q9 to Q14 Before you collect any information. First meeting within 10 business days of the engagement date (our standard)

t: Ask for a health review.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Ask for a health review. A behaviour can be the only way a participant can say they are in pain or unwell. A plan built on the wrong cause leaves the participant in pain and will not work. Practitioner With consent, ask the participant's doctor or another health practitioner to review pain, illness, medicines and their side effects, sleep, hearing, vision, sensory needs and mental health. Do not diagnose. Do not advise a change of medicine. Only the prescriber decides that. If the review cannot happen quickly, record what you asked, of whom and when. A health practitioner has looked for health causes, or a dated request is on record with a date to chase it. FRM-SBS-03 Q24 Ask within 5 business days of consent (our standard)

t: Ask for what is already known.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Ask for what is already known. Practitioner With consent, ask for earlier assessments and plans, allied health and medical reports, school or day service records, and assessments by other providers and mainstream services. Ask each implementing provider for its incident reports and behaviour records (FRM-BSP-04 Behaviour Record). If we are taking over from another specialist provider, ask for the current plan, its lodgement and authorisation details and its data. Our own clocks still run from our engagement date. Record what you asked for and what arrived. Every source is listed with its date, and each gap is written down. FRM-SBS-03 Q16, Q18 to Q20 Within 10 business days of consent (our standard)

t: Collect direct and indirect data.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Collect direct and indirect data. Practitioner Watch the participant yourself in each setting where the behaviour happens, at the times it happens. Interview the participant, their support network and workers. Use behaviour charts and rating tools. Record the period and the settings, and say why they are long enough. Workers and family supply records. They do not assess. The assessment rests on what you saw and what people told you, from every setting. FRM-SBS-03 Q15, Q17 Finish before the assessment report is due, 49 days after the engagement date (our standard)

t: Ask the participant what matters to them.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Ask the participant what matters to them. Practitioner Ask in their way and in their words. Cover their strengths, likes and goals, what is going well and what is not, culture and language, how they communicate, their history, and what home and routines are like. Ask only about history they choose to share. If the participant is Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, ask who in their community they want to advise us. The assessment is about the whole person, their own words are in it and their unmet needs are known. FRM-SBS-03 Q21 to Q23, Q25 to Q28 Within 10 business days of consent (our standard)

t: Describe each behaviour of concern.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Describe each behaviour of concern. Practitioner Write what an observer can see and hear, not what you think it means. Record how often, how long and how intense it is, using a scale you name. Record early warning signs, how it ends, who is at risk and how seriously. Rate the risk of harm. Anyone can recognise and count each behaviour, and the risk is rated. FRM-SBS-03 Q29 to Q32 Before the assessment report is due (our standard)

t: Work out the function of each behaviour.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Work out the function of each behaviour. Practitioner Look at setting events, triggers and what follows the behaviour. Write one summary statement for each behaviour. Say what evidence supports it and what would show it wrong. Say which other explanations you ruled out. Name a skill or behaviour that could meet the same need. Each behaviour has a testable function and a replacement skill. FRM-SBS-03 Q33 to Q38 Before the assessment report is due (our standard)

t: Map the participant's other supports and services.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Map the participant's other supports and services. Practitioner List every NDIS and other support the participant uses: health, mental health, education, housing, justice, day and community services. Record what each does, who to contact and what it does when the behaviour happens. Say how they should fit together and what protocol each needs. With the participant's consent, ask each service to agree. We know every service and what each must do for the plan to work across them. FRM-SBS-03 Q44, Q45 Before the assessment report is due (our standard)

t: List every restrictive practice now in use.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: List every restrictive practice now in use. Apart from a single emergency use, a regulated restrictive practice used without authorisation breaks a condition of registration for the provider using it (Behaviour Support Rules, s 9(2)(a)). It can also harm the participant. Practitioner Include any practice, regulated or not, and any practice in an earlier plan. Record who uses it, where, how often and since when. Record whether it is authorised and whether it is in a current plan. If you see a practice that could cause serious harm, such as a restraint that restricts breathing: call 000 if anyone is in danger, tell the person to stop, and tell the Service Manager the same day. If a regulated restrictive practice is in use without authorisation, tell the implementing provider in writing the same day. Then start PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support); the implementing provider notifies the Commission of its own use, and the Quality Manager decides whether it is also reportable by us. If you think a regulated restrictive practice may be needed in the plan (FRM-SBS-03 Q43), tell the Service Manager and start PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) now, before the plan is drafted. Do not recommend a restrictive practice in the report. Every practice in use is on record with its status, and this report adds none. FRM-SBS-03 Q39 to Q43 Same day for a practice that could cause serious harm. Otherwise before the assessment report is due (our standard)

t: Write the assessment report.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Write the assessment report. Practitioner Finish the recommendations in this order: changes to the environment; skills and replacement behaviours; proactive strategies; response strategies. Add the data each implementing provider should collect, the training they need, and chances for the participant to join community activities and learn new skills. Say whether an automated tool was used. Give the report its number. Set the date to revisit it. The report is complete and ready for checking. FRM-SBS-03 Q8, Q46 to Q53, Q56, Q57 Within 49 days of the engagement date (our standard)

t: Check the assessment report.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Check the assessment report. Clinical Supervisor Check that consent is valid, a health cause was looked at, each function rests on evidence and the sources are listed. Check that no restrictive practice is recommended. Sign the sign-off block, or send the report back with the changes needed. The report is signed off, or returned with reasons. FRM-SBS-03 Q58 Within 3 business days of receiving it (our standard)

t: Go through the findings with the participant.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Go through the findings with the participant. Practitioner Use their way of communicating. Say what you found and what you recommend. Ask what they think. Write down any disagreement in their words. Share the findings with others only as the participant agreed. The participant has heard the findings and said what they think. FRM-SBS-03 Q54, Q55 Within 5 business days of step 16 (our standard)

t: Consult each implementing provider.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Consult each implementing provider. Practitioner With the participant's consent, meet each provider that will carry out the plan. Ask what the plan can ask of them in their setting, who does what, what data they can collect and what training they need. Write down each answer. Consult while you write. Do not wait for the draft. Each implementing provider has been heard before the plan is drafted. FRM-BSP-02 Q11 Before you finish the draft (our standard)

t: Draft the plan on a permitted, complete template.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Draft the plan on a permitted, complete template. A plan copied from another participant, or written on a template that misses an item the Commission's checklist requires, puts wrong strategies into practice and can break the Rules. Practitioner Use the Commission's current template, our own approved template that holds every item in the Commission's plan checklist, or the template the state or territory authorising body requires (Behaviour Support Rules, section 23(1)). Check the Commission's website on the day you start for the current checklist and template edition. Write strategies from this participant's assessment report only. Cover every item in the plan content check (FRM-BSP-02 Q13). Give the participant chances to join community activities and learn new skills. Record each source you used. For each regulated restrictive practice, write the protocol the Commission's checklist requires. For a chemical restraint, copy the medication, dose, route and frequency exactly from the prescriber's current order and name the prescriber and the date of the order; you never decide or change a dose. A complete draft exists on a permitted template. FRM-BSP-02 Q1 to Q6 Within 5 business days of step 16, alongside step 17 (our standard)

t: Check that the restrictive practice process is complete.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Check that the restrictive practice process is complete. the draft includes, or may include, a regulated restrictive practice Practitioner PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) was started at step 14, when a practice first looked likely. Check now that the consultation, the notice of intention in a form the participant can understand, the risks, the alternatives and the state or territory authorisation route are all recorded. Do not finalise the plan until FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record is complete and the Clinical Supervisor has decided at PRO-SBS-02 step 22. The practice has been consulted on, noticed and authorised, or it is taken out of the draft. FRM-BSP-02 Q7, Q8 Before the plan is finalised (our standard, giving effect to Behaviour Support Rules, s 20(2) and s 20(4))

t: Give the draft to the participant.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Give the draft to the participant. Practitioner Give it in a form they understand, such as plain words, pictures or a spoken summary. Go through it with them. Offer an independent advocate. Ask what they want changed. Write down their view, and any disagreement in their words. Change the draft where the change keeps them safe. If they still disagree, tell the Clinical Supervisor. The participant has seen the draft and said what they think. FRM-BSP-02 Q9, Q10 Within 1 business day of finishing the draft (our standard)

t: Send the draft to each implementing provider.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Send the draft to each implementing provider. Practitioner With the participant's consent, send the draft for consideration and written acceptance. Ask for an answer within 5 business days. Ask each provider to say yes, yes with changes, or no, and why. Each implementing provider has the draft and a date to answer. FRM-BSP-02 Q11 Within 1 business day of finishing the draft (our standard)

t: Record each provider's answer.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Record each provider's answer. Practitioner Chase any provider that has not answered by business day 3. If a provider asks for a change that keeps the participant safe, change the draft and tell every provider what changed. If a provider declines, or has not answered by business day 5, see If it goes wrong. Every provider's answer, or its silence, is on record. FRM-BSP-02 Q12 Chase at 3 business days. Close at 5 business days after sending (our standard)

t: Check the final draft.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Check the final draft. Clinical Supervisor Check the draft against every item in the plan content check (FRM-BSP-02 Q13, built from the Commission's checklist). Check that each regulated restrictive practice is named, is authorised or going through authorisation, has a complete protocol, a reduction strategy and a review date, and passed Decision table 2 in PRO-SBS-02. Check that the template is permitted and complete. Sign it as cleared, or send it back with the changes needed. The plan is cleared for finalising, or returned with reasons. FRM-BSP-02 Q13, Q14 Within 5 business days of receiving it, or 2 business days for an interim plan (our standard)

t: Finalise and endorse the plan.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Finalise and endorse the plan. Practitioner Sign and date the plan with your name, position, organisation, location and contact details. The date you sign is the date the plan is in force. Set the review date: for a comprehensive plan, no more than 12 months later; for an interim plan, the comprehensive plan's due date, never 12 months. Finalise only when the Clinical Supervisor has cleared the plan and the participant's view and each provider's answer are on record. The plan is in force from the date of signing. FRM-BSP-02 Q15 Within 1 business day of the Clinical Supervisor's clearance at step 24 (our standard). Comprehensive plan: within 84 days of the engagement date (our standard; the step limits add up to about 77 days). Where a regulated restrictive practice was used and led to our engagement: within 6 months (statutory: Behaviour Support Rules, s 19(2)(b)). Interim plan in that case: within 1 month (statutory: s 19(2)(a))

t: Give the plan to the participant and, with consent, to others.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Give the plan to the participant and, with consent, to others. Practitioner Give the participant their plan in a form they understand, with the help they chose. With consent, give a copy to each person in the support network and each implementing provider. Tell each person to remove the old version. Record who got it, how and when. Everyone who should have the plan has the current version, and the participant knows what it says. FRM-BSP-02 Q16 The participant: the same day as step 25. Each implementing provider: within 1 business day of step 25 (our standard)

t: Lodge the plan with the Commissioner.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Lodge the plan with the Commissioner. A plan that contains a regulated restrictive practice must reach the Commissioner whether or not the state or territory has authorised the practice. Lodging late, or not at all, breaks a condition of our registration. the plan contains a regulated restrictive practice Practitioner. The Service Manager prepares the lodgement The Commission's portal requires the Practitioner to send the lodgement. The Service Manager may enter the data and prepare the draft; the Practitioner checks it and sends it. Attach what the Commission requires: the plan, the assessment report (FRM-SBS-03) for a comprehensive plan, each implementing provider's ABN and outlet, and the details of each practice (Behaviour Support Rules, section 23(1)(b)). Save the Commission's confirmation and write down its reference. Lodge each reviewed version in the same way. Tell each implementing provider the lodgement date. If lodgement fails, see If it goes wrong. The Commissioner has the plan and we hold the confirmation. FRM-BSP-02 Q17, Q18 Within 5 business days of step 25 (our standard). The law says as soon as practicable (statutory: Behaviour Support Rules, s 24(1))

t: Start the handover and training for implementing providers.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Start the handover and training for implementing providers. Practitioner Follow PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure. Make a record on FRM-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Handover and Training Record for each contact. Handover has started for each implementing provider. FRM-SBS-04; REG-SBS-01 col AL Within 5 business days of step 26, or 2 business days for an interim plan (our standard)

t: Start a new version of the plan.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Start a new version of the plan. a review under PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure says the plan must change, or the participant's circumstances change, or the assessment revisit date is within 30 days Practitioner Check whether the function may have changed: a new setting, a health change, a loss, a new practice or new data. If it may have, revisit the assessment and update the report first. Each time, record that you looked. Then repeat steps 18 to 28 for the new version, and step 6 if consent has lapsed or the decision maker has changed. Lodge again if the plan contains a regulated restrictive practice. A new version exists, has passed every step, and the old version is ready to close. FRM-SBS-03 Q57; REG-SBS-01 col D Start within 5 business days of the trigger (our standard). For a plan with a regulated restrictive practice, the law says review as soon as practicable after a change that needs an amendment (statutory: Behaviour Support Rules, s 22(a))

t: Update the plan row.
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Update the plan row. Service Manager Copy each answer marked for REG-SBS-01 from FRM-SBS-03 and FRM-BSP-02. Update the status. Mark the old version superseded when its replacement is in force. Check the row against the Entry rules in REG-SBS-01. A correction is a new version of the row, with a reason. The plan row shows where the plan is up to, and every date can be traced to a form. FRM-BSP-02 Q19; REG-SBS-01 col BC; REG-SBS-01 col BE; REG-SBS-01 col BD Within 2 business days of each stage (our standard)

t: Decision table 1: Which plan do we write, and by when? If Then Time limit and source A reg
w: Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure
x: Decision table 1: Which plan do we write, and by when? If Then Time limit and source A regulated restrictive practice was used, and we were engaged because of that use Interim plan first, under PRO-SBS-06 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). Then a comprehensive plan. Both include the practice and go through PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) Interim: 1 month after the engagement date (statutory: Behaviour Support Rules, s 19(2)(a)). Comprehensive: 6 months after it (statutory: s 19(2)(b)). Our target for the comprehensive plan is 84 days There is an immediate risk of harm to the participant or others, but no regulated restrictive practice has been used Interim plan under PRO-SBS-06, written alongside the assessment The time PRO-SBS-06 sets. Comprehensive plan within 84 days of the engagement date (our standard) A regulated restrictive practice is likely to be used soon but has not been used Interim plan under PRO-SBS-06. Start PRO-SBS-02 before the practice is written into any plan Interim plan within 1 month of the engagement date (our standard). Comprehensive plan within 84 days (our standard) There is no immediate risk and no restrictive practice Assessment, then a comprehensive plan Assessment report within 49 days and plan within 84 days of the engagement date (our standard) We are taking over from another specialist provider whose plan is in force Ask for their plan, assessment, lodgement and authorisation details and data. Do not write a fresh interim plan while a current plan is in force: review the plan in force as an NDIS behaviour support practitioner (Behaviour Support Rules, s 22), adopt or amend it, lodge the reviewed version if it contains a regulated restrictive practice, and start our own assessment. This follows the NDIS Commission's position statement of February 2026. If a regulated restrictive practice is being used outside the plan, or the plan has lapsed, row 1 applies Reviewed plan lodged within 5 business days of our review (our standard). Comprehensive plan within 84 days of the engagement date (our standard). Section 19 is not triggered by a takeover of a lodged plan that is in force (NDIS Commission position statement, February 2026; legal reviewer to confirm) A review or an event means the plan must change A new version. Revisit the assessment first if the function may have changed. Repeat the plan steps Start within 5 business days (our standard). Lodge the new version within 5 business days of finalising it if it contains a regulated restrictive practice (our standard) The step limits for a comprehensive plan add up to about 77 calendar days: the report by day 49, then the check (3 business days), the findings and the draft together (5 business days), sending (1 business day), the providers' answers (5 business days), the final check (5 business days) and finalising (1 business day). That sits inside the 84-day target with a week in hand. t: This register is the one running record of every behaviour support plan [Provider name] wr
x: This register is the one running record of every behaviour support plan [Provider name] writes. It has three sheets. On the plan sheet each row is one plan version. It shows when we were engaged and who wrote the plan. It shows what the participant agreed to and which implementing providers accepted the plan. It shows whether the plan reached the Commissioner on time and when it is next due for review. On the practice sheet each row is one regulated restrictive practice in one plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, and holds the answers FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record routes here, with every authorisation status the practice has held. On the incident review sheet each row is one review under FRM-SBS-06 Restrictive Practice Incident Review Record of an emergency or unauthorised use, keyed on the plan number in col A. "Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018. Indicators evidenced: s 40 (1) to s 40 (6). The register also holds the plan dates and records that s 39, s 41, s 42, s 43 and s 44 rely on. Those threads write to the columns marked with their indicators. Legal basis: the Behaviour Support Rules. Sections 17 and 18 say who writes. Section 19 sets time limits. Section 20 says how plans are developed and section 21 what they contain. Sections 22 to 24 cover review, form and lodgement. Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day the plan is superseded or ends (our standard). We set it to match the 7 years in section 15(3) of the Behaviour Support Rules for records of the use of a regulated restrictive practice. Other law can require longer, for example for records about a child. For a participant under 18, keep the row until they turn 25 or for 7 years, whichever is later (our standard pending state law). Check REG-INF-02 Records Retention and Disposal Register and the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed. Columns H and I are worked out and never typed over. Columns AB, AC, AD and AW are filled only when col Z lists a regulated restrictive practice, and summarise the practice sheet. Columns AN to AP are filled only when col AM is yes. Columns AR to BA are filled from the forms named in the Filled from column. The practice sheet columns RP-A to RP-R are filled from FRM-SBS-02, one row per practice per plan. The incident review sheet columns IR-A to IR-O are filled from FRM-SBS-06, one row per review; col AZ summarises them.

t: The Service Manager opens the row and keeps it. A sole Practitioner does both. Open the ro
x: The Service Manager opens the row and keeps it. A sole Practitioner does both. Open the row on the day we confirm the referral (our standard). Use one row for each plan version. A new version is a new row. Link it to the one it replaces in col D and col BD. The Practitioner gives each answer to the Service Manager within 1 business day of recording it on the form. The forms are FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record for the plan sheet, and FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record for the practice sheet. The Service Manager enters it within 2 business days of the stage (our standard). Columns that hold a list (col R, col Z, col AC, col AD, col AG, col AK, col AW and col BB, and practice sheet cols RP-P and RP-R) take a new dated line for each change. Never overwrite a line. An authorisation status is never typed over: every status the practice has held stays visible with its date. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason. Never type over a worked-out date. To change the engagement date in col F, record the reason and the name of the Clinical Lead who agreed. When systems are down, use the paper forms. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back. When a row is about the work of the Service Manager or the Practitioner who keeps it, the Chief Executive holds it. When it is about the Chief Executive, the Clinical Supervisor holds it. In a sole practitioner provider the Practitioner keeps every row, and the outside Clinical Supervisor reviews them every month under How we review. The practice sheet is the second sheet of this register: one row per regulated restrictive practice per plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, with cols RP-A to RP-R. Open a practice row when col Z first lists or proposes the practice. The incident review sheet is the third sheet: one row per FRM-SBS-06 review, keyed on col A, with cols IR-A to IR-O; open a row when a review starts and summarise it in col AZ. A small provider can keep the other list columns on a further sheet in the same way; each line carries the plan number from col A. A row is closed only when all of these are true: the plan has been replaced by a later version that is in force, or the plan has ended, or the participant has left us, and col BD says which every lodgement is done and recorded in col AO every open line in col BB is done, or has moved to REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date the Service Manager has checked the row and recorded the closing date.

t: behaviour support plan: the plan a behaviour support practitioner writes with a participan
w: Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Policy
x: behaviour support plan: the plan a behaviour support practitioner writes with a participant to meet their behaviour support needs. An interim plan covers an immediate need. A comprehensive plan follows a full assessment. behaviour support practitioner: a person the NDIS Commissioner considers suitable to do behaviour support assessments and write plans that may include restrictive practices. Clinical Lead: the senior Practitioner who owns clinical practice at [Provider name]. In a sole practitioner business, the Practitioner. Clinical Supervisor: the experienced Practitioner who supervises a Practitioner's work and checks it. In a sole practitioner business, always someone outside [Provider name], engaged in writing. trained: a worker is trained when their implementing provider has trained and observed them against the plan and confirmed it to us in writing, or when we have observed them ourselves. implementing provider: any provider, registered or not, that delivers supports to the participant where the plan applies. implementation contact: the person an implementing provider names as our contact for the plan. support network: the family, friends, carers, guardian and advocates the participant chooses. regulated restrictive practice: seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint or environmental restraint, as the Restrictive Practices Rules define them. Examples are a locked cupboard, a medicine given mainly to change behaviour, and bed rails that stop movement. authorisation: the approval a state or territory requires before a regulated restrictive practice is used, however it is described. It can be consent, a decision by a panel or tribunal, or approval by an authorised officer. instructions and guidance: what we give each person so they can carry out the plan. Examples are a strategy card for workers and a version of the plan the participant can use. state or territory note: our one page for each state or territory where we work, kept in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. It names the authorising body, who applies and what evidence is lodged. It carries its sources and the date it was last checked. authorisation summary: one page for each practice that we give an implementing provider. It says who authorises the practice, who applies, what evidence is lodged and what conditions apply. The written notice we give under PRO-SBS-02 is this summary. reporting summary: one page that lists the reporting duties of an implementing provider under the Restrictive Practices Rules and who holds each. barrier: anything that stops a plan being followed as written. say it back: asking a person to explain or show, in their own words, what they understood. given out: a plan is given out when the participant, and with consent the support network and each implementing provider, hold the finished plan. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

t: PRO-BSP-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure sets how

Start it at each of these points: A plan, interim or comprehensive, is given out (steps 1 to 15 and 18 to 20). A worker is new, absent, relief or agency (step 16). A new version of the plan is given out (step 17, then any other step the change touches). A provider raises a barrier, or a check-in is due (steps 21 to 24). The practitioner is the behaviour support practitioner who holds the plan. The practitioner does every step except steps 26 to 28. Only an NDIS behaviour support practitioner explains the plan, teaches its strategies and checks how well people carry them out. Other staff may book sessions, send papers and file records. The Service Manager copies the answers to REG-SBS-01 (step 26) and samples the records (step 28). The Clinical Supervisor reads the records (step 27).
