x: Which version is this, and why is it being made? Number the interim plan 0 and the first full plan 1. Choose the reason from Decision table 4 in PRO-ECS-08. Version number; date; choose one: interim plan; first plan; scheduled review; family asked; change for the child or family; transition; incident No Shows which version is in force and why it changed. The register keeps the current version and the reason Plan lead, Service Manager, Quality Manager REG-ECS-01 col S; REG-ECS-01 col U PRO-ECS-08 step 1 s 62 (2), s 62 (3) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Who agreed to this version for the child, and how do we know they can?
x: Who agreed to this version for the child, and how do we know they can? Check REG-ECS-01 col F and FRM-ECS-04 question 2 first. Ask to see any order or agency letter that limits who agrees. Where two people hold parental responsibility, write each person's answer. Name; authority; date confirmed; change since the last check, or "none"; any order, with where the copy is filed No Only a person with authority for the child can agree to the plan Plan lead, Service Manager REG-ECS-01 col F PRO-ECS-08 step 2 s 62 (3) Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), sections 61B and 61C, and any court order; child protection law of [state or territory]

t: Which language, mode of communication and terms does the family understand best?
x: Which language, mode of communication and terms does the family understand best? Ask before you draft. Ask about speaking and reading separately. Check REG-ECS-01 col G and FRM-RGT-01 first. Ask which words we must explain or leave out. Ask whether a cultural support person should help check the words. Languages; interpreter, yes or no; one or more of spoken, print, large print, pictures, audio, video, key word sign, translated; words to explain or leave out; who in the family should get the plan No A family can use a plan only if it comes in a language, mode and terms they understand. We ask before we draft Plan lead, Service Manager REG-ECS-01 col G; Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 3 s 62 (4) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: How does the family want to hear about progress, how often, and by when do they need a rep
x: How does the family want to hear about progress, how often, and by when do they need a report? Ask before you set the measures. A family may need a report by a date, such as an NDIS plan review. Our reports come at least every 6 months. Format, as at question 4; how often; person; date needed, or "none" No A report helps only if it comes in the form the family wants, and in time for the dates they need Plan lead Participant's file; REG-ECS-01 col AL PRO-ECS-08 step 3 s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Which assessments does this plan draw on, and how did the family take part in each?
x: Which assessments does this plan draw on, and how did the family take part in each? List FRM-ECS-03 with its date. Add any other assessment of the child by us or another provider, and any standardised tool. Say what each is for, who did it and when. Say whether the family was there, helped choose it, gave information, watched or saw the result. Write "none other" if so. One line each: assessment; what for; who did it; date; how the family took part; family agreed before it was done, yes or no, and the date No Shows the family took part in each assessment and did not only hear the result Practitioner, plan lead, Quality Manager Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 4 s 62 (3) Code of Conduct Rules, s 6(1)(a)

t: What does each result mean for the child's routines, in plain words, and when did we expla
x: What does each result mean for the child's routines, in plain words, and when did we explain it to the family? Say which outcome, measure or support the result changes. If it changes nothing, say so. Where the family sees it differently, keep both views. Never give a score without saying what it means. For FRM-ECS-03 write "see FRM-ECS-03 questions 36 and 37". One line each: assessment; what it means; date explained; form given; what the family said No A result the family cannot use does not help them decide. It must be tied back to the outcomes Practitioner, plan lead, family Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 5 s 62 (6) Our standard

t: What does the child show or tell us matters to them in the routines of their day?
x: What does the child show or tell us matters to them in the routines of their day? Start from FRM-ECS-03 question 18. Use the child's own way: words, signs, pictures, gestures, behaviour. Ask the family what each sign means. Write what the child showed, not what you think it means. One line for each routine: routine; what the child showed or told us; who saw it No The child's own view shows what is meaningful to them, in the way they communicate Plan lead, practitioner Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 7 s 62 (1) Code of Conduct Rules, s 6(1)(a)

t: Which priority or need of the family does each outcome come from?
x: Which priority or need of the family does each outcome come from? Take it from FRM-ECS-02 question 19 (priorities) or question 18 (what is hard). Give the question number and the family's own words. The family chooses which outcomes go in, and their order. One line for each outcome: outcome number; FRM-ECS-02 question 19 or 18; the family's words; order; NDIS plan goal this outcome serves, if the family wants it named No Shows that each outcome comes from what the family said, and not from what suits us Plan lead, Service Manager, Quality Manager Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 8 s 62 (1) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: What is each outcome, in the family's words?
x: What is each outcome, in the family's words? Say what the child or the family will do, so anyone could see or hear it. Start from FRM-ECS-03 question 22. Write "Joins in group time at early learning", not "improves social skills". Check each against Decision table 1 in PRO-ECS-08. One line for each outcome: outcome number; the words; who will do it, the child, the family or both No An outcome the family can see or hear can be measured, and shows whether the child's life changed Plan lead, practitioner, family Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 8, step 9 s 62 (1), s 62 (2) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: In which routine, place and with which people will each outcome happen?
x: In which routine, place and with which people will each outcome happen? Name a routine in family or community life (FRM-ECS-03 question 10). Name the place and the people who are usually there. One line for each outcome: outcome number; routine; place; people No Ties each outcome to a real routine, place and set of people Plan lead, family, educator Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 8 s 62 (5) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Why does each outcome matter to the family, and what will they notice when it happens?
x: Why does each outcome matter to the family, and what will they notice when it happens? Ask the family and write their words. This is how you check that the outcome helps the child take part in family or community life. If the family cannot say why, go back to question 9. One line for each outcome: outcome number; the family's words No Only the family can say whether an outcome matters to their family or community life Plan lead, Service Manager, Quality Manager Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 8 s 62 (5) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Which skills need to grow for each outcome, and whose skills are they?
x: Which skills need to grow for each outcome, and whose skills are they? Think about the child, parents and carers, brothers and sisters, educators and other providers. Say how it was worked out: the family's idea, what we saw, an assessment or another provider. Say when the family agreed. One line for each skill: outcome number; skill; whose; how worked out; date the family agreed No Skills named with the family show what has to grow, and in whom, so the supports target them Plan lead, practitioner Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 10 s 62 (1) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: What will be done for each outcome, by whom, in which routine and how often?
x: What will be done for each outcome, by whom, in which routine and how often? One line for each support, in plain words. Name the person who does it: a parent, carer, brother or sister, educator, practitioner (with their discipline) or other provider. Start from FRM-ECS-03 question 23. Name the strength it builds on (FRM-ECS-02 questions 15 to 17). Say how it fits the way the child and that adult learn, and the family's culture (FRM-ECS-02 questions 21 to 27). Write the strategy number from the strategy list and the family's decision on each support, as PRO-ECS-07 steps 12 and 13 set. In the interim plan (version 0), the strategy number may follow within 10 business days. One line for each support: support number; outcome number; what; who; routine; how often and how long; start date; strength used; how it fits; strategy number; evidence explained to the family, date; family's decision, one of agreed, declined, trial No The plan must describe the interventions. Each person needs to know what they will do, in which routine Plan lead, practitioner, family, educator Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 11 s 62 (2) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Where does each support happen?
x: Where does each support happen? Choose the place where the routine happens. We join by video only when the child is in that place and the routine is on. One line for each support: support number; setting, one of home, early learning or school, community, our premises, phone or video; the routine No Proves each support is planned for a place in the child's everyday life Service Manager, Quality Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col M PRO-ECS-08 step 11 s 62 (2), s 62 (5) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 5

t: Is any support away from the child's everyday places? If so, why, who agreed, who approved
x: Is any support away from the child's everyday places? If so, why, who agreed, who approved it and when do we look again? "None, all supports are in the child's everyday places" is an answer. Use Decision table 1 in PRO-ECS-04. The reason is about the child or the family, never our convenience. The look-again date is no more than 3 months away. One line for each support: support number; reason; family's agreement and date; approved by and date; look-again date. Or "none" No A support away from the child's everyday places needs a reason, agreement, approval and an end date Service Manager, Quality Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col M; REG-ECS-01 col AI PRO-ECS-08 step 11 s 62 (2), s 62 (5) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 5

t: What will the family and their network do in daily life, with or without us?
x: What will the family and their network do in daily life, with or without us? Start from FRM-ECS-02 question 20. This goes beyond therapy: play, friends, family time, a rest, belonging to a community. Text No Outcomes happen in daily life, so the plan names what the family and their network will do Plan lead, family Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 12 s 62 (2), s 62 (5) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Which other plans sit beside this plan, who wrote them, and what must every worker know to
x: Which other plans sit beside this plan, who wrote them, and what must every worker know to keep the child safe? Where the provider has adopted FRM-SUP-02, attach its sections on the critical summary, consent, risks, emergencies and who has the plan. Otherwise write here, in short lines, the critical information every worker must know (for example allergies and health conditions as the family and the health practitioner state them), what to do in an emergency and whom to call, each risk and its control, and who holds a copy of this plan. Add any mealtime, medication, behaviour support or health practitioner plan, and any plan from another provider. For any support about eating, drinking, swallowing, medicine or a health procedure, name the qualified practitioner whose plan governs. Never write the clinical detail here. One line for each plan: plan; who wrote it and their profession; date; where it is filed. Then: critical information; emergency steps and contacts; risks and controls; who holds a copy No A plan that ignores another plan can send two workers in different directions. A health strategy must come from a qualified practitioner Plan lead, Service Manager, practitioner Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 13 s 62 (2) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 1, clause 19; Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Where is the child, or the family, now for each outcome?
x: Where is the child, or the family, now for each outcome? This is the starting point. Ask the family what they see today in that routine, then add what we saw. Write the date. The starting point must be below level 3 of the five levels. If it is already at level 3, the outcome is not needed: go back to question 9. One line for each outcome: what the family sees; what we saw; date; who gave it Yes, not in the interim plan (version 0) Without a starting point no change can be measured Plan lead, family, Quality Manager REG-ECS-01 col V PRO-ECS-08 step 14 s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: What are the five levels for each outcome?
x: What are the five levels for each outcome? Write them with the family in words anyone could see or hear. Level 3 is what the family hopes to see by the next plan review. Level 1 is much less than that and level 5 is much more. Mark the level the child is at today. One line for each outcome: level 1; level 2; level 3; level 4; level 5; level today Yes, not in the interim plan (version 0) Five levels in the family's words make progress something the family can see Plan lead, family REG-ECS-01 col V PRO-ECS-08 step 14 s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Who will rate each outcome, from what, and when is the first check?
x: Who will rate each outcome, from what, and when is the first check? The family rates first. Add an educator only with the family's consent. Add what practitioners see, notes or video the family keeps, or a standardised tool. Use a tool only for a stated question, and only a practitioner qualified for it. The first check is 3 months after approval. One line for each outcome: who rates; what they use; date of the first check Yes, not in the interim plan (version 0) Names who judges progress and from what, so a rating is not left to us alone Plan lead, family, Service Manager REG-ECS-01 col V; REG-ECS-01 col AL PRO-ECS-08 step 14 s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Who took part in making this version, and how did the child take part?
x: Who took part in making this version, and how did the child take part? Start with the family. List each person, the language used and whether an interpreter took part. Say how the child took part: present, played while we talked, showed us, told us, or why not. Never ask a child, brother or sister to interpret. One line each: name; role; in person, video or phone; language; interpreter, yes or no. Then: how the child took part No Shows the family and the child took part in making this version Plan lead, Service Manager, Quality Manager REG-ECS-01 col S PRO-ECS-08 step 15 s 62 (1), s 62 (3) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: On what date did the family say this version is theirs, and how did they say it?
x: On what date did the family say this version is theirs, and how did they say it? Copy the answer at FRM-ECS-02 question 34. Do not enter a date until it says yes. Write how: spoken, signed, through an interpreter or through a person they chose. Write any part they did not agree to. That part is not carried out. Date; how; name; any part not agreed No A plan is the family's only when they say so. The date is the proof Plan lead, Service Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col S PRO-ECS-08 step 15 s 62 (3) Code of Conduct Rules, s 6(1)(a)

t: Who approved this version, and on what date?
x: Who approved this version, and on what date? The Service Manager checks it against Decision table 2 in PRO-ECS-08, then signs or returns it with the reasons. A sole trader checks their own plan against the table. Name; role; date; what was returned and fixed, or "nothing returned" Yes, not in the interim plan (version 0), which needs only the family's agreement at question 23 and the plan lead's signature Checks the plan meets our standard before anyone works to it Service Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col S PRO-ECS-08 step 16 s 62 (2) Our standard

t: How many functional outcomes does this version hold?
x: How many functional outcomes does this version hold? Count the outcomes at question 10. Number Yes, not in the interim plan (version 0) The register shows how many outcomes each child is working on Service Manager, Quality Manager REG-ECS-01 col S PRO-ECS-08 step 16 s 62 (2) Our standard

t: When and how did the family get their copy?
x: When and how did the family get their copy? Within 5 business days of approval. The copy is the page "Our plan in our words" at the end of this form, one page per outcome, with the full form available on request. Use what the family chose at question 4. A picture copy for the child is allowed. The words stay the same in every format. Date; given to; language; format, one or more of print, large print, pictures, audio, translated, read through with an interpreter; given by No Shows the family got the plan in a form they can use, and on time Service Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col T PRO-ECS-08 step 18 s 62 (4) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: What did the family say back about what the plan says, and what did we change?
x: What did the family say back about what the plan says, and what did we change? Do not ask "Do you understand?" Ask the family to tell you, in their own way, what their child will be doing, who will help and how we will know. Write their words. If they could not follow a part, change the words or the format and give it again. Text; what we changed; date given again. Or "no change needed" No Asking the family to say it back shows whether the plan was understood. Asking "Do you understand?" does not Plan lead, Quality Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col T PRO-ECS-08 step 19 s 62 (4) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Which of our workers were given this version, and when?
x: Which of our workers were given this version, and when? Every worker of ours who sees the child. Give it before their next contact with the child, and go through it with them. A signature alone is not enough. FRM-SUP-02 question 60 asks the same: answer it once, here. One line each: name; role; date given; how they showed they understood it No A worker can follow only a plan they have been given Plan lead, Service Manager Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 20 s 62 (2) Our standard

t: When was this progress check, and who took part?
x: When was this progress check, and who took part? At least every 3 months from approval. Name the family members, and anyone else the family agreed to. Dated entries: date; names and roles; language; interpreter, yes or no; how the child took part Yes, until the first check is due Shows each check happened, who took part and when. The register keeps the latest date Plan lead, Service Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col V PRO-ECS-08 step 22 s 62 (3), s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Where is each outcome now on its five levels, and what does the family see?
x: Where is each outcome now on its five levels, and what does the family see? Ask the family first: "What are you seeing now?" Then agree the level. Put the family's rating of the routine now beside the last one, on the 1 to 5 scale at FRM-ECS-03 question 17. Add what we saw. Choose the progress word this way. Achieved: level 3 or higher. Progressing: a higher level than the last check, but below level 3. No change: the same level as the last check. Gone back: a lower level. At the first check, compare with the starting point. One line for each outcome: level now; progress, one of achieved, progressing, no change, gone back; the family's words; family's rating now and last time; what we saw Yes, until the first check is due Gives the progress of each outcome in the family's terms. The progress word goes to the register Plan lead, family, Quality Manager REG-ECS-01 col V PRO-ECS-08 step 22 s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: Is each support happening as planned?
x: Is each support happening as planned? One line for each support at question 14. Read the latest FRM-ECS-05 entries and REG-ECS-01 col W. If a support is not happening, say why before you judge the outcome. One line for each support: support number; as planned, partly or no; why; the end confidence rating of the person who does this support at their latest FRM-ECS-05 session; the family's view Yes, until the first check is due A support that is not happening cannot explain a result. This checks whether the intervention was carried out Plan lead, Service Manager Participant's file PRO-ECS-08 step 22 s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: What do the results mean, and what did we agree to do?
x: What do the results mean, and what did we agree to do? Ask what is helping and what is getting in the way. Use Decision table 3 in PRO-ECS-08. Any change is made within 10 business days of the check. One line for each outcome: what we found; what we agreed, one of keep going, change a support, change the levels or the measure, change the outcome, outcome achieved and a new one chosen, stop; owner; due date; the family's words Yes, until the first check is due Measuring means little unless it changes what we do Plan lead, Service Manager, Quality Manager Participant's file; REG-ECS-01 col AK PRO-ECS-08 step 23 s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: When and how did we give the family a progress report?
x: When and how did we give the family a progress report? At each plan review, at least every 6 months, and within 10 business days of a request. Use the format at question 5 and the "Our plan in our words" page as the frame: one block per outcome. For each outcome say where the child started, where they are now, what helped, what got in the way and what happens next. Explain any assessment result in plain words. A score is never the whole report. Write it so the family can give it to the NDIA if they choose. When supports end, this is the final report. Date; format; language; given by; given to; final report, yes or no Yes, until the first report is due Shows the family was told how their child is going, when and in what form Service Manager, Quality Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col V PRO-ECS-08 step 25 s 62 (6) Code of Conduct Rules, s 6(1)(d)

t: What did the family say about the report, and what did we change?
x: What did the family say about the report, and what did we change? Ask: "What does this tell you about your child? What is missing?" Write their words. If they could not follow it, change it and give it again. Tell the family what changed. Dated entries: date; what the family said; what we changed; date told Yes, until the first report is due What the family says shows whether the report was understood and was meaningful to them Plan lead, Quality Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col V; REG-ECS-01 col X PRO-ECS-08 step 26 s 62 (6) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: When was this review, why was it held, who took part and what changed?
x: When was this review, why was it held, who took part and what changed? Choose the reason as at question 2. For each outcome and support say what is kept, changed, new, done or stopped. Confirm who agrees for the child (question 3) and the language and terms (question 4). Review FRM-ECS-02 and FRM-ECS-03 in the same meeting. Date; reason; names and roles; one line for each outcome and support: what changed Yes, until the first review is due Shows the family took part in the review and what changed because of it Plan lead, Service Manager, auditor REG-ECS-01 col U PRO-ECS-08 step 27 s 62 (3) Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 5, clause 9

t: When is the next review due?
x: When is the next review due? No later than 6 months after approval, or after this review. Earlier if the family asks or a change is coming. Date No Keeps every review inside 6 months Plan lead, Service Manager, Quality Manager REG-ECS-01 col U PRO-ECS-08 step 15, step 27 s 62 (3) Our standard

t: Part Who signs What they confirm Date and time Sections A, C, D, E, F and G, except questi
x: Part Who signs What they confirm Date and time Sections A, C, D, E, F and G, except questions 24 and 25 The plan lead: name, role, signature The plan was made with the family, and the words are theirs Date and time Section B The practitioner who assessed: name, role The family took part as recorded, and the results were explained Date Questions 22 and 23 A person named at question 3: name "This plan is mine. I know I can ask to change it." The person may agree by voice, by sign or through an interpreter. The plan lead records which Date Questions 24 and 25 (not for the interim plan, version 0) The Service Manager: name, role, signature The plan passes every row in Decision table 2 in PRO-ECS-08 Date and time Sections H and I The plan lead: name, role Each check and report was held with the family and is true Date of each entry Section J The plan lead and the person who agrees for the child "This review is what was said and agreed." Date of the review A sole trader signs the plan lead line and the Service Manager line. The independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register reads a sample of 3 plans every 6 months.

t: Service Manager: approve the plan, or return it with the reasons, within 5 business days o
x: Service Manager: approve the plan, or return it with the reasons, within 5 business days of the family agreeing (step 16, our standard). The interim plan (version 0) needs no approval. Plan lead: enter the approved plan in REG-ECS-01 within 2 business days of approval (step 17, our standard). Plan lead: give the family their copy within 5 business days of approval. Ask them to say it back (steps 18 and 19, our standard). Plan lead: give the plan to each of our workers who sees the child before their next contact (step 20, our standard). Plan lead: hold a progress check at least every 3 months. Enter it in REG-ECS-01 within 2 business days (steps 22 and 24, our standard). Plan lead: give the family a progress report at each plan review, and at least every 6 months (step 25, our standard). A person with parental responsibility can ask for a copy of any record about their child. We give it within 10 business days (our standard). The plan is filed in the child's file. Keep it for 7 years after supports end (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026), or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard). Check the law of [state or territory] before a child's record is destroyed. Some laws set a longer time.

c: FRM-ECS-07 Our plan in our words (the family's copy)
t: This page is for you, the family. We fill one page for each outcome, in your words, in the
x: This page is for you, the family. We fill one page for each outcome, in your words, in the language and format you chose at question 4. It is the copy of your plan that you keep (question 26) and the frame for your progress report (question 33). A picture version for your child is welcome. You can ask for the full plan at any time. Our child: [the name the family uses]. Plan version: [0 for the interim plan, then 1, 2, 3]. Date: [date]. What will change: [the outcome in our words, from question 10]. Where, when and with whom: [the routine, the place and the people, from question 11]. Why it matters to us: [from question 12]. Who does what: [each support, who does it and how often, in plain words, from question 14]. Where we are now: [the starting point in our words, from question 19]. What we hope to see by the next review: [level 3, from question 20; not in the interim plan]. How we will check, and when: [who rates it and the date of the next check, from question 21]. How it is going: [at each check, the progress word and our words, from question 30; this block is the progress report]. Who to call: [our plan lead and backup, and how to reach them]. We can ask to change this plan at any time. Saying no to any part never reduces our child's supports.

t: Control
Specialised support coordination
x: Each participant receiving specialised support coordination receives tailored support to implement, monitor and review their support plans and reduce the risk and complexity of their situation.

t: Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of the risk factors experienced by each participa
x: Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of the risk factors experienced by each participant with high-risk and/or complex needs.

t: Participants are involved in the evaluation of their situation and the identification of t
x: Participants are involved in the evaluation of their situation and the identification of the supports required to prevent or respond to a crisis, incident or breakdown of support arrangements, and the promotion of safety for the participant and others.

t: Consultation is undertaken with the participant and, with the participant’s consent, the p
x: Consultation is undertaken with the participant and, with the participant’s consent, the participant’s support network and mainstream services (as appropriate) in planning and coordinating supports to implement the participant’s plan, and any plan review.

t: In consideration of each participant’s individual needs, preferences and circumstances, su
x: In consideration of each participant’s individual needs, preferences and circumstances, suitable NDIS providers and mainstream service providers that have the appropriate skills and experience to deliver the required support are identified.

t: There is proactive engagement to ensure that all providers implementing the participant’s
x: There is proactive engagement to ensure that all providers implementing the participant’s plan understand and respond to the risk and/or complexity of the participant’s situation, and collaborate with other relevant providers, where required.

t: All monitoring and reporting obligations associated with the participant’s plan are manage
x: All monitoring and reporting obligations associated with the participant’s plan are managed effectively.

t: Specialised Support Coordination Policy
This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to when we provide specialised support c
x: This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to when we provide specialised support coordination. It is for participants whose situation carries high risk or complexity, their families and advocates, our coordinators, and the people who check our work.

t: Every participant who receives specialised support coordination from [Provider name], and
x: Every participant who receives specialised support coordination from [Provider name], and every person who asks us for it, before they sign (the Registration Rules, Schedule 6, clause 1(2)(a)). Everyone who works for us on that support: employees, contractors, agency workers, volunteers and key personnel. The whole of the coordination: assessing risk and complexity, planning for a crisis, finding and briefing providers, monitoring, and reporting. Any other support we or anyone connected with us provide to the same participant. Commitment 13 keeps it separate from the coordination. Short names used here: "The Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018. "The Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018. "The Code" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018, section 6.

t: Commitments
We will allocate each participant a coordinator who is qualified, trained and signed off a
x: We will allocate each participant a coordinator who is qualified, trained and signed off as competent for that participant's risks and complexity. A coordinator holds [qualification and years of experience we require]. The NDIA expects specialised support coordination to be delivered by a qualified and experienced practitioner, such as a social worker, psychologist, occupational therapist or mental health nurse, or a person with equivalent demonstrated experience in complex situations; set the requirement at adoption with that in mind. They have completed our training on the risk factors listed in FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan. They have supervision with the Service Manager at least every month.

t: We will assess each participant's risks and complexity with them. We use their own account
x: We will assess each participant's risks and complexity with them. We use their own account and the risk factors and rating scale in FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan. At the first meeting we agree interim safety steps and set a provisional risk level. We make the plan within the time for that level in PRO-SCO-02 Decision table 2, counted from the first meeting: 5 business days for extreme risk, 10 for high, 15 for medium and low. A second person, the case reviewer, reads and challenges the assessment and plan: before the plan is issued for a participant at high or extreme risk, and within 10 business days of issue for every other participant.

t: We will make a Risk and Crisis Response Plan with each participant, in their words and in
x: We will make a Risk and Crisis Response Plan with each participant, in their words and in a form they can use. We review the plan at the interval for their risk level, and after any crisis, incident or major change.

t: We will always have someone who has read the participant's plan and can respond to a crisi
x: We will always have someone who has read the participant's plan and can respond to a crisis. That is the coordinator, or the cover coordinator when the coordinator is away. In our hours a coordinator or cover who has read the plan answers a crisis call and starts the plan within 2 hours. Outside our hours the participant's plan names who they call, and we say truthfully whether that is us.

t: We will consult the participant when we plan and coordinate supports, and before each plan
x: We will consult the participant when we plan and coordinate supports, and before each plan review. With their consent, we also consult their support network and mainstream services. We record who the participant agreed we may talk to and what we may tell them. We respect a refusal.

t: We will identify suitable providers for each support. We check registration where it appli
x: We will identify suitable providers for each support. We check registration where it applies, evidence of skills and experience for the participant's kind of situation, and fit with their preferences. We follow one options rule, set in POL-SCO-02 C4: at least three suitable options able to meet the need, of which at least two have no relationship to us, where that many exist, and we say which have a relationship to us. Where fewer exist we record who we asked and tell the participant why.

t: We will make sure every provider who carries out the plan understands the participant's ri
x: We will make sure every provider who carries out the plan understands the participant's risks and their own part before their first support. We brief each provider on the parts of the plan the participant agreed to share. We get their confirmation in writing.

x: We will bring the participant's providers and other services together to work as one team. We hold a coordination meeting at the interval for the participant's risk level. t: We will monitor each participant's plan. We contact the participant at the interval for th
x: We will monitor each participant's plan. We contact the participant at the interval for their risk level and check that each support is delivered as planned. When a support is not delivered as planned we act within 5 business days.

t: We will check each participant's plan budget and plan dates every month, in the first 5 bu
x: We will check each participant's plan budget and plan dates every month, in the first 5 business days of the month. t: We will meet every reporting obligation attached to the participant's plan. We list each r

t: We will arrange supports as the participant directs, using their plan funds for the purpos

t: We will keep specialised support coordination separate from any other support we, or anyon
x: We will keep specialised support coordination separate from any other support we, or anyone connected with us, provide. x: We will not leave a participant without a plan when coordination ends or changes. Before our last day we hand the Risk and Crisis Response Plan to the next coordinator, with the participant's consent. We also give the participant their copy.

t: specialised support coordination: help for a participant whose situation carries high risk
x: specialised support coordination: help for a participant whose situation carries high risk or complexity. It means putting their NDIS plan into action, monitoring it and reviewing it, and reducing the risk and complexity of their situation. participant: a person with disability who receives specialised support coordination from us, or who is asking us for it. NDIS plan: the plan the NDIA approves for the participant, with its funding and dates. NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency, which runs the NDIS and approves NDIS plans. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency". coordinator: the worker who does the coordination with a participant. cover coordinator: a second coordinator, with the same sign-off, who acts when the coordinator is away. For a sole trader this may be a coordinator from another provider, engaged in writing. case reviewer: a person who reads the assessment and plan for each participant, and challenges them. They are not the coordinator for that participant. For a sole trader the case reviewer is a person outside the business. Risk and Crisis Response Plan: the plan we make with the participant in FRM-SCO-01. It holds their risks, warning signs, what helps and the steps to take in a crisis. risk and complexity: the things in a participant's life that could seriously harm them or others. It also means anything that makes their supports hard to arrange or keep steady. crisis: a point where someone is at risk of serious harm, or where supports the participant depends on have broken down or are about to. breakdown of supports: a support the participant relies on stops, or is not delivered as planned, and the participant is at risk or worse off. critical support: a support that would put the participant at risk if it stopped, named in FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan. provider: an NDIS provider, registered or not, who gives a support in the participant's NDIS plan. mainstream service: a service for the whole community, such as health, housing, justice, child safety, mental health, education or transport. support network: the people in the participant's life whom they choose to involve, such as family, friends, carers and advocates. independent advocate: a person outside [Provider name] who speaks up for the participant's wishes and rights. decision maker: a person with legal authority to make decisions for a participant, such as a guardian, administrator or nominee. interest: ownership of a provider, a shared owner or director, a family tie, a referral arrangement, or any payment, gift or benefit from a provider. independent contact for concerns: in a provider with one owner, the outside person who receives concerns about the owner. REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register names them. This may be the case reviewer. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

t: Control
Specialised Support Coordination Procedure
The result: every participant who receives specialised support coordination has their risk
x: The result: every participant who receives specialised support coordination has their risks understood, and a crisis plan they helped make. Their providers understand and act on that plan. The plan is monitored and reported on until it ends. This procedure gives effect to POL-SCO-01 Specialised Support Coordination Policy, C1 to C14. Short names used here: "The Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018. "The Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018. "The Code" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018, section 6. "The NDIA" means the National Disability Insurance Agency. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency".

t: Start this procedure when: a participant, or their decision maker, agrees to start special
x: Start this procedure when: a participant, or their decision maker, agrees to start specialised support coordination (steps 1 to 19) you learn of a crisis, an incident or a breakdown of supports (steps 25 to 28) a contact, a meeting, a budget check or a report falls due (steps 20 to 24) a review date arrives, or a trigger in Decision table 4 happens (step 29) coordination is about to end, or the coordinator is about to change for good (step 30). A crisis is a point where someone is at risk of serious harm. It is also a point where supports the participant depends on have broken down or are about to. Who acts: The coordinator does the work with the participant. Each participant has one named coordinator. The cover coordinator acts when the coordinator is away. They read each plan within 2 business days of issue, the same day for a participant at extreme risk. The Service Manager names the coordinator and the cover coordinator, takes same-day calls, reads the register every month and approves each closing. The case reviewer reads the assessment and plan for each participant and challenges them: before the plan is issued for a participant at high or extreme risk, and within 10 business days of issue otherwise. The Service Manager is the case reviewer, unless they are also the coordinator for that participant. Then an outside person is the case reviewer. The Quality Manager checks that the register is kept and acts on trends. The Chief Executive takes concerns about managers. Whoever takes a crisis call may be any of these people. Outside our hours it is whoever Q27 of the participant's plan names. That can be a crisis service and not us. In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register shows who holds each. If you are a sole trader, or the one director of a company: You hold every role except the case reviewer. The case reviewer is a person outside the business, engaged in writing with a confidentiality undertaking and agreed response times (a draft plan read within 2 business days of receiving it). They also give you supervision at least every month and do the register reads that REG-SCO-01 sets for the case reviewer. The independent contact for concerns, named in REG-GOV-01, takes concerns about you; this may be the same person as the case reviewer. Your cover coordinator may be a coordinator from another provider, engaged in writing. They read each plan within 2 business days of issue, the same day for a participant at extreme risk. You name the case reviewer and the cover before your first participant, and tell each participant who they are and what they may be told. Where a step says to tell the Service Manager, write the date and time. For a participant at high or extreme risk, also tell the case reviewer the same day. A concern about you goes to the independent contact for concerns.

t: The participant, or their decision maker, has agreed to start. You have AGR-SUP-01 Service
x: The participant, or their decision maker, has agreed to start. You have AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template signed, or an interim written agreement, and the participant's NDIS plan. The plan includes specialised support coordination funding. You have the participant's communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form), or a blank copy. You have a blank FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan and can open REG-SCO-01 Support Coordination Register. You have completed training on the risk factors at FRM-SCO-01 Q11 and on this procedure. REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register shows you are signed off as competent for specialised support coordination. You know who your cover coordinator and case reviewer are. You have the numbers for 000, for the crisis service for [state or territory], and for the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. The Commission line is not an emergency line. Before first use, the Chief Executive fills every square bracket in the four coordination documents, except [Provider name]. The Quality Manager checks that none is left blank. These are the decisions: the qualification and years of experience a coordinator needs (POL-SCO-01 C1) our hours, and what we tell a participant about outside them (FRM-SCO-01 Q27) the crisis service for [state or territory] (FRM-SCO-01 Q26) the child protection reporting rule for [state or territory] (FRM-SCO-01 Q31) for a sole trader, the case reviewer, the cover coordinator and the independent contact for concerns the name of the system that holds REG-SCO-01, and where paper copies are kept who takes a privacy complaint (FRM-SCO-01 Privacy). Before adoption, walk these scenarios through with two coordinators and the case reviewer, or, for a sole trader, with the case reviewer and the cover coordinator. Record it under "Reviewed with": a participant who is evicted tomorrow and has nobody to call a night call from a participant who says they want to die a provider who withdraws on a Friday afternoon a family member who asks for the plan after the participant said no a plan that ends in 3 weeks with no review date.

t: Call 000 first. Call before anything else when a person is in danger now. A delay in a cri
x: Call 000 first. Call before anything else when a person is in danger now. A delay in a crisis can cost a life. A crisis plan nobody has read does not work. A cover coordinator or provider who has not read it cannot act at 2 am, and may make things worse. You are not a clinician. Health or behaviour advice you are not trained to give can harm the participant. Ask their practitioner and write what they say. A plan we write never holds a restrictive practice. Holding, locking in, withholding things or a medicine to calm, written into a plan, can harm the participant and break the law. Only an authorised behaviour support plan can hold one. Never share beyond what the participant agreed. A plan shared with the wrong person can put the participant in danger, most of all where the concern is someone close to them. Do not promise secrecy. You may have to act to keep someone safe. A promise you cannot keep breaks trust. Payment or a gift for naming a provider breaks the Code. It puts our advice in doubt and can lead to action by the NDIS Commission (the Code, section 6(1)(d)). A plan whose reassessment date passes with no review scheduled leaves the participant unsure of their funding. The plan stays in effect until the NDIA makes a new one, but a late review can leave a gap between what the plan funds and what the participant now needs. Check the dates every month and ask the NDIA 12 weeks out. A missed report date can weaken the participant's plan review. The NDIA may decide without our evidence. The concern may be about a colleague or a manager. A report that goes only to the person it is about can be buried. "If it goes wrong" gives another line. A participant's refusal is a decision. Record it, respect it and ask again at the next review. Do not end coordination because of it.

FRM-SCO-01 Q2 to Q4 At the first meeting (our standard)

t: Ask the three safety questions and agree interim steps.
x: Ask the three safety questions and agree interim steps. A danger found at the first meeting cannot wait until the plan is written. The coordinator Ask: is anyone in danger right now? What could stop or go wrong in the next 4 weeks? Who should we call first if something does? Write each answer in the participant's words. Agree what you and they will do if it happens before the plan is finished. If anyone is in danger now, go to step 25 first. From the answers, set a provisional risk level with Decision table 1 and write it at Q15 as provisional; the plan clock in Decision table 2 starts today. Give the participant your number, our hours and who to call outside them. The participant is safe enough to wait for the plan, and knows who to call. FRM-SCO-01 Q7 to Q9 and Q15 (provisional); REG-SCO-01 col K and col Q At the first meeting. The same day for any danger (our standard)

t: Record who we may talk to and share the plan with.
x: Record who we may talk to and share the plan with. The coordinator Ask who we may talk to, which parts they may be told and until when. Think of family, carers, current providers, health practitioners, housing, justice, child safety and the NDIA. Ask on their own who must not be told. Record a refusal and do not argue. Complete FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form for each person. Say what we cannot keep private. That is a call to 000, a duty the law gives us, and a serious threat to someone's life, health or safety. Everyone we talk to has been agreed by the participant, for the parts agreed. FRM-SCO-01 Q5 and Q6; REG-SCO-01 col N Before we contact anyone about the participant (our standard)

t: List every report and notice we owe.
x: List every report and notice we owe. The coordinator Read the NDIS plan, the service agreement, the request for service and any written request from the NDIA, the plan manager or another funder. For each report write what is owed, to whom, the due date and where the duty comes from. The NDIA's reports are: the implementation report, due 8 weeks after coordination starts; mid-term reports at the frequency the request for service sets; and the plan reassessment report before the plan review, which we draft with the participant 8 weeks before the reassessment date and send 6 weeks before it, or by the date the NDIA sets (steps 23 and 24). Take due dates from the request for service and the provider portal. Add any date the participant tells you matters, such as a tribunal or a housing review. Update the list whenever the plan changes. Every duty has a due date and a source before supports start. REG-SCO-01 col AG Within 10 business days of opening the row (our standard)

t: Learn the participant's situation, their words first.
x: Learn the participant's situation, their words first. The coordinator Ask the participant what is hardest now and what they want to change. Write what they say. Then, with their consent from step 5, read the NDIS plan, earlier assessments and reports, and the incident and crisis history. List the supports in place now. Talk only to the people they agreed. Write each conversation in col W. Link to another provider's clinical content. Do not copy it into our plan. The participant's account comes first, and the facts support it. FRM-SCO-01 Q10 and Q21; REG-SCO-01 col W Within 5 business days of the first meeting, and inside the plan deadline in Decision table 2 (our standard)

t: Assess the participant's risks and complexity with them.
x: Assess the participant's risks and complexity with them. A risk rated without the participant, or without the facts, can miss the thing most likely to cause harm. The coordinator Go through each factor in the hint at Q11. For each that applies, write what has happened, what the participant thinks, and a rating on the scale printed at Q12: low, medium, high or extreme. Ask what they want done and which risks they accept. Explain the risk and the options first. For a risk rated high or extreme that they accept, complete FRM-RGT-04 Dignity of Risk Decision Record. Ask who else could be harmed. Set the overall level with Decision table 1. A final level higher than the provisional one set at step 4 shortens the remaining time in Decision table 2; a lower one never lengthens it. Tell the Service Manager the same day if the level is high or extreme, and re-check the caseload (step 1). Each risk is named, rated and discussed, and the participant has an overall level. FRM-SCO-01 Q11 to Q15; REG-SCO-01 col O to col Q Inside the plan deadline in Decision table 2 (our standard)

t: Write the warning signs and what helps, in the participant's words.
x: Write the warning signs and what helps, in the participant's words. The coordinator Ask what they notice in themselves when things start to go wrong. Ask what family, workers and other providers notice, and write who said it. Ask what makes things worse, what helps and what must not be done. Ask for the first sign, not the last. Never write a restraint, a lock, a withheld item or a medicine to calm. Only an authorised behaviour support plan can hold one, and PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies if someone asks for it. Section C holds the signs and the responses the participant chose. FRM-SCO-01 Q16 to Q20 Inside the plan deadline in Decision table 2 (our standard)

t: Agree what keeps things steady and what happens in a crisis.
x: Agree what keeps things steady and what happens in a crisis. The coordinator In Section D, list the supports and people who keep things steady. Mark each support that would put the participant at risk if it stopped, and how long it can be missed. Agree actions that stop a crisis, each with an owner and a date. In Section E, say what counts as a crisis, the first steps for each kind, and the call list in order. State our hours truthfully. Say where the health information is kept, where the participant will go if home is not safe, and what they want in an emergency. Do not write a dose or a clinical step. Link to the practitioner's plan. Check the plan does not conflict with any behaviour support plan, health plan or court order the participant has. A coordinator, a cover coordinator or a provider can act from this plan at 2 am. FRM-SCO-01 Q21 to Q31; REG-SCO-01 col P; REG-SCO-01 col R; REG-SCO-01 col V Inside the plan deadline in Decision table 2 (our standard)

t: Read the assessment and the draft plan, and challenge them.
x: Read the assessment and the draft plan, and challenge them. The case reviewer Check the plan against the participant's own words. Check each factor has a rating and an action. Check the crisis steps work at 2 am, and each call-list number is complete. Check nothing restrictive is written in, and nothing conflicts with a behaviour support plan or health plan. Check the sharing list matches what the participant agreed. Write the changes you ask for. The coordinator makes them. Sign when they are settled. A second person has tested the plan before it is used. FRM-SCO-01 Q41; REG-SCO-01 col U Before the plan is issued for a participant at high or extreme risk, within 2 business days of receiving the draft. Within 10 business days of issue for medium or low (our standard)

t: Go through the finished plan with the participant and give them a copy.
x: Go through the finished plan with the participant and give them a copy. The coordinator Go through each section in the format they chose at Q2. Ask whether it says what they want. Change what they ask. If they disagree, write what with, tell them how to complain under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure, and do not record agreement. Set the contact interval and the next review date. Give their copy that day. Copies for the participant and for providers omit Section F and Q5, Q6 and Q12, and you initial each copy issued. The cover coordinator reads the plan within 2 business days of issue, the same day for a participant at extreme risk. For a participant at high or extreme risk, give the Service Manager a copy of Section E that day, and again at each new version. The participant has a plan that is theirs, in a form they can use, and our cover can act on it. FRM-SCO-01 Q37 to Q40 and Q42; REG-SCO-01 col S; REG-SCO-01 col T Within 1 business day of the case reviewer's sign-off (our standard)

t: Consult the participant's support network and mainstream services.
x: Consult the participant's support network and mainstream services. The coordinator Ask the participant first, and tell them what each person said. With the consent from step 5, ask each person and agency what they see and what they can do. Ask what is needed to put the NDIS plan into action. Include health, housing, justice, child safety, income support, transport, mental health and education services that already work with the participant. Write who, when, why and what was agreed. The plan is built with the people who know the participant and the services already in their life. REG-SCO-01 col W Before supports are arranged at step 17, and again in the 12 weeks before each NDIA plan review (our standard)

t: Check whether we hold an interest in any provider before naming it.
x: Check whether we hold an interest in any provider before naming it. The coordinator An interest is ownership, a shared owner or director, a family tie, a referral arrangement, or any payment, gift or benefit from a provider. If we hold one, stop. Follow PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure before naming that provider. It uses FRM-SCO-03 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Disclosure Record. Take nothing from a provider for naming or referring a participant. Tell the Service Manager the same day if anything is offered. Every provider we name is named on merit, and any interest is declared to the participant. REG-SCO-01 col X Before naming any provider to the participant (our standard)

t: Find suitable providers and check each one.
x: Find suitable providers and check each one. The coordinator Use Decision table 3. For each support the plan needs, follow the options rule in POL-SCO-02 C4: find at least three suitable options where that many exist, at least two of them with no relationship to us, and say which have one. Check registration on the NDIS Provider Register. Ask for evidence of skills and experience with people in a similar situation, such as examples, team qualifications and referees the participant agrees to. Check availability, place, cost and fit with the participant's language, culture and preferences. Ask who they already know and trust. Write what you asked and what you got. Do not recommend a provider you could not check. Every option put to the participant is checked, and the checks are on record. FRM-SCO-01 Q32 and Q33; REG-SCO-01 col X Within 10 business days of identifying the support. For a critical support, the urgent path in PRO-SCO-03 applies: steps 15 to 17 within 3 business days (our standard)

t: Record who you asked and what they said.
x: Record who you asked and what they said. fewer than three suitable providers exist for a support The coordinator List each provider you contacted, the date and the answer. Say why the others were not suitable. Tell the participant there are fewer choices, and why. Ask whether they want to wait or go ahead. If the only option is one of ours, follow PRO-SCO-01 and tell the Service Manager the same day. The participant knows why choice is limited, and the search is on record. FRM-SCO-01 Q34; REG-SCO-01 col Y With the step 15 checks, within 10 business days of identifying the support (our standard)

t: Put the options to the participant and record their choice.
x: Put the options to the participant and record their choice. The coordinator Follow PRO-SCO-03 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure. It sets how to explain the options in the participant's way. It also sets how to record their choice and their direction on using their funds, on FRM-SCO-02 Support Options and Choice Record. It also sets how we build their skills to manage their own supports. The participant chooses, not you. FRM-SCO-02 is the one record of the options and the choice. Enter it as a row in REG-SCO-01 sheet 2, and write the support, the record number and the record date in col Z. The participant has chosen each provider, and has directed how their funds are used. REG-SCO-01 col Z At the pace PRO-SCO-03 sets, counted from step 15 or step 16. For a critical support, its urgent path applies: within 3 business days (our standard)

t: Brief each provider who carries out the plan on the parts that apply to them.
x: Brief each provider who carries out the plan on the parts that apply to them. The coordinator This includes providers already in place, not only new ones. Share only the parts the participant agreed at Q5, and only what the provider needs. That means the risk factors that affect their support (Q11 and Q14) and the warning signs. It means what helps and what must not be done. It means their part in prevention and in a crisis, and who to call. Check they are not a person named at Q6. Brief by phone, video or in person. Email alone is not a briefing. Say the risks in plain words. Do not pass on the participant's whole history. Each provider knows the participant's risks and their own part before supports begin. FRM-SCO-01 Q35; REG-SCO-01 col AA Before the provider's first support. If supports have already started, within 5 business days of the plan being issued (our standard)

t: Get each provider's confirmation that they understand.
x: Get each provider's confirmation that they understand. The coordinator Ask each provider to say in their own words what they will watch for and do. Get their confirmation in writing. An email is enough. Get the name and number of their contact in a crisis. Ask them to tell you within 1 business day of an incident, a missed or changed support, or a worker change that affects the participant. If a provider has not confirmed after 5 business days, ask again. After 10 business days, the Service Manager phones their manager. Each provider has confirmed, and we have a crisis contact for each. FRM-SCO-01 Q36; REG-SCO-01 col AA Within 5 business days of the briefing (our standard)

t: Hold a coordination meeting with the participant and their providers.
x: Hold a coordination meeting with the participant and their providers. The coordinator Ask the participant who they want at the meeting and how it should run. With their consent, invite their providers and any mainstream service involved. Cover how supports are going and any crisis or near miss since the last meeting. Cover the warning signs seen, what is not working and who does what next. Write each action with an owner and a date. Send the actions to everyone who attended within 2 business days. If a provider misses two meetings in a row, tell the Service Manager. The providers work as one team, and every action has an owner and a date. REG-SCO-01 col AB First meeting within 20 business days of the first support starting. Then at the interval in Decision table 2, and within 5 business days of any crisis, incident or breakdown (our standard)

t: Check in with the participant, and ask how each support is going.
x: Check in with the participant, and ask how each support is going. The coordinator, or the cover coordinator when the coordinator is away Contact them at the interval in Decision table 2, in the way they chose at Q37. Ask how they are, how each support is going, what has changed and what worries them. Ask whether the supports are helping them towards the goals in their NDIS plan. Check each critical support first. Ask the provider when the participant reports a problem or a support was missed. When a support is not delivered as planned, act within 5 business days. Talk to the provider, adjust the support, or go to step 26 if it is a breakdown. If you cannot reach a participant at high or extreme risk, follow "If it goes wrong". Where Q14 names a risk to workers, tell the Service Manager when and where you visit, and check in with them after. We know how supports are going, and the participant has been heard. REG-SCO-01 col AC; REG-SCO-01 col AD At the interval in Decision table 2 (our standard)

t: Run the monthly plan check on the budget and the dates.
x: Run the monthly plan check on the budget and the dates. The coordinator Run the one monthly funds check, on a new copy of FRM-SCO-02 Section H. For each funding category, compare the share used and booked with the share of the plan time that has passed. If the two differ by more than 15 percentage points (our standard), find out why. Tell the participant within 5 business days, and the plan manager if there is one. Check the coordination funding and hours. Check the provider portal for the due dates of the NDIA's reports. If the plan is within 12 weeks of its reassessment date and no review has been scheduled, ask the NDIA in writing to confirm the date. Do this with the participant's agreement. If you cannot see the budget, ask the participant, the plan manager or the NDIA, with the participant's consent. Update the dates in col F to col J, and the next report date in col AI. PRO-SCO-03 steps 26 and 27 set what the participant may choose to do about a gap. No budget surprise and no missed date. FRM-SCO-02 Q32 to Q35; REG-SCO-01 col AF (date and flags); REG-SCO-01 col AI In the first 5 business days of each month (our standard)

t: Prepare the plan review report with the participant.
x: Prepare the plan review report with the participant. The coordinator Start 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date (the plan end date where none is set). For a plan shorter than 12 weeks, start at its first meeting. This is the one plan review preparation for the participant; PRO-SCO-03 step 30 points here. Ask the participant what has worked, what has not and what they want next. Use the consultations, delivery checks, funds checks and events in the register. Say what changed in their risks, which supports worked and what is needed next, and why. Say plainly if different funding is needed and what happens without it. Show the participant the whole draft, in their format, with a plain summary of how their funds were used. They may add their own words or ask us to leave something out. Record what they asked. For a participant at high or extreme risk, the case reviewer reads it. A report that says what the participant wants, backed by our records. REG-SCO-01 col AH Draft and plain summary to the participant at least 8 weeks before the plan reassessment date, and never later than the date the NDIA sets (our standard)

t: Send each report by its due date.
x: Send each report by its due date. The coordinator Send each report listed in col AG, using the channel the NDIA or funder names. Send the plan review report only with the participant's agreement. Check it was received. Keep a copy. Send a participant's information to a funder only as far as the participant agreed, or the law requires. If a due date will be missed, tell the recipient before it passes, give a new date, and tell the Service Manager the same day. Every report is received on time, and the participant has seen it. REG-SCO-01 col AH By the due date the NDIA or funder sets. Where none is set, 6 weeks before the plan reassessment date for the plan reassessment report, and 8 weeks after coordination starts for the implementation report (our standard)

t: Call 000.
x: Call 000. someone is in danger now Whoever takes the call or sees the danger Call when a person is hurt, unconscious or not breathing, or has taken too much of something. Call when they say they are about to end their life or harm someone. If you are not sure, call 000. Say what has happened and where the person is. Stay on the line and follow the operator. Tell the crew what the plan says at Q28: the participant's conditions, allergies, that they take medicines and where the list is held, and how they communicate. Do not read out doses. If you are with the participant, stay with them. If you are not, stay on the phone with them until help arrives if you can, and ask someone nearby to stay. If they speak of wanting to die but are not about to act, stay with them, call the crisis service at Q26 and follow the plan. Then go to step 26. Emergency help is coming and the participant is not alone. REG-SCO-01 col AE Straight away (our standard)

t: Follow the participant's plan for this kind of crisis.
x: Follow the participant's plan for this kind of crisis. The coordinator, the cover coordinator, or the person at the top of the call list Open the plan. Find the kind of crisis at Q25 and do the first steps. Phone the people at Q26, in order, until someone takes responsibility. Share only what the participant agreed. The exceptions are a call to 000, a duty in law, and a serious threat to life, health or safety when you cannot ask first. If a provider has not arrived or has withdrawn, phone them. Then phone the next choice at Q32 and tell the participant. Stay in contact until the crisis is settled or someone they trust has taken over. Write the times as you go. Do not give clinical advice. Connect them with a health professional or the crisis service. The participant is safe, and the right people know what is happening. REG-SCO-01 col AE Within 2 hours in business hours. Outside them, as Q27 says (our standard)

t: Tell the Service Manager.
x: Tell the Service Manager. The coordinator Phone them. Say what happened, how the participant is, what you have done and which providers are involved. For a death, a serious injury or an allegation of abuse, phone at any hour. If the concern is about the Service Manager, phone the Chief Executive. In a provider with one owner, phone the independent contact for concerns. The Service Manager offers you a debrief within 5 business days. A manager knows, and can help the participant and the coordinator. REG-SCO-01 col AE Straight away for a death, a serious injury or an allegation of abuse. Otherwise the same day (our standard)

t: Raise an incident report.
x: Raise an incident report. the event is, or may be, an incident in connection with our supports, or you cannot tell The coordinator Use FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form and follow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. An incident in connection with our supports includes harm during our contact. It includes something we did or did not do, and an allegation about one of our workers. Raise it whenever we learn of it, whether or not another provider also reports it: we are a provider to this participant in our own right. When unsure, raise it. The Quality Manager decides under PRO-INC-02 Reportable Incidents Notification Procedure whether it is in connection with our supports and whether it is reportable, and notifies the NDIS Commission: within 24 hours of becoming aware where the incident involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm; otherwise within 5 business days. Ask the participant whether they want help to contact the Commission. With their consent, ask the other provider to confirm it has reported. If you believe a person is at serious risk, you can also phone the NDIS Commission yourself on 1800 035 544. The incident record exists, and the NDIS Commission is told in time where our supports are involved. REG-SCO-01 col AM Before the end of that day (our standard). For a reportable incident the law requires you to tell the Quality Manager, or the person our incident system names, as soon as possible (the Incident Rules, section 19)

t: Review the Risk and Crisis Response Plan with the participant.
x: Review the Risk and Crisis Response Plan with the participant. a review date arrives, or a trigger in Decision table 4 happens The coordinator Start fresh. Ask what is working, what has happened and what they want now. Check each section. Update the warning signs, the call list, our hours and the providers. Rate each risk again. If the level changes, set new times from Decision table 2 the same day. After a crisis, ask what would have helped and what we got wrong. Make a new version, give the participant their copy and brief each affected provider again (step 18). For a participant at high or extreme risk, the case reviewer reads the new version. Consult the network and mainstream services (step 13) before an NDIA plan review. The plan is current, the participant has it, and the providers have been told what changed. FRM-SCO-01 Q37 to Q41; REG-SCO-01 col S; REG-SCO-01 col T By the time in Decision table 4, and by the date in col T (our standard)

t: Hand over the plan and close the row.
x: Hand over the plan and close the row. coordination is ending, or the coordinator is changing for good The coordinator Follow PRO-SUP-04 Transitions to or from a Provider Procedure for notice and handover. With the participant's consent, give the next coordinator the plan, the provider list, the open actions and the report dates, before our last day. Tell each provider who the new contact is. If we must stop at short notice, the cover coordinator holds the plan until the next coordinator is confirmed. PRO-COS-01 Continuity of Supports Procedure applies. If the participant refuses handover, record it and give them their copy. Close the row only when the closing conditions in REG-SCO-01 Entry rules are all true. The Service Manager approves the closing. The participant is not left without a plan, and the row is closed correctly. REG-SCO-01 col AK; REG-SCO-01 col AL Before our last day of coordination (our standard)

t: Decision table 1: overall risk level (step 4 for the provisional level, step 8 for the fin
x: Decision table 1: overall risk level (step 4 for the provisional level, step 8 for the final level). Use the highest rating at Q12. Raise the level one step, to extreme at most, when Q14 shows a serious risk to someone else. At the first meeting, set a provisional level from the answers to the three safety questions. If Then the level is A risk is rated extreme. Or serious harm or loss of life is likely within 4 weeks. Or a critical support is likely to stop within 14 days with nothing in place Extreme The highest rating is high. Or three or more risks rated medium make each other worse High The highest rating is medium, and no critical support is at risk Medium Every risk is low Low. Tell the participant and the Service Manager within 2 business days. Use the Medium times. The participant and the Service Manager decide together whether this support fits. Any change to funding is the NDIA's decision, through a plan review the participant asks for Decision table 2: times for each level (steps 1, 4, 8 to 12, 20, 21 and 29). Plan times count from the date of the first meeting, the second date in col C. The provisional level set at step 4 starts the clock; the final level set at step 8 can shorten the remaining time but never lengthen it. The interim safety steps at step 4 are always agreed at the first meeting. Overall level Plan made within (from the first meeting) Case reviewer reads Contact with the participant at least Coordination meeting and plan review at least Extreme Interim plan (Section A and the call list at Q25 and Q26) within 1 business day; full plan within 5 business days Before the plan is issued, within 2 business days of receiving the draft Every week Every 4 weeks High 10 business days Before the plan is issued, within 2 business days of receiving the draft Every 2 weeks Every 2 months Medium 15 business days Within 10 business days of issue Every 4 weeks Every 3 months Low 15 business days Within 10 business days of issue Every 4 weeks Every 3 months Decision table 3: what to check for each kind of provider (steps 15 and 16). If the support is Then check Paid from funds the NDIA manages The provider must be a registered NDIS provider (NDIS Act 2013, section 73B, note). On the NDIS Provider Register check that registration is in force, covers the class of support, and has no condition or suspension that stops it Specialist disability accommodation, specialist behaviour support assessment or plans, or any support where a regulated restrictive practice is or is likely to be needed The provider must be registered (the Registration Rules, section 7). Check the class of support on the Register. Supported independent living is not in section 7: a SIL provider must be registered only where row 1 applies (the funds are NDIA-managed, which is usual for SIL) or a regulated restrictive practice is involved Paid from funds the participant or a plan manager manages, and none of the above The provider may be registered or not. Search the Register for a banning order or compliance action (NDIS Act 2013, section 73ZDA). The Code applies to every NDIS provider, registered or not. Ask them to confirm they follow it A mainstream service such as health, housing, justice, child safety, mental health, education or transport Eligibility, cost, waiting time, access and how they take referrals. No Register check Any provider or service Evidence of skills and experience with people in a similar situation. Availability and place. Fit with the participant's language, culture and preferences. Whether we hold an interest (step 14) Decision table 4: when to review the plan early (step 29). If Then review the plan within A crisis, an incident or a breakdown of supports 5 business days of the event The participant moves, goes into or comes out of hospital, loses their housing, or someone moves in or out 5 business days of our knowing A provider the plan relies on starts, changes or stops a support 5 business days of our knowing Police, a court, child protection or a guardianship tribunal becomes involved 5 business days of our knowing A person the participant agreed we may talk to raises a worry about the participant's safety 5 business days of the call A new NDIS plan starts, or the funding changes 10 business days of getting the new plan The participant asks for a review 10 business days of the request The risk level changes Set the new times the same day The interval in Decision table 2 ends The date in col T

x: If Then The participant does not want an assessment or a plan, or refuses part of it Respect it. Explain what the plan does and what happens without it. Agree the smallest version they accept: the safety questions at Q7 to Q9 and the call list at Q26. Write "chose not to say" at Q39. Tell the Service Manager within 2 business days. High risk: the same steps, finished by the end of the next business day. Where there is an immediate risk to life, call 000 whatever the plan says. Never contact a person named at Q6. Tell the Service Manager the same day, and the case reviewer for a sole trader.
