Tell the Service Manager at the end of that time. Keep the plan open and try again at the next interval The coordinator is away, sick or cannot be reached The cover coordinator takes over the same business day and reads the plan if they have not. The Service Manager tells the participant who to contact. For a sole trader, the cover coordinator is the coordinator from another provider named on adoption. If no cover can be reached, the Service Manager or the Chief Executive acts, and phones each participant at high or extreme risk that day A provider will not engage, or has not confirmed after 10 business days The Service Manager phones their manager. Tell the participant. Offer the next choice from step 15. If their response puts the participant at risk, raise it as an incident (step 28) or a complaint under PRO-FBK-01 A provider gives short notice to stop, or a worker does not arrive Go to step 26. Phone the provider, then the next choice at Q32. Tell the participant what is happening. PRO-COS-01 Continuity of Supports Procedure applies The plan is within 12 weeks of its reassessment date and no review has been scheduled Ask the NDIA in writing, with the participant's agreement, to confirm the reassessment date. Tell the participant that the plan stays in effect until a new plan starts. Tell the Service Manager. If supports are at risk, go to step 26 A report deadline will be missed Tell the recipient before the date passes and give a new date. Tell the Service Manager the same day. Write the reason at col AH. The Quality Manager tells the Chief Executive of any report more than 10 business days late Coordination hours or funding will run out before the plan ends Tell the participant and the Service Manager within 5 business days of the check. Agree priorities with the participant. They may ask the NDIA for a plan review. Do not stop contact with a participant at extreme risk without a handover under step 30. The Chief Executive decides what unfunded contact we can carry and for how long; ask the NDIA for a plan variation the same day The participant chooses a risk you are worried about Do not stop them and do not withdraw. Explain the risk and the options in a way they understand. Complete FRM-RGT-04 Dignity of Risk Decision Record for a risk rated high or extreme. t: NDIS Practice Standards, Module 4, Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports: Quality In
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Policy
x: NDIS Practice Standards, Module 4, Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports: Quality Indicators Guidelines section 65; Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 6, clause 4. This is the controlled policy for clause 4; POL-SCO-01 commitment 12 points here. Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 6, clauses 3 and 5: specialised support coordination and conflict of interest, the standards that sit beside this one. Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 1, clauses 3, 4, 6, 12, 13 and 20: person-centred supports, individual values and beliefs, independence and informed choice, information management, complaints and service agreements. NDIS Act 2013, sections 73F(2)(b) and (c), 73J, 73T and 73V: complying with the NDIS Code of Conduct and the Practice Standards is a condition of registration. NDIS Act 2013, section 73B (note) and section 73ZDA: when the NDIA manages the funds, a registered provider must provide the supports. The NDIS Provider Register lists registered providers and banning orders. Code Rules, section 6(1)(a), (b), (d), (e) and (f): self-determination and decision-making, privacy, integrity, honesty and transparency, raising concerns, and preventing exploitation. National Disability Insurance Scheme (Complaints Management and Resolution) Rules 2018, when a participant complains about our advice or a decision. NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years. That is the floor for every record of a support we arranged or claimed. Seven years is our standard for the other records in this thread, and until the participant turns 25 where they were under 18. It matches the 7 years the Incident Rules and the Complaints Rules set for their records. Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), where it applies to us, and the privacy and health records law of [state or territory]. The guardianship and decision-making law of [state or territory]: who may decide for a participant. Law changing: from 20 November 2026 a new section 73VA of the NDIS Act 2013 makes it an offence and a civil penalty for an NDIS provider to give or offer any gift or benefit likely to induce a person to use its services (Act No. 66, 2026, Schedule 2, Part 8). Ground rule 3 already bars gifts and benefits. Review it on that date. Law changing: from 1 December 2026 the time a provider has to make a payment claim under the NDIS Act 2013 falls. It is 2 years now and becomes 90 days. Review step 26 of PRO-SCO-03 on that date. Law changing: from 1 February 2027 the Act's rules on plan renewal and on reasonable and necessary supports change. Review commitment 9 and steps 6, 24 and 30 of PRO-SCO-03 before that date. Law changing: the Act will require plan managers to be registered, on a date to be fixed. When it starts, a registered plan manager cannot also be registered for other supports: remove plan management from our list of interests or restructure. Review how we record the plan manager (FRM-SCO-02 Q5) when it starts.

t: participant: a person with disability we provide specialised support coordination to. fund
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Policy
x: participant: a person with disability we provide specialised support coordination to. funds: the NDIS amounts in a participant's plan, which the plan sets for each support category. NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency". direction: what the participant tells us about which support, from whom, from which funds, and for what purpose. decision maker: the person who decides. It is the participant, unless a legal document gives that role to someone else. supporter: a person the participant chooses to help them decide. A supporter does not decide for them. option: a way to meet a need. It may be a funded provider, a mainstream service, a community group or an informal support. mainstream services: services for the whole community, such as health, education, transport and housing. informal supports: help from family, friends and neighbours. It is unpaid. NDIA-managed, plan-managed, self-managed: who pays providers from the funds. It is the NDIA, a plan manager, or the participant. value for money: the best result for the participant's goals from the funds, judged on price and quality together, not on price alone. skills plan: the small steps a participant agrees to take to coordinate, direct or manage more of their own supports. funds check: our monthly comparison, for each funding category, of the share of the participant's funds used and booked with the share of plan time elapsed. independent contact for concerns: in a small provider, the outside person who receives concerns about the owner. This may be the case reviewer. case reviewer: the person who reads and challenges coordination work, as POL-SCO-01 sets out. For a sole trader, a person outside the business who also does the checks that would otherwise be done by the person who did the work. plan manager: a person or business that pays a participant's providers from their funds and keeps the records for them. NDIS Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission, which registers and oversees providers. independent advocate: a person outside [Provider name] who speaks up for the participant's wishes and rights. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. price limit: the most that can be claimed from NDIA-managed or plan-managed funds for a type of support, set by the NDIA. A self-managed participant may agree a higher price. Where none applies to a support, we say so on the record.

w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Policy

t: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
w: Management of a participant’s NDIS supports

t: The result: each participant decides how their funds are used, understands their options,
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: The result: each participant decides how their funds are used, understands their options, builds the skills they want, and sees their funds used well. This procedure gives effect to POL-SCO-02 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Policy, C1 to C14. Short names used here: "The NDIA" means the National Disability Insurance Agency. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency". "Funds" means the NDIS amounts in the participant's plan. "The Code Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018.

t: Start this procedure when any of these happens: a participant starts specialised support c
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Start this procedure when any of these happens: a participant starts specialised support coordination with us a participant asks for a new support, or to change or end one a participant says a support is not working a funds check, a 3 monthly review or a plan review comes due. Who acts: The coordinator does every step. The Service Manager takes every escalation, and names a cover coordinator for each participant (PRO-SCO-02 step 1). The Quality Manager samples the records. POL-SCO-02 sets those checks, so they are not steps here. If you are a sole trader, you do every step yourself. Where a step says to tell the Service Manager, write the date and time and, for a participant at high or extreme risk or for a same-day matter, tell your case reviewer: the person outside the business named on adoption (PRO-SCO-02, When and who). The case reviewer reads five of your records every 3 months, or all of them if you have fewer than five. A concern about you goes to the independent contact for concerns named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register; this may be the case reviewer.

t: You have a new copy of FRM-SCO-02 Support Options and Choice Record for this decision, fun
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: You have a new copy of FRM-SCO-02 Support Options and Choice Record for this decision, funds check or review. It has its own record number. You know where the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form and FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form are filed. You have time booked with the participant. They choose the place, the time and who comes. You have walked through this procedure with the Service Manager. REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register shows it. For a funds check, you have the figures from the participant, the plan manager or the NDIA portal, with consent. Before first use, the Service Manager checks that this procedure has no square bracket left to fill. The cover coordinator for each participant is named under PRO-SCO-02 step 1. The Quality Manager checks that none is left blank. Urgent path: where the support is critical or urgent (PRO-SCO-02 step 15; PRO-SCO-01 Decision table 3), do steps 5 to 20 within 3 business days, by phone where needed, and complete the record within 2 business days afterwards. The participant still chooses. The urgent path shortens our clocks, never their time to decide; you tell them plainly what will stop and when.

t: The participant decides, not the person pushing. A family member, provider or worker may p
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: The participant decides, not the person pushing. A family member, provider or worker may press for a choice. Following them instead of the participant takes away the participant's control. It can also hide abuse or exploitation. "Do you understand?" is not a check. People say yes to end a hard conversation. A choice made without understanding is not the participant's choice. Never hold their money. We are not the participant's plan manager. Money that passes through us is unlawful plan management and a conflict of interest, and it can harm the participant. Never take a gift or benefit from a provider. It makes your advice untrue. It is a conflict of interest and may be a breach of the Code Rules. A guess is not a "no". Telling a participant their plan will not cover something, without checking, can stop them using funds they are entitled to. Share only what the participant agreed. Telling a provider more than they agreed breaches their privacy. A rushed choice is not a free choice. Pressure to decide fast, or a false deadline, leaves the participant with a support they did not choose. Funds can run out or sit unused without anyone noticing. A support that stops partway through a plan can leave the participant without care. Our interest must be known before they choose. If we, or someone linked to us, gain from an option, the participant must hear it from us first.

t: Steps
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure

t: Confirm who makes the decision for the participant.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Confirm who makes the decision for the participant. Coordinator Start with the participant. An adult decides for themself unless a legal document says otherwise. Use Decision table 1. Ask to see any guardianship order, nomination or parental authority, note what it covers and when it ends, and file a copy. Write the record number in question 1. You know who decides, and the participant's own voice is still heard. FRM-SCO-02 Q1 to Q2; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col A, col B and col D Before the first conversation about options (our standard)

t: Confirm how the participant wants to communicate for this conversation.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Confirm how the participant wants to communicate for this conversation. Coordinator Read their FRM-RGT-01 and ask whether it is still right. Ask about language, an interpreter, Auslan, pictures, a device, more time, and who they want with them. Book what they need before you meet. If it cannot be booked in time, move the meeting and tell the participant why. The meeting will be in the participant's way of communicating, with the people they chose. FRM-SCO-02 Q3 Before the first conversation about options (our standard)

t: Confirm what the participant allows us to share, and with whom.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Confirm what the participant allows us to share, and with whom. Coordinator Check that FRM-INF-01 covers the NDIA, any plan manager, and each provider and service you may contact. If it does not, ask the participant to update it. Without consent, contact no one. Work only from what the participant tells you. You know exactly who you may contact and what you may say. FRM-SCO-02 Q4 Before you contact anyone (our standard)

t: Record the plan dates, how the funds are managed, and what is left.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Record the plan dates, how the funds are managed, and what is left. Coordinator Ask the participant for their plan or latest statement. Look in the NDIA portal only with their consent, and show them what you see. For plan-managed funds, ask the plan manager. For self-managed funds, ask the participant for their records. The participant may share only part. Write "not shared" for the rest. You know the plan dates, the funds and who manages them. FRM-SCO-02 Q5 to Q6 Within 3 business days of step 3 (our standard)

t: Ask the participant what they want to achieve and how they want to use their funds.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Ask the participant what they want to achieve and how they want to use their funds. Coordinator Ask open questions and write their words, not yours. Ask what matters most, what they do not want, and which providers they like or want to avoid. Do not suggest options yet. The participant's purpose is on the record, in their own words, before any option is put. FRM-SCO-02 Q7 to Q8 Within 5 business days of the participant's request (our standard)

t: Check whether the support can be arranged as the participant wants.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Check whether the support can be arranged as the participant wants. Telling a participant "the plan will not cover that" on a guess can stop them using funds they are entitled to. Coordinator Use Decision table 2. Check the plan wording, the support category, the NDIA price limit that applies and how the funds are managed, and whether the support is safe and lawful. If you are not sure, help the participant ask their NDIA contact or planner, with their consent, and record the question and the date. Step 7's time runs from the answer, and you tell the participant what is waiting. Do not guess. You know whether you can arrange it, and why. FRM-SCO-02 Q9 Within 5 business days of step 5 (our standard)

t: Tell the participant what you cannot do, why, and what else is possible.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Tell the participant what you cannot do, why, and what else is possible. you cannot arrange the support as the participant wants Coordinator Use their way of communicating. Offer the nearest option, other funds if the plan allows, a request to the NDIA to change the plan, and an independent advocate. Tell them how to complain, as PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure sets out. Help them ask for a review if they want one. The NDIA decision notice says how and by when. Do not decide for them. When they choose, carry on from step 8 with the changed need. If the reason is that the support is unlawful, tell the Service Manager the same day. The participant knows where they stand and chooses what to do next. FRM-SCO-02 Q10 Within 2 business days of step 6 (our standard)

t: Find the options for each need.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Find the options for each need. Coordinator Follow the options rule in POL-SCO-02 C4: find at least three suitable options able to meet the need, of which at least two have no relationship to us, where that many exist, and say which have a relationship to us (step 12). List mainstream services, community groups and informal supports such as family and friends as well, not instead. Add every provider the participant names. Never leave one out because it competes with us, or because you do not know it. If fewer exist, write why. A fair list of options exists, and it is not limited to what we know or sell. FRM-SCO-02 Q11 Within 10 business days of step 6 (our standard)

t: Check each funded provider on the NDIS Provider Register.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Check each funded provider on the NDIS Provider Register. A provider that is not registered cannot be paid from NDIA-managed funds. A provider whose banning order covers this support must never be put to a participant. Coordinator Check that the provider is registered for this support. Check for a banning order and read what it prohibits or restricts. Note the date. Drop any provider whose order covers this support, and tell the Service Manager. If the funds are NDIA-managed, drop any provider that is not registered, and tell the participant why. For other funds, tell the participant that an unregistered provider is not assessed against the NDIS Practice Standards. The Code of Conduct still applies to them. Every funded option can be paid from the participant's funds, and none is banned. FRM-SCO-02 Q12 Before step 13 (our standard)

t: Ask each provider and service the same questions, and write the answers.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Ask each provider and service the same questions, and write the answers. Coordinator Ask the same questions of every option. Ask what the support would do, the price for each unit and the total for what the participant wants. Ask how soon it can start, where, and who would deliver it. Ask how the participant can change or end it. Ask only what you need. Name the participant only with their consent. Write "not known" where you could not find out. Every option has the same facts, so the participant can compare them. FRM-SCO-02 Q13 Within 10 business days of step 6 (our standard)

t: Compare the options on price and quality against what the participant wants.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Compare the options on price and quality against what the participant wants. Coordinator Check how the funds for this support are managed. For NDIA-managed and plan-managed funds, a price above the NDIA price limit cannot be claimed: tell the participant and offer other options. For self-managed funds the participant may pay more: tell them the limit, what the difference will cost from their budget, and record their decision. Where no limit applies, compare the price with similar options and write that. Compare the total with the funds left. Compare quality on what matters to the participant: skills, experience, place, hours, culture and language. Do not rank by cost alone. Keep a dearer option on the list if the participant may prefer it. The participant has a plain comparison tied to their own goals. FRM-SCO-02 Q14 Before step 13 (our standard)

t: Tell the participant about the interest before they hear about the option.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Tell the participant about the interest before they hear about the option. we, or a person or business linked to us, provide an option or gain from it Coordinator Follow PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure and complete FRM-SCO-03 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Disclosure Record. Show the option as one among the others. Tell the participant that their choice will not change how we coordinate for them. The participant knows of our interest before they hear about the option. FRM-SCO-02 Q15 Before step 13 (our standard)

t: Go through the options with the participant, one at a time, in the format they use.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Go through the options with the participant, one at a time, in the format they use. Coordinator Prepare each option in their format before you meet: spoken, large print, pictures or symbols, a plain summary, audio or video, a translation, or Auslan. Let them set the pace and the place. Say what each option would do, cost and need, and how soon it could start. Say what you do not know. Give your own view only if they ask, and say it is your view. The participant has the facts on every option in a form they can use. FRM-SCO-02 Q16 Within 5 business days of step 11 (our standard)

t: Ask the participant to tell you, in their own way, what each option is and what choosing i
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Ask the participant to tell you, in their own way, what each option is and what choosing it would mean. Coordinator Do not ask "Do you understand?". Write what they say, sign or show. If something is missing, explain it another way and ask again. If they still cannot, offer more time or a supporter they choose. If it is still not clear, see "If it goes wrong". You know the participant understands, or you know what is still to explain. FRM-SCO-02 Q17 In the same meeting as step 13 (our standard)

t: Tell the participant how long they have to decide, and leave the decision with them.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Tell the participant how long they have to decide, and leave the decision with them. Coordinator Say any real deadline, such as the plan end date or a provider's waiting list, and where it comes from. Say they can take time, talk to people they trust and ask for an advocate. If they want to wait, agree a date to ask again. Never say an offer will close unless it will. The participant decides at their own pace, knowing any real deadline. FRM-SCO-02 Q18 At the end of the same meeting as step 14 (our standard)

t: Write down what the participant decided and exactly how they direct their funds.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Write down what the participant decided and exactly how they direct their funds. Coordinator Use their words for the decision and the purpose. Write the support, the provider, the funds to use, how much, the start and end dates, and any condition they set. If they have not decided, write "not decided", the date to ask again and any deadline. If they choose none of the options, write that, and go back to step 8 with what they said was missing. If they later change their mind, open a new copy and keep this one. The decision and the direction are on the record in the participant's terms. FRM-SCO-02 Q19 to Q20; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col C and col I On the day the participant decides (our standard)

t: Explain the risk, and record what you said and what the participant chose.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Explain the risk, and record what you said and what the participant chose. the participant's choice carries a risk to them Coordinator Say the risk in plain words and what could reduce it. A risk alone is never a reason to refuse. If the risk is serious, complete FRM-RGT-04 Dignity of Risk Decision Record, follow PRO-RGT-04 Independence and Informed Choice Procedure, and tell the Service Manager. The participant chose with the risk in view, and their choice stands. FRM-SCO-02 Q21 In the same meeting as step 16 (our standard)

t: Ask the participant for their own wishes, and record them beside the decision.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Ask the participant for their own wishes, and record them beside the decision. someone other than the participant makes the decision Coordinator Ask in their way of communicating, and alone if they want that. If their wishes differ from the decision, record both and tell the Service Manager the same day. The decision maker's legal authority stands. Ask them to take the participant's wishes into account, and offer the participant an advocate. The participant's own voice is on the record. FRM-SCO-02 Q22 In the same meeting as step 16 (our standard)

t: Read the record back to the participant and ask whether it says what they want.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Read the record back to the participant and ask whether it says what they want. Coordinator Use their format. Change anything they say is wrong. Tell them they can change the record at any time. Tell them they can ask for a different coordinator or an independent advocate. Tell them they can complain to us or to the NDIS Commission. Say how to do each. Ask them to confirm in the way they choose. The participant has confirmed the record and knows their rights. FRM-SCO-02 Q23 to Q24 In the same meeting as step 16 (our standard)

t: Arrange the support exactly as the participant directed.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Arrange the support exactly as the participant directed. Taking, holding or paying out a participant's funds, or accepting a gift from a provider, puts the participant at risk and ends our independence. Coordinator Contact the provider with the participant's consent and share only what the provider needs. Ask the provider to confirm the support, the price, the start date and who will deliver it. Make sure the provider can be paid from the funds the participant chose, in the way those funds are managed. Agree no change without the participant. Take, hold and pay out no funds, and accept no gift or benefit. The support is arranged as directed, and nothing passes through us. FRM-SCO-02 Q25 Within 2 business days of step 19 (our standard)

t: Check with the participant that what was arranged matches their direction.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Check with the participant that what was arranged matches their direction. Coordinator Compare the provider's confirmation with question 20, line by line. Tell the participant each difference and why. Change nothing until they agree. If it does not match and cannot be fixed, go back to step 16. Give them their copy of sections A to F, in their format. The participant has agreed that the arrangement is theirs. FRM-SCO-02 Q26; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col J Within 2 business days of the provider's confirmation (our standard)

t: Help the participant make their own service agreement with the provider.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Help the participant make their own service agreement with the provider. Coordinator Explain what a service agreement is. It should cover the supports, the price, how to cancel or change it, and how to complain. Let the participant read it in their format. For NDIA-managed and plan-managed funds, check the prices against the NDIA price limit that applies; for self-managed funds, check the price is the one the participant agreed at question 14. Check the terms against question 20. The participant, or their decision maker, signs. Never sign for them. AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template shows what a good agreement covers. The participant understands and has agreed the terms with the provider. FRM-SCO-02 Q27 Before the first support is delivered (our standard)

t: Agree with the participant which skills they want to build, and how.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Agree with the participant which skills they want to build, and how. Coordinator Go through each skill on question 28: coordinating supports, choosing and changing providers, managing funds and budget, directing workers, taking part in plan reviews, making service agreements, and using the flexibility in the plan. Ask what they do now and what they want to do alone. "Not now" is a valid answer. Record it, and ask again at each 3 monthly review. Never tie a support to whether they want to learn. A skills plan in the participant's words exists, or their choice not to have one is recorded. FRM-SCO-02 Q28 to Q29; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col K Within 20 business days of the first record, then at each 3 monthly review (our standard)

t: Explain how NDIA planning works and the participant's part in it.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Explain how NDIA planning works and the participant's part in it. Coordinator Cover how a plan review works and what the participant brings. Cover how to ask for a change, how service agreements work, and how funds can move within the plan. Use their format and ask them to say it back. Add what you gave to REG-RGT-01 Communication and Accessible Information Register. The participant understands how to take part in NDIA planning. FRM-SCO-02 Q30 Within 20 business days of the first record, and again at step 30 (our standard)

t: Review the participant's skills plan with them.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Review the participant's skills plan with them. Coordinator Ask what they now do on their own. Hand over one more task if they want it. Step back where they can manage. Agree the date of the next review. The skills plan is up to date, and you have stepped back as far as the participant wants. FRM-SCO-02 Q31 Every 3 months from the first record (our standard)

t: Check each category of the participant's funds against what was planned.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Check each category of the participant's funds against what was planned. Coordinator This is the one monthly funds check, set in PRO-SCO-02 step 22 and recorded on FRM-SCO-02 Section H; do not run a second one. Use the participant's statement, the plan manager's statement or the NDIA portal, with consent. For each category, compare the share of the plan amount used and booked with the share of the plan time that has passed, and write the forecast at plan end. Mark any gap over 15 percentage points. Show the participant what you found, and tell them within 5 business days. You and the participant both know where the funds stand. FRM-SCO-02 Q32 to Q34; REG-SCO-01 col AF; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col L In the first 5 business days of each month (our standard)

t: Work out why, and agree with the participant what to do.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Work out why, and agree with the participant what to do. a category is off track, or will run out before the plan ends Coordinator Use Decision table 3. Ask the provider and the participant what caused it. Offer the options and let the participant choose. Tell the Service Manager the same day if funds will run out more than 30 days before the plan ends. The participant has chosen what to do, and the Service Manager knows of any early run out. FRM-SCO-02 Q35 Within 5 business days of step 26 (our standard)

t: Check with the participant whether each funded support is helping them reach their goal.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Check with the participant whether each funded support is helping them reach their goal. Coordinator Ask the participant first, in their way. Then look at hours delivered against hours planned, cancellations, progress against the goal, and any concern or complaint. If a support is not helping, offer to change or end it. If they agree, go back to step 8 for a new option, or end it as they direct. When a support changes or ends, check that FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan still names who acts if it breaks down. Each support is kept, changed or ended on the participant's decision. FRM-SCO-02 Q36; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col M Every 3 months, or within 10 business days of the participant saying a support is not working (our standard)

t: Link the participant with the mainstream, community and informal supports they chose.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Link the participant with the mainstream, community and informal supports they chose. Coordinator For each need, ask which they want to try, such as health, education, transport, housing, work, local groups, family and friends. With consent, make the introduction, go with them if they ask, and follow up. Write what is in the way. If a mainstream service refuses or has a long wait, offer an advocate and tell the Service Manager. The participant is connected to the supports they chose, and barriers are known. FRM-SCO-02 Q37 Within 10 business days of the participant agreeing (our standard)

t: Prepare the participant for their plan review.
w: Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure
x: Prepare the participant for their plan review. Coordinator Follow PRO-SCO-02 step 23, which sets the one plan review preparation: start 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date; give the participant their plain summary of how funds were used, what worked and what did not, with the draft report, at least 8 weeks before it; the report goes 6 weeks before it, or by the NDIA's date (PRO-SCO-02 step 24). Ask what they want in the next plan and write it in their words. Offer to go with them. The participant decides what to ask for. Repeat step 24. The participant goes into the plan review prepared, and in charge of what they ask for. FRM-SCO-02 Q38; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col N Start 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date (our standard)

t: Use this record to show how a participant chose a support and how we explained their optio
x: Use this record to show how a participant chose a support and how we explained their options. It also shows how their funds are used and watched, and what they are learning to do for themself. The coordinator completes it with the participant, and writes the participant's words, not their own. Use a new copy each time, and give each copy its own record number. This form holds four uses in one; the list below gives the minimum questions for each use (a split into separate forms is planned for 0.4.0): When: a decision about a support (Sections A to F). Complete these questions: 1 to 27, with 10, 21 and 22 only where they apply. One copy may cover several supports arranged together for the same purpose; name each support at question 20. When: the skills plan (Section G). Complete these questions: on the copy for the participant's first decision, 1 and 28 to 30; at each 3 monthly review, 1, 28, 29 and 31 on the review copy; question 30 again when you prepare the plan review. When: the monthly funds check (Section H), a new copy every month in the first 5 business days of the month. Complete these questions: 1 and 32 to 35. This is the one monthly funds check for the participant (PRO-SCO-02 step 22). When: the support review and plan review preparation (Section I). Complete these questions: at each 3 monthly review, 1, 36 and 37; from 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date, 1 and 38. Answer question 1 on every copy. File every copy for a participant together, newest last. Have ready: the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form their consent in FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form their plan or latest statement, if they choose to share it. Ask the participant themself first. Ask a family member or other supporter only when the participant wants that, or when that person holds legal authority to decide. What happens next: the coordinator enters each copy as a row in REG-SCO-01 Support Coordination Register sheet 2 and gives the participant their copy. PRO-SCO-03 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure sets every step. Short names used in the question protocol: "The Practice Standards Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018. "The Code Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018.

t: We collect this information to help you choose supports, to arrange them as you direct and
x: We collect this information to help you choose supports, to arrange them as you direct and to watch your funds with you. We also collect it to meet our duties under the NDIS Act 2013 and the NDIS Practice Standards. Your coordinator and the Service Manager read it. The Quality Manager reads samples to check our work. We share it with a provider, a service or a person only as you agree in FRM-INF-01, or where a law requires or allows it. We never share it to push you towards a choice. You can choose not to answer a question. Tell us, and we will explain what that means for the help we can give. You can ask to see what we hold and ask us to correct it. We keep this record for 7 years after your coordination with us ends, or longer where the NDIS Act 2013 (section 45B) or the law of [state or territory] requires, and until you turn 25 if you were under 18. We use it only for your supports. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.

t: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure
The result: every participant who uses [Provider name] for support coordination hears our
w: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure
x: The result: every participant who uses [Provider name] for support coordination hears our conflict of interest policy. They hear about every interest we hold in a support they may choose. They hear that their choice of provider never changes their coordination. Every referral to or from another provider is on the record. This procedure gives effect to POL-SCO-01 Specialised Support Coordination Policy, C13, and to the options rule in POL-SCO-02 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Policy, C4. It is also the support coordination part of the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02). An interest is anything that [Provider name], a worker, or a person close to either could gain from a participant's choice of provider. It can be money, a business, a home, a favour or a referral arrangement. A referral is each time we pass a participant to another provider, or another provider or person passes a participant to us. In this procedure: "coordination" means specialised support coordination "the Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018 "the Code of Conduct Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018. the business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

t: Start this procedure when any of these happens: A person asks us for support coordination
w: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure
x: Start this procedure when any of these happens: A person asks us for support coordination (steps 1 to 13). A participant needs a support from another provider, or asks to change provider (steps 14 to 18, 20 to 22 and 24 to 27). Someone refers a participant to us (steps 14, 19 to 21 and 23 to 27). A plan review comes up, 12 months pass, or one of our interests changes (step 28). A person who has not yet signed with us is covered in the same way as a participant (the Registration Rules, Schedule 6, clause 1(2)(a)). Two procedures send you here. PRO-SCO-02 Specialised Support Coordination Procedure step 14 does it before a provider is named. PRO-SCO-03 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure step 12 does it when we hold an interest in an option. Use FRM-SCO-02 Support Options and Choice Record for the detail of each option. This procedure adds our interest, the disclosure and the referral record. Who acts: The coordinator does steps 1 to 11, 14 to 26 and 28. The Service Manager owns this procedure and does steps 12, 13, 27 and 29. The Chief Executive keeps REG-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Register and decides each interest of [Provider name] under PRO-GOV-01 Delegations and Decision-Making Procedure. The Quality Manager does step 30. A sole trader is the coordinator, the Service Manager and the Chief Executive. The case reviewer, a person outside the business named on adoption (POL-SCO-01 ground rule 9), reads the rows every 3 months at step 29 and decides any interest the sole trader holds. Name an independent contact for concerns in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register to receive concerns about you; this may be the case reviewer. A provider that offers coordination only still follows every step. Its list of interests then says "none held".

t: You can open REG-GOV-02 and REG-SCO-02 Support Coordination Referral Register. You have FR
w: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure
x: You can open REG-GOV-02 and REG-SCO-02 Support Coordination Referral Register. You have FRM-SCO-03 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Disclosure Record. You have STA-GOV-01 Conflict of Interest: Plain Summary and STA-SCO-01 Specialised Support Coordination: Plain Summary, in the formats your participants use, and the full POL-GOV-02, where the provider has adopted them. Until then, you explain the policy and the difference in plain words (steps 4 and 5 give the words) and record "explained, no document given". You know where the participant's communication needs are kept: FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form and REG-RGT-01 Communication and Accessible Information Register. You know who to call for an independent advocate: [local advocacy service and phone]. You know how to reach the Service Manager today: [Service Manager phone]. Separation of functions: where we also provide other supports, a coordinator is not supervised by, set targets by, or paid by reference to the other service; coordination records are held apart from the other service's records; and a participant may ask for a coordinator from outside the organisation, and we help them find one. The Chief Executive records the arrangement in REG-GOV-02, and the coordinator tells the participant about it at step 6 (FRM-SCO-03 Q12).

t: Telling a participant late takes away their choice. A participant who hears about our inte
w: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure
x: Telling a participant late takes away their choice. A participant who hears about our interest after they choose did not choose freely. A steer is a conflict even when nobody means it. Putting our service first, praising it, or leaving out other options is steering. It can breach the Code of Conduct Rules, section 6(1)(d), which requires integrity, honesty and transparency. Coordination never changes because of a choice. Cutting hours, slowing replies or ending coordination after a participant picks another provider punishes them for choosing. They can complain to the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. "Do you understand?" proves nothing. A yes can mean "I want this to end". Ask the participant to say it in their own words. A signature is not understanding. A participant who signs without having heard each interest has not been told. Nothing is paid for a referral. A payment, commission, referral fee, gift or favour for a referral, given or taken, creates a conflict. Our rule is stricter than the Code of Conduct Rules: we take none and we give none. Law changing: from 20 November 2026, a new section 73VA of the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 makes it an offence and a civil penalty for an NDIS provider to give or offer any gift or benefit likely to induce a person to use its services. Our rule already bans payment for referrals, given or taken, and is wider. Check the section when it starts.

FRM-SCO-03 Q10; REG-SCO-02 col M At the same meeting as step 3, or the next one if the participant asks for more time (our standard)

t: Tell the participant about each interest on your list, in plain words.
w: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure

Ask them to say it back, and write their words. One plain way to say it is "Whoever you choose, we coordinate for you in the same way." The participant can say that choosing someone else is safe. FRM-SCO-03 Q13; REG-SCO-02 col O Before the participant chooses any provider (our standard)

t: Explain how the participant can change coordinator or provider, and how to complain.

The participant is not rushed and can ask someone independent. FRM-SCO-03 Q15; REG-SCO-02 col Q At the same meeting as step 3, or the next one if the participant asks for more time (our standard)

Set the date to go through this again: the next plan review, or 12 months, whichever comes first. Add the row to REG-SCO-02. The decision, the acknowledgement and the next date are on the record. FRM-SCO-03 Q1 to Q3, Q16, Q17 and Q19; REG-SCO-02 col A to col G, col R, col S and col T Within 2 business days of the meeting (our standard)

t: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Disclosure Record
Use this record to show that a participant heard three things, in a way they understand. F
w: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Disclosure Record
x: Use this record to show that a participant heard three things, in a way they understand. First, how we handle conflicts of interest. Second, which interests we hold in the supports they may choose. Third, that their choice of provider never changes their coordination. It also records each referral to or from another provider, and what happened to it. The coordinator completes it with the participant, at the time. Do not write it up later from memory. Section A: every record. Section B: a disclosure record. Complete it at the first meeting where supports are discussed, at each plan review, every 12 months, and when one of our interests changes. Sections C and D: a referral record. Start a new copy for each referral, whether it is out or in. Complete Section C as you put the options and as the participant chooses. Complete Section D when the outcome is known and at the follow-up. Section E: the Service Manager completes it for every record. Have ready: the participant's communication needs the list of our interests from REG-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Register STA-GOV-01 Conflict of Interest: Plain Summary and STA-SCO-01 Specialised Support Coordination: Plain Summary, in the participant's format, where the provider has adopted them; until then, the plain words in PRO-SCO-01 steps 4 and 5 an interpreter or advocate, if the participant wants one. Ask the participant themself. Ask a family member or other supporter only when the participant wants that, or when that person is their legal decision maker. Tell the participant everything either way. What happens next: the Service Manager checks the record and enters it in REG-SCO-02 Support Coordination Referral Register and REG-GOV-02. PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure sets every step.

t: Read this to the participant. We collect this information for three reasons. It shows that
w: Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Disclosure Record
x: Read this to the participant. We collect this information for three reasons. It shows that you were told about our interests before you chose. It keeps a record of each referral made for you. It meets the NDIS Practice Standards and the NDIS Code of Conduct. Your coordinator, the Service Manager, the Chief Executive and the Quality Manager read it. An auditor or the NDIS Commission may see it as the law allows. We share your information with another provider only when you agree, or when a law requires or allows it. FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form records what you agree to. You can ask to see what we hold and ask us to correct it. You can ask us to stop sharing. We keep this record for 7 years after it is closed, or longer where section 45B of the NDIS Act 2013 requires. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.

t: Support Coordination Referral Register
This register is the running record of what each participant heard about our conflicts of
x: This register is the running record of what each participant heard about our conflicts of interest, and of every referral to or from another provider. A disclosure row shows the policy we gave, the interests we told them about and the promise that their choice never changes their coordination. A referral row shows the options, our relationship to each one, what the participant chose, and what happened next. It holds three kinds of row: a disclosure: each time we go through our conflict of interest policy and our interests with a participant a referral out: a participant is sent to, or helped to choose, another provider a referral in: another provider or person refers a participant to us. In this register: "the Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018 "the Code of Conduct Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018. Indicators evidenced: s 66 (1), s 66 (2), s 66 (3) and s 66 (4). The register also supports s 6 (2), s 9 (4), s 9 (5), s 11 (8), s 14 (1) and s 22 (2). Legal basis: the Registration Rules, Schedule 6, clause 5, which gives each participant transparent, factual advice about their support options that promotes choice and control. Clause 1(2)(a) applies the same duty to a person who has not yet become a participant. The Code of Conduct Rules, section 6(1)(a) and (d), require respect for decision-making, and integrity, honesty and transparency. No NDIS rule sets the columns of this register, so the columns are our standard. Section 45B of the NDIS Act 2013 (from 27 August 2026) requires records relating to claimed supports to be kept for 7 years; our retention standard meets it. Retention: keep each row for 7 years after it is closed (our standard). For a participant who was under 18 when the row was made, keep it until they turn 25 when that is later. Which columns apply: Every row fills columns A to J and AK to AM. A disclosure row also fills columns K to T. Columns U to AJ say "not applicable". A referral out row fills columns U to AJ. Columns K to T say "not applicable". A referral in row fills columns U, Y to AA and AC to AJ. Columns V to X and AB say "not applicable". Column AN is filled when a row is closed. A blank is never an answer. Write "none", "no" or "not applicable".

t: SDA agreement: the written agreement between us and a participant about their home. dwelli
x: SDA agreement: the written agreement between us and a participant about their home. dwelling: a home in which we provide SDA. An enrolled dwelling is one the NDIA has enrolled so that SDA can be provided in it. participant: a person with disability who lives in a dwelling, or is offered a place in one. tenant: a person who lives in a dwelling and has a right to be there. eligible participant: a participant the NDIA has decided is eligible for SDA funding (SDA Rules 2020, section 11). other supports: every NDIS support a participant gets apart from the home, from us or from anyone else. Examples are SIL, support coordination and plan management. supported independent living (SIL): help with, or supervision of, daily tasks so a person can live as independently as possible. design category and building type: the features the NDIA enrolled a dwelling under. The SDA Rules 2020 set five design categories and four building types. density limit: a cap on how many eligible participants can be funded for SDA across every dwelling on one parcel of land (SDA Rules 2020, section 31). conflict of interest: a clash between what we, a worker or someone close to us gains and what is best for the participant. It is actual when it affects a decision, potential when it could, and perceived when it looks as if it could. security of tenure: a participant's right to keep living in their home unless the SDA agreement and tenancy law allow it to end. tenancy law: the law of [state or territory] about renting a home, including notices, bonds and entry. notice to vacate: a written notice that tells a participant they must leave their home. tenancy action: a notice to vacate, a breach notice, any rent or board increase, a room move, or a change to the agreement or house rules for one participant. tenure check: the Chief Executive's decision, before a tenancy action is served, on whether anything links it to the participant's support decisions or worries. modification: a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice or communicate. urgent defect: a fault that puts anyone at risk of harm, or stops a participant washing, using the toilet, preparing food, sleeping or leaving home. Examples: no water or power, a gas or electrical fault, a broken lock or door, a failed lift, hoist or fire alarm, a blocked exit. independent advocate: a person who is not part of [Provider name], chosen by the participant, who speaks up for their wishes and rights. An advocate does not make decisions for them. independent contact: in a small provider, a person outside our management, named in REG-GOV-01, who acts when the Chief Executive has an interest. NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency. The SDA Rules 2020 give its notices to its CEO. NDIS Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission. SDA Manager: the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. Tenancy Officer: the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. SDA Rules 2020, SDA Conditions Rule, Practice Standards Rules, Complaints Rules, Incident Rules, Quality Indicators: short names for the instruments in Authority.

t: specialist disability accommodation (SDA): housing built or changed for people with very h
w: Rights and Responsibilities Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: specialist disability accommodation (SDA): housing built or changed for people with very high support needs or extreme functional impairment. It does not include the supports a person receives while living there. enrolled dwelling: a dwelling enrolled with the NDIA as one where SDA can be provided. rights at home: the rights a participant has in their home under tenancy, anti-discrimination, privacy and human rights law and the NDIS Code of Conduct. Examples are a home that is theirs, privacy, and deciding who visits and stays. Others are equal treatment, support to decide for themselves, and asking for a reasonable adjustment. They also include having an advocate and the right to complain. request: any ask by or for a participant to change their dwelling or how we manage it. It counts however it arrives. modification: a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. adjustment: a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice, enter the home or communicate. reasonable adjustment: a change that lets a participant use and enjoy their home on the same basis as other people. We make it unless it is unlawful or unsafe, or it would impose unjustifiable hardship on us (Disability Discrimination Act 1992 (Cth), sections 5, 6, 11 and 25). entry: any time a person acting for us goes into a participant's home or room. format: the language, mode of communication and terms a participant is most likely to understand. It can be words, pictures, signs, audio, large print or an interpreter. say-back: the participant telling or showing us what they understood, in their own way. decision maker: a person with legal authority, by an order or instrument, to decide something for a participant. A family member or advocate is not one unless the order says so. restrictive practice: anything that limits a person's rights or freedom of movement. The law regulates seclusion and chemical, mechanical, physical and environmental restraint. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. SDA Rules 2020: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency. NDIS Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission. SDA Manager: the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. Tenancy Officer: the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.

t: Use this procedure for every SDA dwelling that [Provider name] has enrolled. It starts at
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Use this procedure for every SDA dwelling that [Provider name] has enrolled. It starts at seven points: before a participant signs an agreement, at move-in, every 12 months, and when a right changes (steps 1 to 3 and step 8) before anyone acts for us at a dwelling (steps 4 to 7) before every entry to a participant's home or room (steps 9 to 12) when a participant raises privacy, a relationship, intimacy or sexual expression (steps 13 and 14) when anyone asks for, or sees the need for, a change to a dwelling or to how we manage it (steps 15 to 28) when anyone has a concern that a participant's rights are not respected (step 29) every 3 months (step 30). A request is any ask for a modification or an adjustment. A modification is a change to the building or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice, enter the home or communicate. An entry is any time a person acting for us goes into a participant's home or room. A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. Who acts: The Tenancy Officer is the participant's main contact for the dwelling. The Tenancy Officer explains rights, gives notice of entry, acknowledges requests and keeps the records. The SDA Manager leads this procedure. The SDA Manager briefs and watches workers and contractors, assesses and decides requests, and closes them. The Chief Executive reviews any refusal and hears concerns about the SDA Manager. The Quality Manager reviews the records every 3 months, decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission. Every worker, agent and contractor who acts for us follows steps 9 to 14 and step 29. In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader completes the briefing checklist at step 4 for themselves, and the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register signs it. The independent contact watches their practice at step 5 and reviews any refusal at step 22. The same person hears any concern about the sole trader at step 29. Another NDIS provider that supports a participant in their home is not acting for us. This procedure never stops that provider coming in. Short names used here: SDA Rules 2020: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020 SDA Conditions Rule 2018: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018 Code of Conduct Rules 2018: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018 NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency NDIS Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission

t: A person in danger comes first. Call 000 before you give notice, knock or phone anyone. A
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: A person in danger comes first. Call 000 before you give notice, knock or phone anyone. A delay can cost a life. Step 12 says how far to go in. Entering without lawful notice or agreement breaches the participant's tenancy rights and their privacy. It can frighten them in their own home. A signature is not understanding. A participant who signs what they did not follow has not agreed. The agreement may not hold, and the participant may stop trusting us. Asking why pressures a participant who wants privacy, a visitor or a relationship. It also puts private matters on a record. A request is not a repair. If you treat a request as a repair, the participant loses their say and the decision is never explained. A change can alter the dwelling's enrolment. Work that alters the design category, building type or suitability, or adds a resident beyond the enrolled number, breaches the SDA conditions. The NDIA must be told within 5 business days. Housing never depends on a request. A hint that a participant's home is at risk because they asked for a change, complained or refused to share information is a serious breach. Other residents have rights too. An objection from a resident is heard but is not a veto. A change that affects a resident cannot go ahead until that resident has been asked.
