t: Find out how the participant wants information given to them.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Find out how the participant wants information given to them. The Tenancy Officer Ask the participant, in the way they communicate best, which language, words, pictures, signs, large print, audio or other format they want. Ask whether they want an interpreter, a communication partner or a supporter beside them, and who. Read their FRM-RGT-01 if one exists. If there is none, or it is more than 12 months old, complete a new one with them. Ask who they want told about their home. Record their consent on FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form. If someone says they hold legal authority to decide for the participant, read the order or instrument yourself and file a copy. A family member is not a decision maker unless the order says so. You know the language, mode of communication and terms the participant understands best, and who they want involved. FRM-RGT-01; REG-RGT-01 Before anything about the dwelling is explained or signed, and again every 12 months (our standard)

t: Explain the participant's rights and responsibilities in relation to their dwelling, one t
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Explain the participant's rights and responsibilities in relation to their dwelling, one topic at a time. The Tenancy Officer Use the format from step 1. Cover eight topics in this order. The home is theirs, and what that means for keys, privacy and visitors. When and how we may enter, and the notice we give. How to ask for a repair, and how to ask for a change to the dwelling or to how we manage it. Their responsibilities: rent, care of the home, reporting damage, respecting other residents, and the safety features and fire alarms. Our responsibilities: a home in good repair, safe and secure. Housing is separate from their other supports, and a request, a complaint or a refusal to share information never puts their home at risk. How to complain, how to reach the NDIS Commission, and the right to an advocate. Their right to privacy, relationships, intimacy and sexual expression. STA-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement: Plain Summary and STA-RGT-03 Participant Rights: Plain Summary can help if their format suits. PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) explains the agreement itself. Stop between topics and ask if they want to go on. They can stop and finish another day. The participant has heard each topic in a way they can follow. REG-RGT-01 Before an agreement is signed, at move-in, every 12 months, and within 10 business days of a change to a right (our standard)

t: Check that the participant understood by asking them to say or show it back.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Check that the participant understood by asking them to say or show it back. The Tenancy Officer Ask open questions. For example, ask what they would do if they wanted a lock on their door. Ask what happens when someone needs to come in. Do not ask whether they understand. Write what the participant said or showed, in their words. If they could not say a topic back, explain it another way and ask again. Give them a copy of what you covered, in their format, and note that you did. Give a copy to a supporter only with the participant's consent. A signature is not proof of understanding. You can show that the participant understood, or what is still to explain. REG-RGT-01 At the same sitting as step 2 (our standard)

t: Brief each worker on participants' rights at home before their first visit to a dwelling.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Brief each worker on participants' rights at home before their first visit to a dwelling. The SDA Manager Walk the worker through steps 9 to 14 and Decision tables 1 and 2. Give them the one page of entry notice periods. Cover the participant's rights at home. They have a right to a home that is theirs, and to privacy. They decide who visits and who stays. They have a right to equal treatment and to make their own decisions with support. They have a right to ask for a reasonable adjustment, to an advocate, and to complain. Cover how to find and use each participant's way of communicating. Cover how to knock and wait, and what a worker may never do in a participant's room. Cover why visitors are never signed in, how to respond about relationships and intimacy, and what to do with a concern. Check the worker has signed FRM-HRM-02 NDIS Code of Conduct Acknowledgement Form. Record the briefing under PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure. Repeat it every 12 months and after any change to this procedure. Each worker knows how to act on a participant's rights before they enter a home. REG-HRM-02 Before the worker's first visit to a dwelling, then every 12 months (our standard)

t: Watch each worker's practice at a dwelling and give feedback.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Watch each worker's practice at a dwelling and give feedback. The SDA Manager Go with the worker to a planned visit, with the participant's agreement. Check that notice was given. Check that the worker knocked and waited, and asked before going into a room. Check that they spoke in the participant's format, kept to the purpose of the visit and recorded the entry. Sign the worker off only if they did all of these. A worker who is not yet signed off visits only with a worker who is signed off. In a small provider, the independent contact, or the SIL provider's supervisor with the participant's agreement, may watch the visit and sign the worker off. Ask the participant, in their format, how the visit felt. Record the result under PRO-HRM-03. Practice, and not only training, shows that rights are respected. REG-HRM-02 Within 3 months of the worker's first visit, then every 12 months (our standard)

t: Brief each contractor before each job at a dwelling.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Brief each contractor before each job at a dwelling. The SDA Manager Check the contractor first: the trade licence where the trade needs one, current public liability insurance, an NDIS worker screening clearance where the work involves more than incidental contact with participants, and a signed NDIS Code of Conduct acknowledgement (FRM-HRM-02). PRO-HRM-07 Contractor and External Provider Verification Procedure sets the full check once written. Give the briefing in person and in writing. It covers steps 9 to 12 and the one page of entry notice periods. It sets out what the contractor may never do. They may never enter without notice, go into a bedroom without the participant's agreement, or take photos. They may never move or take belongings, or talk about the participant with others. It also covers leaving the home as found, and who to phone. Ask the contractor to confirm in writing that they have read it. Record the briefing. Contractors enter only as the participant and the law allow. REG-HRM-03 Before the first entry for each job (our standard)

t: Check every house rule, notice, form and agreement we use against participants' rights.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Check every house rule, notice, form and agreement we use against participants' rights. The SDA Manager Read each one a participant sees or signs. Look for anything that limits a participant's access to their home, their belongings, their movement, their visitors, their overnight guests, their privacy or their relationships. Look for a rule that applies to everyone but would stop one person using their home. A limit may stay only where the law requires it. It may also stay where it sits in the participant's own behaviour support plan, with the authorisation the law requires (PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure). A lock, camera, gate or visitor limit that we apply is an environmental restraint: we then act as an implementing provider and need the state or territory authorisation and the NDIS Commission reporting that PRO-BSP-02 requires. A plan that allows the limit, or a SIL provider's request, does not by itself give us that authority. Remove any other limit. Tell each participant affected, in their format. Send any new lock, key rule, camera, microphone, visitor limit or house rule to the Chief Executive. It is not adopted until the Chief Executive has checked it. Check again before any new rule, notice or form is issued. No rule limits a participant's rights without lawful authority. REG-SDA-01 col BN and col BO (house rules check) Within 5 business days of finding a limit. Every 12 months, and before a new rule is issued (our standard)

t: Ask the participant whether their rights at home are respected, and what they want changed
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Ask the participant whether their rights at home are respected, and what they want changed. The Tenancy Officer Sit with the participant in private, in their format, or with the supporter they choose. Ask: Do people knock and wait? Do you get notice before someone comes in? Can you have the visitors you want, and stay with the people you want to? Do you understand your agreement and your rights? Is anything about your home not working for you? Is there anything you want changed? Write the answers in the participant's own words. Anything they want changed starts a request at step 15. If they say a right was not respected, go to step 29. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for any topic they could not say back. Each participant has been heard about their rights at home in the past 12 months. REG-RGT-01; the participant's file Every 12 months from move-in, and within 10 business days of a change in the participant's needs or circumstances (our standard)

t: Give the participant notice of every planned entry, in their format.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Give the participant notice of every planned entry, in their format. Entering a participant's home without lawful notice or agreement breaches their tenancy rights and can frighten them. The Tenancy Officer Say who is coming, why, the day, the time window, which rooms, and how to change the time or say no. Give at least the longer of the notice that tenancy law of [state or territory] sets for that reason and our own minimum: 7 days for an inspection, a check or planned work, and 2 business days for a repair the participant asked for. No notice is needed in an emergency (step 12). A participant may agree to less. Write down that they agreed. Ask for the best time. Send the notice the way they prefer: a text, a letter, a visit or a picture card. In a shared dwelling, give each resident affected their own notice. A notice never covers a bedroom unless it names the room. Use Decision table 1. The participant knows what is coming and has a say about when. REG-SDA-01 col BH (entry record) At least 7 days before an inspection, a check or planned work, and at least 2 business days before a repair the participant asked for (our standard). Where tenancy law of [state or territory] sets a longer notice, the law applies

t: Knock, wait for an answer and ask before you go in.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Knock, wait for an answer and ask before you go in. The person who is entering Knock, say who you are and why you are there. Wait for the participant to answer. If there is no answer, knock again and wait 1 minute. Never use a key to enter a home while the participant is in it, except at step 12. Ask each time before you go into a bedroom, even where the notice named it. If the participant says no or asks you to leave, leave at once and tell the SDA Manager the same day. Stay only as long as the purpose needs. Leave things as you found them. Do not open drawers, cupboards, mail or devices. Do not take photos. Use Decision table 1. The participant lets you in, or you leave. None At the start of every entry (our standard)

t: Record the entry.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Record the entry. The person who entered Write the date and time in and out, who entered and who they work for, and the reason. Write the notice given: the date, the format and how long before. Write who agreed, or why there was no agreement. Write the rooms entered, whether the participant was home, and any key used and by whom. Write anything the participant said or asked. If the participant refused entry, record that too. Write no private detail about the participant or their belongings. For a contractor, the Tenancy Officer records the entry from the contractor's report. Each entry can be traced and checked. REG-SDA-01 col BH (entry record) The same day (our standard)

t: Enter only as far as you must to protect life or property.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Enter only as far as you must to protect life or property. A person in danger needs help before anything else. Stopping to give notice can cost a life. there is a fire, flood or gas leak, or a person may be badly hurt or very unwell, or a participant does not answer and you reasonably believe they are injured or unwell inside The person who is there If a person is in danger, call 000 first. Stay on the line and follow the operator. Let the emergency service go in first if you can. If you reasonably believe the participant is injured or unwell inside and cannot answer, call 000, then use the sealed emergency key or ask the emergency operator what to do; do not wait for the ambulance if the operator tells you to go in. Do not search or move the participant's belongings. Phone the SDA Manager at once. The SDA Manager tells the participant what happened and why, in their format, and offers a talk with someone they trust. Complete FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form if anyone was harmed or at risk. PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure then applies, and the Quality Manager decides whether the incident is reportable. The person is safe, and the participant knows why we came in. REG-SDA-01 col BH (entry record); FRM-INC-01 Straight away. Tell the participant within 24 hours (our standard)

t: Respond as Decision table 2 sets out.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Respond as Decision table 2 sets out. a participant tells you or shows you they want privacy, a visitor, a partner, information about relationships or sex, or help with an intimate matter The worker, Tenancy Officer or SDA Manager the participant tells Listen. Stay calm and kind. Do not ask why. Do not judge, joke or give your own views. Do not tell anyone, including family, other residents or other providers, without the participant's consent. Write nothing about their private life. Where they want a change, write down a request at step 15 and tell the SDA Manager the same day. The participant is heard without judgement, and knows what happens next. FRM-SDA-01 Q6, where the participant asks for a change. Otherwise none At the time. Tell the SDA Manager the same day where Decision table 2 says so (our standard)

t: Keep what you learn about a participant private.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Keep what you learn about a participant private. Every worker, agent and contractor Share information about a participant's health, relationships, intimate life, requests and home only with a person the participant has agreed to. The other exception is where the law requires it. Family, supporters, other residents, other providers and owners do not get information because they ask. Never put a participant's name or private details on a notice, on another resident's file or in a group message. Never place or use a camera, a listening device or a tracker in a bedroom, bathroom or toilet. A device in a shared area needs each resident's agreement under POL-TEC-02 Surveillance and Monitoring Technology Policy. Photos and recordings need FRM-RGT-03 Photo, Video and Audio Recording Consent Form. If you share something by mistake, tell the SDA Manager the same day. PRO-INF-02 Privacy and Data Breach Response Procedure then applies. Nobody learns a participant's private matters unless the participant agrees. FRM-INF-01 (the participant's consent, where it was asked) Always (our standard)

t: Write down the request as the participant makes it.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Write down the request as the participant makes it. The worker who hears the request A request counts however it arrives: in words, signs, pictures, behaviour, a message, or through a supporter or another provider with the participant's agreement. A need a worker sees, or one that comes up at a check, also starts a request. Complete Section A of FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling Modification and Adjustment Request in the participant's own words. Do not tidy them up. Ask only what the change needs to do. Do not ask for a diagnosis or for why they want it. Give Section A to the Tenancy Officer, who enters it in REG-SDA-01 col BB to BG (modification record) and gets the request number. A repair is not a request. Report a repair under PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure. Never say or hint that a request puts a home at risk. The request is on record as the participant made it, and the clock has started. FRM-SDA-01 Q1 to Q8 The same day the request is made (our standard)

t: Put an interim arrangement in place.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Put an interim arrangement in place. anyone is at risk of harm while the request is decided The SDA Manager Agree it with the participant. Choose the smallest step that makes people safe, such as moving an item, a temporary ramp, or a worker beside them for a task. Never remove a right to make a home safe. Review the arrangement every 20 business days until the decision. If harm has already happened, complete FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form. Nobody is left at risk while the request is decided. FRM-SDA-01 Q9; REG-INC-01 The same day the risk is known (our standard)

t: Acknowledge the request and agree how the participant wants to take part.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Acknowledge the request and agree how the participant wants to take part. The Tenancy Officer Use the participant's format. Tell them who will decide, and the date they will hear the decision, which is within 20 business days. Ask who they want involved, and record their consent on FRM-INF-01. Ask whether anyone holds legal authority for this kind of decision. Read the order or instrument yourself, and check it covers this decision. The participant still takes part. Offer an independent advocate. If their FRM-RGT-01 is more than 12 months old, update it first (step 1). Look at Decision table 3, row 1. If the request fits it, agree it with the participant now and go to step 21. The participant knows who decides, by when, and how they will take part. FRM-SDA-01 Q10 to Q13 Within 2 business days of the request (our standard)

t: Assess the request with the participant at the dwelling.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Assess the request with the participant at the dwelling. The SDA Manager Go to the dwelling, with the participant's agreement. Ask what the change needs to do. Look for other ways to meet the need, and ask what the participant thinks of each. Get advice where you need it, for example from an occupational therapist, a builder, a building surveyor or an accredited SDA assessor. Get the participant's consent before you share their information. Weigh the risk of making the change against the risk of leaving things as they are. Rate a risk on FRM-RSK-01 Risk Assessment Form where needed. The need, the options and the participant's views are on record. FRM-SDA-01 Q14 to Q17 Within 10 business days of the request (our standard)

t: Check what the change needs before it can go ahead.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Check what the change needs before it can go ahead. The SDA Manager Approvals: where the owner must agree, ask the owner in writing. Also check owners corporation, planning, building and tenancy law consent. Cost: we pay for repairs, upkeep and every feature the enrolled design category needs. Never charge the participant for them. Agree any cost to the participant in writing, and only with their agreement. Before a participant applies for NDIS funding for a modification to an enrolled dwelling, ask the NDIA how it affects the enrolment. The NDIA does not usually fund home modifications in an enrolled SDA dwelling; plan for us to pay. Enrolment: check whether the change could alter the design category, building type or suitability. Also check whether it adds a resident above the enrolled number. If it could, ask an accredited SDA assessor and go to step 24. You know which approvals, funding and enrolment limits apply. FRM-SDA-01 Q18 to Q20 Ask the owner within 5 business days of the request. Finish within 10 business days of the request (our standard)

t: Ask each resident affected, in their own format, before the decision.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Ask each resident affected, in their own format, before the decision. the change affects a shared area or another resident The SDA Manager Ask each resident separately and in private what they think, and what the change would mean for them. Write no resident's name on the form. Keep each answer on that resident's own file. A resident may choose not to say. An objection alone is not a reason to refuse. Look for a design, a time or a place that works for both. Other residents' views are known and weighed, and nobody is surprised. FRM-SDA-01 Q21 to Q23 Before the decision, and within 12 business days of the request (our standard)

t: Decide the request using Decision table 3, and write the reasons.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Decide the request using Decision table 3, and write the reasons. The SDA Manager, or the Tenancy Officer for an adjustment agreed on the day Decide with the participant's views and the advice in front of you. Write the reasons in plain words. For any answer but "agreed on the day" or "approved in full", give the Decision table 3 row, the evidence and the other way offered. Agree with the participant what happens to the change when the tenancy ends. The Tenancy Officer may agree a simple adjustment on the day. Three answers go to step 22 before the participant is told: approved in part, not approved, and the need cannot be met in this dwelling. The request has a decision, reasons the participant can test and a named decision maker. FRM-SDA-01 Q24 to Q27 Within 15 business days of the request. The same day for an adjustment agreed on the day (our standard)

t: Review the decision before the participant is told.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Review the decision before the participant is told. the decision is "approved in part", "not approved" or "the need cannot be met in this dwelling" The Chief Executive, or the independent contact in a small provider Read the participant's own words, the reasons and the other ways offered. Ask whether every other way was tried and whether the participant was heard. Ask whether an objection was treated as a veto. Ask whether the ground in Decision table 3 is real. Confirm, change or reverse the decision. The reviewer is never the person who decided. No refusal reaches a participant without a second, independent look. FRM-SDA-01 Q26 Within 3 business days of the decision (our standard)

t: Explain the decision, the reasons and the participant's options, in their format.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Explain the decision, the reasons and the participant's options, in their format. The Tenancy Officer Explain in person where you can. Check understanding by asking them to say or show it back, as at step 3. Tell them every option, whatever the decision. They can ask the Chief Executive for another look. They can use our complaints process under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. They can phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544, or ask an independent advocate to help. They can go to the tribunal or anti-discrimination body of [state or territory], or to the Australian Human Rights Commission. Give a written copy in their format. Do not make a signature a condition of anything. Remind them that asking for a change, or complaining, never puts their home at risk. The participant understands the decision and knows how to challenge it. FRM-SDA-01 Q28 and Q29; REG-RGT-01 Within 2 business days of the decision being final, and within 20 business days of the request (our standard)

t: Tell the NDIA in writing.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Tell the NDIA in writing. the dwelling's design category, building type or suitability is changing or likely to change, or the dwelling is no longer suitable (FRM-SDA-01 Q20) The SDA Manager Say what has happened, the date the circumstances arose, and which dwelling. Use the way the NDIA tells providers to notify, through PRO-SDA-01 step 25, which owns the notices for SDA Rules 2020 section 29(1)(a) to (d). Keep a copy. The 5 business days run from the day the event occurs. That can be before the decision is made. If you are unsure whether the event has happened, ask the NDIA early. The NDIA knows inside the statutory time. FRM-SDA-01 Q30 Within 5 business days of the event occurring (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2))

t: Start the conversation with the participant about where their need can be met.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Start the conversation with the participant about where their need can be met. the decision is "the need cannot be met in this dwelling" The SDA Manager Tell the participant first, in their format, with an advocate or supporter if they want one. This form never ends a tenancy. The participant chooses what happens next. Offer to tell their support coordinator and support providers, and do so only with their consent. Give them time. Offer to look at other ways to meet the need and at other homes. For any tenancy matter, follow PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation). If the participant gives notice to leave, or is given a notice to vacate, the NDIA must be told under PRO-SDA-05 step 2. The limit is 5 business days (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(1)(e) and (2)). The participant, and anyone they choose, hears early and decides what happens next. FRM-SDA-01 Q31 Within 2 business days of the decision being final (our standard)

t: Agree the work with the participant and each resident affected.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Agree the work with the participant and each resident affected. the decision includes work The Tenancy Officer Agree the start date with the participant. Give entry notice to each resident affected, as at step 9. Choose a licensed contractor where the trade needs one, and brief them at step 6. Confirm the approvals from step 19 are in hand. No work starts without them. Agree with the participant how the days of work will run, including privacy, noise and access. Work starts only with approvals, the participant's agreement and a briefed contractor. FRM-SDA-01 Q32 and Q33; REG-HRM-03 Before work starts (our standard)

t: Walk the finished change with the participant and ask whether it works.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Walk the finished change with the participant and ask whether it works. The SDA Manager Check at the dwelling that the work is finished as agreed and is safe. Get any certificate the law requires. Walk it with the participant where they agree. Ask in their own way whether it does what they needed. Write down yes, partly or no, and what else is needed. Fix any defect. If the answer is partly or no, start a new request at step 15 and tell the participant. The change is finished and checked, and the participant has said whether it works. FRM-SDA-01 Q34 and Q35 Within 5 business days of the change being in place (our standard)

t: Update the records and close the request.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Update the records and close the request. The SDA Manager Update the dwelling's record in REG-SDA-01 col BB to BG (modification record). Update AGR-SDA-01 where a term changed. Update the participant's emergency plan, FRM-SUP-07 Participant Emergency and Disaster Plan, where an exit or alarm changed. Tell support providers only with the participant's consent. Do not close the request while question 35 says partly or no, unless a new request is open. Every record agrees with the home as it now is. FRM-SDA-01 Q36 and Q37 Within 5 business days of the walk-through at step 27 (our standard)

t: Report the concern to the SDA Manager.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Report the concern to the SDA Manager. Any worker, contractor or other person who sees, hears or is told that a participant's rights are not respected A participant can tell anyone, in any way. If the concern is about the SDA Manager, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, tell the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01. You can always phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. Whoever receives the concern records it on FRM-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Form and follows PRO-FBK-01. If a participant was harmed or put at risk, also complete FRM-INC-01. Offer the participant an advocate. Nobody is treated worse for raising a concern: POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy applies. The concern is on record and moving. FRM-FBK-01; REG-FBK-01 The same day. PRO-FBK-01 sets the complaint times (our standard)

t: Review the rights records and report what they show.
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Review the rights records and report what they show. The Quality Manager Read the request and entry records in REG-SDA-01, REG-RGT-01, REG-FBK-01, REG-INC-01 and REG-HRM-02 for this topic. Count the requests by kind, and the days from request to decision. Count the refusals and what the review decided. Count the entries made without notice or agreement, and the entries a participant refused. Count the complaints about rights. Count the participants not asked about their rights in 12 months, and the workers and contractors briefed late. Read a sample of the step 8 conversations for what participants said about feeling respected at home; do not interview them again for this report. Enter each fix in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date. Report to the governing body. In a small provider where one person holds the Quality Manager role, the independent contact reads the report. Gaps are found, fixed and reported before an auditor finds them. REG-QMS-01 Every 3 months (our standard)

t: Decision table 1: entering a participant's home (steps 9 to 12). Entry is allowed only on
w: Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Decision table 1: entering a participant's home (steps 9 to 12). Entry is allowed only on these terms. If Then A planned visit for an inspection, repair, work or a check Give notice at step 9. Go in only with the participant's agreement, or where tenancy law of [state or territory] allows entry with that notice for that reason The participant is home and says no, or asks you to wait Do not go in. Leave if asked. Tell the SDA Manager the same day, who offers another time. Never use a key or force The participant is not home Go in only if the notice said you would and tenancy law of [state or territory] allows entry in their absence for that reason. Never go into their bedroom alone unless the notice named it and the participant agreed in writing You need to go into the participant's bedroom Ask each time, even where the notice named the room. Let them stay in the room or choose who comes in. Do not open drawers, cupboards or devices Work is needed in a shared area and a resident objects Do not go into that resident's room. Work only in the shared area. Ask the SDA Manager the same day Someone needs to see the home, such as a person who may move in, a valuer or a buyer Treat it as a planned entry. Ask the participant whether they want to be there. Show their bedroom only if they agree Another NDIS provider arrives to support the participant Do not stop them or ask them to sign in (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 37; SDA Conditions Rule 2018, section 10(2)(b)). The participant decides who comes into their own room A participant has a visitor or an overnight guest Do not sign them in, ask who they are or ask for identification. Visitors are the participant's choice within their agreement and tenancy law (PRO-ENV-02 Visitors Procedure) There is a fire, flood, gas leak or a person in danger Go to step 12 You are worried about a participant's welfare but see no danger Phone the participant. Phone the contact they chose, if they have given consent. If you think they may be badly hurt or very unwell inside and cannot answer, call 000 and go to step 12 A key to the participant's home or room is needed The participant decides who holds keys and codes to their home and room. Where a SIL provider works in the dwelling this is recorded at AGR-SDA-02 Q18; otherwise on the participant's file. Where the participant cannot decide, their decision maker's consent counts, and the participant still takes part. We hold a sealed emergency key for every dwelling, used only at step 12, and we record each use at step 11 Decision table 2: privacy, relationships, intimacy and sexual expression (step 13). If Then A participant asks for more privacy, such as a lock, a sign or more notice before entry Do not ask why. Say they can ask for it, and offer to write the request down now (step 15). Tell the SDA Manager the same day A participant wants a partner, friend or family member to visit or stay the night That is their choice within their agreement and tenancy law of [state or territory]. Do not ask who, why or how long. Do not sign anyone in. Tell the SDA Manager the same day if the agreement, another resident or a worker seems to stand in the way A participant wants a partner or another person to live with them Write down a request (step 15) as "a change to a house rule or to who lives in the dwelling". The person counts toward the number of residents the dwelling is enrolled for (SDA Conditions Rule 2018, section 11(a)). If they would share a bedroom, help the participant tell the NDIA in writing; the NDIA must be satisfied the participant's needs are not harmed (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(d) and (e)). If the dwelling's suitability or occupancy changes, go to step 24. Tell the SDA Manager the same day A participant asks for information about relationships, sex or sexual health Give plain facts in their format, or help them find a trusted source: their doctor, a sexual health service or an advocate. Do not give your own opinion A participant asks for help that involves their body or personal care That is a support, not a housing matter. Tell the SDA Manager the same day. With the participant's consent, the SDA Manager tells their support provider or support coordinator A participant asks a worker for sexual contact or a sexual service Say no, kindly and clearly, and do not shame them. No worker takes part in sexual activity with a participant: it is sexual misconduct, and we must take all reasonable steps to prevent and respond to it (statutory: Code of Conduct Rules 2018, section 6(1)(g)). Tell the SDA Manager the same day. The SDA Manager talks with the participant in private within 2 business days about what we can support, and offers independent advice. If sexual activity between a worker and a participant has occurred, follow PRO-SGD-01, complete FRM-INC-01, and the Quality Manager notifies the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware (Incident Rules 2018, section 20) You believe an adult participant who can consent may be pressured or harmed in a relationship Call 000 if anyone is in danger. Do not stop the relationship, search a room or question the people. Tell the SDA Manager at once. The SDA Manager talks with the participant in private within 2 business days, offers an independent advocate and, with the participant's consent, asks their behaviour support practitioner or their decision maker what would help. Follow PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure and complete FRM-INC-01 if harm is alleged. The concern is about safety, not about the relationship One of the people is under 18, or you believe a participant cannot consent to the sexual contact Stop the contact if it is safe to do so, and keep everyone safe. Call 000 or the police where anyone is in danger or an offence may have occurred. Do not disturb the scene or question the people. Phone the SDA Manager at once, who tells the Quality Manager the same day. Follow PRO-SGD-01 and complete FRM-INC-01. The Quality Manager treats it as a reportable incident (unlawful sexual contact: Incident Rules 2018, section 20), notifies the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware, and checks whether a mandatory report to the police or the child protection authority of [state or territory] is required Another resident complains about a participant's visitor, partner or noise Do not tell the participant who complained and do not ask them to stop. Tell the SDA Manager the same day. The SDA Manager hears each person in private and looks for a time or place that works for both A family member, supporter or guardian asks about, or wants to limit, the participant's relationship or visitors Tell them nothing. Say the SDA Manager will talk with the participant. The SDA Manager reads any order to see what it covers, and asks the participant what they want shared A worker jokes about, judges or comments on a participant's relationships or body Say it is not acceptable, and report it to the SDA Manager the same day (step 29). It may breach the Code of Conduct (Rules 2018, section 6(1)(a) and (b)) Decision table 3: deciding a request (step 21). More than one row can apply. Follow every row that does. If Then Who decides The change costs nothing, alters no building or fixture, affects no other resident and breaks no law, such as a different way to give notice or a different time for visits Agree it on the day. Record it as "agreed on the day" and tell the participant the same day The Tenancy Officer The change meets the need, is lawful and safe, and the approvals are in hand Approve in full The SDA Manager Part of the change can go ahead and part cannot Approve the part that can. t: Dwelling Modification and Adjustment Request
Use this form each time a participant wants something about their specialist disability ac
x: Use this form each time a participant wants something about their specialist disability accommodation dwelling changed. It follows one request from the day it is made to the day the participant says the change works. A modification is a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice, enter the home or communicate. A request about who visits or lives in the dwelling is recorded here too. Who completes it: the worker who hears the request starts Section A the same day. The Tenancy Officer completes Section B. The SDA Manager completes Sections C to F. The participant never has to fill in a form to be heard. Start a form when: a participant asks, in words, signs, pictures or behaviour a supporter or another provider asks, and the participant agrees a worker sees a need, or a need comes up at a dwelling check or the yearly rights check a participant's needs or circumstances change. Have ready: the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, and the dwelling's row in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register. A simple adjustment can be agreed on the day. It costs nothing, changes no building or fixture, affects no other resident and breaks no law. For one, complete Sections A and B, then question 24 (write "agreed on the day"), question 28 (the date and how the participant was told) and questions 35 to 37. Skip every other question. The form is for modifications, and for any request that is refused, approved in part or affects another resident. What happens next: the participant is told the decision within 20 business days of the request. PRO-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) sets every step. A repair is not a request under this form. Report a repair under PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure. This form never ends a tenancy and authorises no restrictive practice. When to use which questions: Adjustment agreed on the day: Sections A and B; question 24; question 28; questions 35 to 37. Modification, or an adjustment that needs assessment: every question in Sections A to F. Request refused, approved in part, or affecting a shared area or another resident: every question in Sections A to F, including Section D and the review at question 26. Request the dwelling cannot meet: every question, and question 31. An adjustment agreed on the day is also written as a one-line modification record in REG-SDA-01 (request number, date, participant, what was agreed, date told, records updated).

t: We collect this information to decide the request and to make the change safely. The SDA M
x: We collect this information to decide the request and to make the change safely. The SDA Manager, the Tenancy Officer, the Chief Executive and the Quality Manager see it. An adviser or contractor sees only what they need, and only with the participant's consent. An auditor sees it only to check our work. The participant does not have to give a diagnosis. We ask what the change needs to do, not why the participant's body or mind works as it does. We never ask a participant to explain a wish for privacy, a visitor or a relationship. We keep the form on the participant's file. We write no other resident's name or personal details on it. Each resident's view is kept on that resident's own file. The participant can see this form and ask us to correct it. They use FRM-INF-02 Request to Access or Correct Personal Information Form, or they ask any worker. Asking for a change never puts a participant's home at risk.

t: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
The result: every participant in a specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwelling know
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: The result: every participant in a specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwelling knows, before they choose, what interests we hold. They know their home and their supports are separate. They know their home does not depend on the supports they choose. We record each of these things and keep them true. This procedure gives effect to the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) as it applies to SDA, and to POL-SDA-01 Specialist Disability Accommodation Policy, C2.

t: Use this procedure for every participant who lives in, or is offered a place in, a dwellin
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Use this procedure for every participant who lives in, or is offered a place in, a dwelling that [Provider name] enrols or manages as SDA. These terms are used here: An interest is anything that gives us, a related business, a worker or a worker's relative a gain. It is also anything that gives a reason to prefer one option. A conflict is an interest that affects a decision now (actual) or could affect one later (potential). It is also an interest that could look, to a reasonable person, as if it affects one (perceived). We manage all three. A related business is a business that we, our owners or directors, or a worker's relative own, run or share profit with. A tenancy action is a notice to vacate, a breach notice, any rent or board increase or a room move. It is also a change to the agreement or house rules for one participant. A tenure check is the check at step 23 that a tenancy action does not rest on a support decision or a concern. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. Start at When Step 1 A person enquires about a place, or a participant is offered a support from us or a related business. When we adopt this procedure, start here for each current participant within 6 months, beginning with participants who take any support from us or a related business Step 2 Anyone finds an interest that is not in REG-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Register Step 17 One of the triggers in Decision table 3 happens Step 18 A participant changes, ends or declines a support or a provider Step 19 A provider the participant chose asks to come to the dwelling Step 22 A tenancy action is planned Step 24 A participant says they feel pushed, or you see a link between supports and housing Who acts: The Tenancy Officer meets participants, explains and records. The SDA Manager owns this procedure, writes our statement of interests, runs the checks and reports. The Chief Executive decides how our interests are managed and decides each tenure check. Every worker, manager and director follows steps 2, 4 and 24. A worker who hears that a participant has changed a support tells the Tenancy Officer the same day. In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds all of them. A sole trader still needs a second person for three things. These are deciding the sole trader's own interests (step 3), the tenure check (step 23) and hearing a concern about the sole trader (step 24). REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register names that person as [independent contact for concerns]. If we also give the participant support coordination or plan management, follow PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure as well.

w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: You can open REG-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Register and REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register. You have the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form. You have STA-GOV-01 Conflict of Interest: Plain Summary in the participant's format. You have AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement and any support agreement as separate documents. You know the contacts to give: [complaints contact], [independent contact for concerns], [advocacy service] and [tenancy advice service]. You know the NDIS Commission number, 1800 035 544, and the on-call number: [on-call number]. You have read POL-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Policy and POL-SDA-01 Specialist Disability Accommodation Policy. REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register shows you have done the training for this procedure under PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure.

t: A home offered on condition of supports. "You can have this room if you use our supports"
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: A home offered on condition of supports. "You can have this room if you use our supports" takes away the participant's choice. It breaks the standard, and the participant may feel unable to say no. A vacancy filled for the support income. A place given for the supports a person will buy, and not for their needs, harms that person and their housemates. A tenancy action after a support choice. A notice, rent change, room move or slow repair soon after a participant changes provider looks like punishment. The participant can lose their home. Telling after the choice. A disclosure made once the participant has decided is too late. They chose without the facts. A signature taken for understanding. A signed record does not show that the participant knows who provides their home and who provides their supports. A worker who steers. A hint, a favour or praise for one provider limits the participant's choice. The participant may not notice it is happening. A provider kept out. Delaying or refusing a provider the participant chose limits their choice. It breaks a condition of our registration. A decision by the person with the interest. A conflict managed by the person who holds it is not managed.

t: Offer or accept no gift, fee, discount or other benefit tied to a participant's choice.
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Offer or accept no gift, fee, discount or other benefit tied to a participant's choice. Every worker, manager and director This covers a rent reduction, a free item, a voucher, cash, an upgrade and a payment for a referral. It covers what we give a participant, a family member, a support coordinator or another provider. It also covers what any of them offers us. Refuse the offer and tell the SDA Manager the same day. Integrity, honesty and transparency are a Code of Conduct duty (Code of Conduct Rules, section 6(1)(d)). Declare any other gift on FRM-GOV-01. Never accept money or a loan from a participant. Never borrow from them or sell to them. Never take a place in their will, or act as their attorney, nominee, guardian or administrator. A gift from a participant worth more than the amount the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) sets ($[set at adoption]) is declared, and the Chief Executive decides what happens to it. Nobody's choice of home or supports has been bought, and every offer is on record. FRM-GOV-01 Q11; REG-GOV-02 (gifts and benefits) At the time of the offer. t: Find out how the participant wants to be told, and who they want with them.

Ask who they want at the meeting: an advocate, a family member, a support coordinator or nobody. A person from us or from a related business is never the advocate. Book an interpreter through TIS National on 131 450, or use the National Relay Service, when needed. Check the authority of anyone who decides for the participant. The participant still takes part. The meeting is set up in the participant's way, with the people they chose. FRM-SDA-02 Q5 to Q7 Before the meeting, and in time for the policy to reach the participant 3 business days before they are asked to sign (our standard)

t: Write our statement of interests for this participant.
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Write our statement of interests for this participant. A statement that leaves out an interest is not a disclosure. The participant then chooses without the facts. The SDA Manager Use the rows listed at step 1. Cover who owns the dwelling and who is the landlord. Cover every other support we or a related business give or offer, and what we gain either way. Cover any referral arrangement or benefit, and any worker who has declared an interest. Decision table 2 shows what to say in each situation. Write it in plain words, in the participant's format. When we hold no other interest, say so. The Tenancy Officer has a statement the participant can follow, with nothing left out. FRM-SDA-02 Q8 to Q12 Before the meeting (our standard)

t: Give the participant our conflict of interest policy, or explain it.
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Give the participant our conflict of interest policy, or explain it. The Tenancy Officer Give STA-GOV-01 in the format from step 5. Offer POL-GOV-02 in full. Read it aloud if the participant wants. Write the version you used. Do not ask the participant to sign anything yet. The participant has our policy in a form they can use. FRM-SDA-02 Q13 At least 3 business days before the participant is asked to sign the SDA service agreement. The participant may ask for less, in their own words. For a current participant, before the review meeting (our standard)

t: Tell the participant about each interest we hold.
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Tell the participant about each interest we hold. The Tenancy Officer Use the statement from step 6, in the participant's own format. Stop after each interest and ask if they have questions. A worker who has declared an interest in this participant's choices takes no part. Write down what you said. The participant knows every interest we hold before they decide anything. FRM-SDA-02 Q14 Before the participant makes any choice about their home or supports, and 3 business days before they are asked to sign (our standard)

t: Explain the difference between the home and the supports.
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Explain the difference between the home and the supports. The Tenancy Officer SDA is the home. It does not include the supports given in it (SDA Rules 2020, section 5). Say who provides the home and who provides each support. Say that each has its own agreement and that the participant can change one without the other. Ask the participant to say or show you back three things. Who provides their home? Who provides their supports? What happens to their home if they change a support provider? If they cannot, explain again another way. A signature is not proof of understanding. The participant can say which is their home and which are their supports. FRM-SDA-02 Q15 to Q17 At the same meeting as step 8 (our standard)

t: Tell the participant that their home does not depend on the supports they choose.
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Tell the participant that their home does not depend on the supports they choose. The Tenancy Officer Say it in plain words. "You keep your home whatever you decide about your supports. Nobody can end your tenancy because of that." Add that the same is true if they complain. Say that neither agreement is a condition of the other. Ask what they heard. Write the words you used and their answer. The duty rests on Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 4 and Quality Indicators Guidelines, section 69(4). The participant knows their home is safe from their support choices. FRM-SDA-02 Q18 At the same meeting as step 8, and again at each review (our standard)

t: Tell the participant about their choice of provider and the options open to them.
w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)

This includes plan management and support coordination. Say how to change: they tell any worker, in any way, and we help with the handover. Say that any provider they choose can come to their home with no fee. Apart from the safety rules every visitor follows, we set no condition on their work. Do not recommend one provider over another. Where we offer a support, also name at least 3 other providers of it in the area, or the NDIS Provider Finder. Use the participant's format. Where fewer than 3 exist, write how many. The participant knows they can say no to us, and has somewhere to look. FRM-SDA-02 Q19 and Q20 At the same meeting as step 8 (our standard)

t: Offer the participant independent help and a way to raise a concern.

None may be run by us or a related business. Write the contacts in the participant's format. Offer to book the first visit, and do not stay in the room unless asked. Give [complaints contact], [independent contact for concerns] and the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. Say that nobody will treat them worse for raising a concern. Someone who holds no interest in the matter manages it. The participant has an independent route to advice and a way to raise a concern. FRM-SDA-02 Q21 and Q22 At the same meeting as step 8 (our standard)

w: Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)

Ask how they want to acknowledge the record: sign, say it aloud, or decline to sign. Not signing never changes their home or supports. The participant's own choice and words are on record. FRM-SDA-02 Q23 to Q26 At the meeting, before you leave or end the call (our standard)

t: Check that the agreements are separate and that the offer of the place has no support cond

The SDA Manager Read the SDA service agreement and the offer letter. Read any support agreement we offer: AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template. Set the next review date, no more than 12 months away. Link any complaint or other record. Each change is a new version with your name and the reason. t: specialist disability accommodation (SDA): a home for a person with extreme functional imp
w: Service Agreements with Participants Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: specialist disability accommodation (SDA): a home for a person with extreme functional impairment or very high support needs. It does not include the supports the person gets while they live there. enrolled dwelling: a dwelling the NDIA has enrolled so that SDA can be provided in it. agreement: the completed AGR-SDA-01 for one participant and one dwelling, with every change to it. proposed agreement: an agreement we worked out with the participant and gave them a copy of, before they have signed it. tenancy law: the residential tenancy law of [state or territory] that applies to the dwelling. rent: what the participant pays to live in the dwelling. reasonable rent contribution: the part of the rent a participant is expected to pay, as the NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation (current year) set it: currently 25 per cent of the basic Disability Support Pension plus 100 per cent of any Commonwealth Rent Assistance. The rent limit is the SDA amount in the participant's plan plus this contribution. bond: money held as security against unpaid rent or damage. It may be nothing. board: a payment, if the participant chooses it, for things we agree to provide, such as food or household costs. agent: a person or business that acts for us on a dwelling, such as a property manager. NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency. NDIA addendum: the addendum to the NDIA's Terms of Business for Registered Providers that lists the terms an SDA agreement must include. decision maker: a person with legal authority to decide for the participant, such as a guardian, a financial administrator, an attorney or a nominee. risk of harm: a real and present chance that the participant or another person will be seriously hurt. We show it with facts, and never with a diagnosis or a label. supported independent living (SIL) provider: a provider who gives a participant help with, or supervision of, daily tasks in their home. tenure check: the Chief Executive's decision, before a notice goes out, on whether anything links it to the participant's support decisions or concerns. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. SDA Rules 2020, SDA Conditions Rule: short names for the instruments in Authority. SDA Manager: the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. Tenancy Officer: the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.

Steps 25 to 27 prepare the notice. PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) steps 24 to 27 serve it. A participant gives us notice that they are leaving: PRO-SDA-05 step 28 ends the tenancy. Then do step 28 here. Who acts: The Tenancy Officer prepares the agreement, explains it, gives the copy and keeps the records. The SDA Manager checks every draft, decides changes, signs for us, tells the NDIA and decides whether we may end an agreement. The Chief Executive decides whether to charge rent above the limit and approves every notice to end an agreement. The Quality Manager samples the records every 3 months. Every worker tells the Tenancy Officer within 1 business day when a participant asks about, or wants to change, their agreement. If an agent does the Tenancy Officer's work, the agent follows this procedure. [Provider name] stays responsible, and the SDA Manager checks the agent's work at step 10. In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader still needs a second person for steps 6, 10, 25 (the tenure check at PRO-SDA-03 step 23) and 26, and for the approval of any notice to end an agreement at PRO-SDA-05 step 24. REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register names that person as [independent contact for concerns]. A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. The agreement is the completed AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement for one participant and one dwelling, with every change. A proposed agreement is an agreement we have worked out with the participant and given them a copy of, before they have signed it. Short names used here: SDA Rules 2020: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020 SDA Conditions Rule: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018 NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency NDIS Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission

w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)

t: Open an agreement record for the participant and the dwelling.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Open an agreement record for the participant and the dwelling. The Tenancy Officer Open it when the participant accepts a place, or when you find a participant living in a dwelling with no agreement. Copy the dwelling details from its row in REG-SDA-01. Check the number of residents it is enrolled for. Check the participant's plan includes SDA funding, and write the date you saw it. Complete the first questions of AGR-SDA-01. One agreement record exists for this participant and this dwelling. AGR-SDA-01 Q1 to Q2; REG-SDA-02 Within 2 business days of the participant accepting the place (our standard)

t: Ask the participant how they want to take part.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Ask the participant how they want to take part. The Tenancy Officer Ask which language, way of communicating and format they want, and who they want with them. Copy the answers from FRM-RGT-01. If it is more than 12 months old, ask again. Book an interpreter, a communication partner, a supporter or an advocate if they want one. Offer to meet at the dwelling or where they choose. Every meeting about the agreement will be in the way the participant understands best. AGR-SDA-01 Q28 Before the participant sees any draft (our standard)

t: Confirm who decides about this agreement.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Confirm who decides about this agreement. A family member or carer with no legal authority cannot sign for an adult. An agreement they sign may not bind the participant. The Tenancy Officer Start from the participant deciding, with support if they want it. Ask whether anyone has legal authority to decide for them, such as a guardian, a financial administrator, an attorney or a nominee. Ask to see the document. Check it covers a housing or tenancy agreement. Write what it covers, the date you saw it and where the copy is filed. Decision table 2 says who may sign. Involve the participant whoever signs. You know who signs, and on what authority. AGR-SDA-01 Q3 Before the draft is prepared (our standard)

t: Check the law that applies to this agreement.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Check the law that applies to this agreement. The Tenancy Officer Copy the current notice rule rows for [state or territory] from REG-SDA-02 col AU (entry, rent change, breach, ending by us, ending by the participant) and the date each was checked at col AV. Copy the date the SDA Manager last checked the NDIA addendum. Ask the SDA Manager if any row or check is older than 12 months, or if you are unsure. From those rows, write each rule that gives the participant a longer period, a lower limit or an extra step. Write whether the tenancy law applies to this dwelling and, if it does, the prescribed agreement form and how this agreement sits with it, as the tenancy-law review for [state or territory] decided. The terms the NDIA addendum requires are fixed terms in AGR-SDA-01; write only the addendum version checked at Q6. The draft will meet the tenancy law and the terms the NDIA requires. AGR-SDA-01 Q4 to Q6 On the day you prepare the draft (our standard)

t: Set the rent and check it against the limit.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Set the rent and check it against the limit. Charging rent above the limit without telling the NDIA breaks a condition of enrolment. The SDA Manager Work out the rent from the income support and rent assistance figures the participant gave you. The limit is the SDA amount in the participant's plan plus the reasonable rent contribution as the NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation (current year) set it (currently 25 per cent of the basic Disability Support Pension plus 100 per cent of any Commonwealth Rent Assistance). Compare the total rent we propose to charge with that limit. Write the figures and how the rent was worked out, in plain words. If the total is above the limit, do step 6 before the draft goes to the participant. The rent is within the limit, or step 6 is under way. AGR-SDA-01 Q7 to Q8 Before the draft is prepared (our standard)

t: Decide whether to charge rent above the limit.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Decide whether to charge rent above the limit. the rent we propose is above the limit The Chief Executive Charge it only if a qualified property valuer certifies that the rent is fair and reasonable. If you agree, the SDA Manager tells the NDIA and attaches the certificate, at PRO-SDA-05 step 2. Tell the participant what you decided, in their way of communicating. If you do not agree, lower the rent to the limit and go back to step 5. A sole trader asks [independent contact for concerns]. The rent is within the limit, or the NDIA has been told and the participant knows. AGR-SDA-01 Q8 Before the draft is checked at step 10. The NDIA is told within 5 business days of proposing the rent (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2))

t: Complete the bond, board, other charges and the notice before an increase.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Complete the bond, board, other charges and the notice before an increase. The Tenancy Officer Write the bond, which may be nothing, and where it is held. Never ask for more than the tenancy law of [state or territory] allows. Write board only if the participant chose it. Write every other charge, or "none". Write the days of notice before rent or board goes up: the longer of 60 days and what the tenancy law of [state or territory] requires. Nothing is charged that is not written here. Every amount the participant will pay is written, and nothing else will be charged. AGR-SDA-01 Q11 to Q15 Before the draft is checked at step 10 (our standard)

t: Complete who the participant deals with, and how to ask for repairs.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Complete who the participant deals with, and how to ask for repairs. The Tenancy Officer If we use an agent, write the agent's name, telephone number, address and responsibilities. If not, write "no agent". Always write our address and telephone number. Write our repair contact and our urgent number. Ask the participant how they like to ask for repairs, and write it. The participant knows who to contact, and about what. AGR-SDA-01 Q16 to Q17 and Q24 Before the draft is checked at step 10 (our standard)

t: Complete the safety features, and the list of providers who need the safety information.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Complete the safety features, and the list of providers who need the safety information. The Tenancy Officer Copy the safety features from the dwelling's latest FRM-SDA-03. If an item is missing or not working, tell the SDA Manager the same day, and do not write it as working. Write the route and the meeting point for leaving the building. Ask the participant which providers deliver supported independent living in the dwelling, and write each one. PRO-SDA-05 step 14 gives each provider the information before their first shift. The agreement says so. The safety information is complete, true and ready to explain. AGR-SDA-01 Q25 and Q27 Before the draft is checked at step 10 (our standard)

t: Check the draft.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Check the draft. The SDA Manager A person who did not prepare it checks it. Check every question has an answer. Check the terms are the current AGR-SDA-01, and that nothing protecting the participant has been cut. That includes 90 days' notice, the repair times and the grounds for ending. Check the rent against its limit, the law against Q4 to Q6, and the safety features against the latest inspection. Check PRO-SDA-03 steps 7 and 8 are on track to reach the participant at least 3 business days before they are asked to sign. A sole trader asks [independent contact for concerns]. The draft is complete and correct before the participant sees it. AGR-SDA-01 Q38 Within 3 business days of the draft being complete (our standard)

t: Give the participant the draft and the plain summary, with time to think.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Give the participant the draft and the plain summary, with time to think. The Tenancy Officer Give them AGR-SDA-01 and STA-SDA-01 in their format. Add our conflict of interest policy and statement of interests. Add the tenancy information from [state or territory], how to complain, how to find an advocate and the house rules, if there are any. Tell them they can take it away, show a person they trust, and ask for changes. Offer at least 5 business days to think. They can sign sooner if they choose to. Offer no gift, discount or reward for signing. The participant has everything, in their format, and time to decide. AGR-SDA-01 Q29 and Q31 At least 5 business days before the participant is asked to sign, unless they choose to sign sooner (our standard)

t: Go through the agreement with the participant, one topic at a time.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Go through the agreement with the participant, one topic at a time. The Tenancy Officer Use the language, mode and format from step 2. Cover eight topics in this order. First, your home and your supports. Then rent and other money, who you deal with, dates and ending, repairs, safety and the way out, your rights, and your responsibilities. Ask the participant to choose how they pay rent and get receipts. Agree the start date, how long it lasts, the review date and the notice each side gives. PRO-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) steps 2 and 3 can happen at the same meeting. Stop when the participant is tired and carry on another day. Write who was there and how you explained it. The participant has heard each topic in a way they can follow, and has made their own choices. AGR-SDA-01 Q9 to Q10, Q18 to Q23, Q26 and Q30 Within 10 business days of step 11, or later if the participant asks (our standard)

t: Ask the participant to say or show back what the main terms mean.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Ask the participant to say or show back what the main terms mean. A signature does not show that someone understood. A participant who signs without understanding can lose rights they did not know they had. The Tenancy Officer Ask five things. What will you pay, and when? How much notice would you get if we asked you to leave? How do you ask for a repair? What do you do if there is a fire? Who can help you if you are unhappy? Write what they said or showed, in their words. If they cannot answer, explain it another way and try again at another meeting. This is not a test. Write anything still to explain, with a date. You know what the participant understands, and what is still to explain. AGR-SDA-01 Q32 At the end of the last meeting, and before step 15 (our standard)

t: Decide each change the participant asks for.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Decide each change the participant asks for. The SDA Manager Agree to a change that is better for the participant, or neutral, unless the law stops it. Do not agree to a term that is worse for the participant than the standard terms, unless the law requires it. The standard terms include 90 days' notice, the grounds for ending, the repair times and rent within the limit. Tell the participant the answer and the reason in their way of communicating. Make each agreed change as a new version of the draft. If you cannot agree, offer another way and an advocate. Every change asked for has an answer and a reason. AGR-SDA-01 Q33 Within 5 business days of the change being asked (our standard)

t: Ask the participant to sign.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Ask the participant to sign. A participant who signs under pressure may not have understood or agreed. The agreement may not stand, and the participant may lose trust in us. The Tenancy Officer Check Q3 and Decision table 2 for who signs. Check every question is answered and nothing is blank. Check PRO-SDA-03 step 7 and step 8 were done at least 3 business days ago, unless the participant asked for less in their own words. Let the participant sign in their own way, such as a signature, a mark or an electronic signature. Tell them they can wait. A supporter or advocate may sit with them but does not sign for them. If they do not want to sign yet, write why in their words and go to step 18. The participant signs by choice, or chooses to wait. AGR-SDA-01 Q34 After step 13, and at least 5 business days after step 11 unless the participant chooses sooner (our standard)

t: Sign for [Provider name].
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Sign for [Provider name]. The SDA Manager Sign as the person named in REG-GOV-01. An agent signs only if the agent holds that authority in writing. The agreement is signed by both of us. AGR-SDA-01 Q35 Within 1 business day of the participant signing (our standard)

t: Give the participant a copy signed by both of us.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Give the participant a copy signed by both of us. The Tenancy Officer Give it in the participant's format, with the plain summary. Use paper, large print, email, a read-aloud recording or pictures, as they choose. If the participant would rather not keep a copy at home, keep it safe for them and give it whenever they ask. If you cannot give the copy, write the circumstances on the same day. Offer it again within 5 business days and at each review until they have it. The participant has their copy, or the reason they do not is written down. AGR-SDA-01 Q37 Within 2 business days of the last signature (our standard)

t: Provide the dwelling under the proposed agreement.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Provide the dwelling under the proposed agreement. the participant has not signed The SDA Manager Check the participant holds a copy of the proposed agreement. Check we worked it out with them at steps 11 to 14. Check we will provide the dwelling exactly as it says. This is the second way SDA may lawfully be provided (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1)(b)). Write the participant's reason in their words, the date SDA began and the date you will talk with them again. Talk with them again within 10 business days. Not signing is not a reason to end the agreement or to take their home. The participant has a copy and their home does not wait for a signature. AGR-SDA-01 Q36 Before we provide the dwelling (statutory: SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1))

t: Make sure the agreement is in the participant's tenancy row in REG-SDA-02.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Make sure the agreement is in the participant's tenancy row in REG-SDA-02. t: Practise leaving the building with the participant.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Practise leaving the building with the participant. A participant who has not practised leaving may not get out in a fire. A smoke alarm that is covered or disabled may not warn them. The Tenancy Officer Walk the route to the meeting point with them, in their way of communicating. Show them each smoke alarm. Tell them never to cover or disable one. Use what they need to get out, such as a flashing alarm, equipment or help from a person. Where the participant needs help from a person to get out, the SIL provider's worker is present and takes part, and the practice date is also recorded at AGR-SDA-02 Q13. With their consent, link it to their FRM-SUP-07 Participant Emergency and Disaster Plan. Write what happened. Tell the SDA Manager the same day about anything that does not work. The participant has practised getting out, and anything that does not work is being fixed. AGR-SDA-01 Q26 Within 5 business days of the participant moving in, and after any change to the safety features (our standard)

AGR-SDA-01 Q27; REG-SDA-02 col AB Within 5 business days of the change (our standard)

t: Tell the participant in writing about a change to our agent or our details.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Tell the participant in writing about a change to our agent or our details. If the tenancy law of [state or territory] sets a different period, use it. Change the answer as a new version and give the participant the changed copy.
