The notice period is right before the notice goes out. AGR-SDA-01 Q42; REG-SDA-02 col S The longer of what the tenancy law of [state or territory] requires and 60 days before the increase starts (our standard)

t: Review the agreement with the participant.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Review the agreement with the participant. The Tenancy Officer Review it at least every 12 months, when the participant asks, and when something important changes. Ask what is working and what is not. Go through the main terms again, as in steps 12 and 13. Change the agreement only with the participant's agreement, except a change the law requires or a notice under step 22 or step 23. Save each change as a new dated version and keep the old one. Give the participant the changed copy, as in step 17. For a fixed term, write at least 90 days before the end date to confirm that it continues on the same terms. The agreement is current, and the participant has the changed copy. AGR-SDA-01 Q40, Q43 and Q44 Every 12 months. A changed copy within 2 business days of the change. A fixed term letter at least 90 days before the end date (our standard)

t: Check that the agreement lets us end it, and set the days of notice.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Check that the agreement lets us end it, and set the days of notice. Ending an agreement can leave a person without a home. A reason we cannot use, or a missed step, can break the law and leave the participant homeless. The SDA Manager Use Decision table 3. Check the reason is on the list in the agreement, and is not one the agreement says we never use. Check the steps that must come first are done, and write what we tried, with dates. Send a tenure check request to the Chief Executive under PRO-SDA-03 steps 22 and 23, and wait for the decision. Set the notice at the days in Q23. That is at least 90, and longer where the law says. Offer the participant an independent advocate. Then go on at PRO-SDA-05 step 24, which checks the notice rule and gets the Chief Executive's approval. AGR-SDA-01 Q45 Before any notice is written (our standard)

t: Decide in writing whether shorter notice is needed.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Decide in writing whether shorter notice is needed. we propose fewer than 90 days of notice The Chief Executive Allow fewer days only where a risk of harm to the participant or to others needs it, and only where tenancy law allows it. Write the risk, and why 90 days would not keep people safe. Write your name and the date. The notice is never shorter than the law allows. When the notice is served, the Tenancy Officer tells the participant the reason in their way of communicating. A sole trader asks [independent contact for concerns]. A shorter notice has a written reason before it is given. AGR-SDA-01 Q46; REG-SDA-02 col AX Before the notice is given (our standard)

t: Check the days of notice before the notice is served.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Check the days of notice before the notice is served. The SDA Manager Count the days from the date the law treats the notice as received to the date the participant must leave. The count must be at least the days in Q23, or the days step 26 approved. Write the dates and the days. If the count is short, change the date to leave. Then the Tenancy Officer serves the notice under PRO-SDA-05 steps 24 to 27, and tells the participant how to seek a review. PRO-SDA-05 step 2 tells the NDIA within 5 business days. The notice gives the days the agreement promises. AGR-SDA-01 Q46; REG-SDA-02 col AZ Before the notice is served (our standard)

t: Settle the bond and give the participant a final statement.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Settle the bond and give the participant a final statement. The Tenancy Officer PRO-SDA-05 step 28 ends the tenancy and does the final inspection. This step applies the agreement's own terms. Give a final rent statement. Return the bond within the days in Q12. Keep back only unpaid rent, or damage the participant caused beyond fair wear and tear. Before you ask for any damage payment, check whether a missing support or adjustment caused it. Show the evidence in writing first and say how to dispute it. Write the keys returned. The participant has their bond, or the evidence for what was kept, and a final statement. AGR-SDA-01 Q47; REG-SDA-02 col U Within the days written in the agreement, and never later than tenancy law allows (our standard, and statutory: tenancy law of [state or territory])

t: Close the agreement.
w: Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation)
x: Close the agreement. The SDA Manager Check that Q45 to Q47 are complete, and that REG-SDA-02 col W shows how the tenancy ended. Check the participant was helped to find a home, with the supporters they chose. Write anything we learned in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register. File the agreement and every change. Keep them for 7 years after it ends (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026). The agreement is closed, with every record in place. AGR-SDA-01 Q47; REG-SDA-02 col W Within 10 business days of the participant leaving (our standard)

c: AGR-SDA-01 What this agreement is for
t: This is the written agreement between [Provider name] and a participant about the particip
x: This is the written agreement between [Provider name] and a participant about the participant's specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwelling. It sets out the rent and other money, how long the agreement lasts and how it can end. It also sets out how repairs work, and the rights and responsibilities of both of us. It is the written service agreement that the SDA Conditions Rule, section 9, requires. The SDA Rules 2020, section 36, require it too. The SDA Conditions Rule is the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018. The SDA Rules 2020 are the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. In this agreement "you" is the participant and "we" is [Provider name]. The Tenancy Officer completes the Schedule with you, in the way you choose to communicate. You can take your time, bring a person you trust, and ask for changes. STA-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement: Plain Summary says the same things in fewer words. This agreement is about your home only. If we also give you supports, we do that under a separate agreement, AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template. PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) sets every step. A copy signed by both of us is yours to keep. Records go to REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register.

x: You pay for damage only if you cause it and it is more than fair wear and tear. Before we ask you to pay, we check whether a missing support or adjustment caused it. If it did, we fix that first and do not charge you. We show you the evidence in writing, and you can dispute it.

x: We enter your dwelling only for a reason this agreement or the law allows: an inspection, a repair or work, a check on the safety features, or to show the dwelling to a person who may move in, a valuer or a buyer. The notice is at least 7 days for an inspection, a check or planned work, and at least 2 business days for a repair you asked for, or longer where the law of [state or territory] gives you more. You can agree to less. We go into your bedroom only with your agreement, each time. We never use a key to come in while you are home, except in an emergency. We enter without notice only in an emergency, to keep someone safe or to protect the dwelling, and we tell you why within 24 hours.

x: You can ask for a repair or for maintenance in any way you choose. You can tell a worker, phone, write, send a message, or ask a supporter to ask for you. Schedule Q24 gives our repair contact and our urgent number.

x: We acknowledge every repair request by the next business day. We tell you who will deal with it and how we have rated it.

x: A repair is an emergency if someone's life or health is at immediate risk, such as a failed ventilator power supply or a gas leak: call 000 first, your medical emergency plan applies, and we act the same day. Examples are a smoke alarm that does not work, a gas smell, a lock that does not work, no water or power, or a lift, hoist or door opener you rely on that is out of use. We make an urgent repair safe within 24 hours, and the same day where your safety or a life-support device depends on it, or we agree another safe way for you to use the room or feature. We finish it within 2 business days. If anyone is in danger, call 000 first.

x: Schedule Q25 lists the safety features of your dwelling, including smoke alarms and other fire alarms. Schedule Q26 sets out how you get out of the building in a fire or other emergency.

x: We keep the safety features working, and check them as often as the law and building standards require. You tell us straight away if one does not work.

x: We give the safety features and the way out to each provider who delivers supported independent living to you in the dwelling. t: We treat you with respect and dignity. We respect your privacy, your culture, your relatio
x: We treat you with respect and dignity. We respect your privacy, your culture, your relationships and your right to make your own decisions.

t: You can have visitors and relationships in your home, and your privacy and intimacy are re
x: You can have visitors and relationships in your home, and your privacy and intimacy are respected. We set no rule about visitors that is not in this agreement or the law. t: SDA: specialist disability accommodation. It means the building a person lives in. It does
x: SDA: specialist disability accommodation. It means the building a person lives in. It does not mean the supports given inside it. dwelling: a home where we provide or plan to provide SDA, whoever owns it. enrolled dwelling: a dwelling that the NDIA has enrolled as one where SDA can be provided. NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency. The SDA Rules 2020 call its Chief Executive Officer "the CEO". In our documents, "the Chief Executive" is always ours. resident: a person who lives in the dwelling, whether or not they are an NDIS participant. resident number: the number we use in place of a resident's name, for example the participant's record number in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register. eligible participant: a participant the NDIA has found eligible for SDA funding. SDA building type: one of four types in Schedule 1 of the SDA Rules 2020: apartment; villa, duplex or townhouse; house; group home. design category: one of five categories in Schedule 2 of the SDA Rules 2020: basic; improved livability; fully accessible; robust; high physical support. stock class: new build, existing stock or legacy stock, as sections 6 to 8 of the SDA Rules 2020 define them. design standard: for a new build, the SDA Design Standard edition named in the accredited SDA assessor's final as-built certificate; for existing or legacy stock, the Minimum Design Requirements in the NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation current at enrolment. The SDA Rules 2020 still call that document the "SDA Price Guide" (section 5). Where our documents say "feature list" they mean the requirements of the design standard for the dwelling's design category. density restriction: a limit on the number of eligible participants on one parcel of land that has 2 or more dwellings. parcel of land: the land that the law of the state or territory treats as one parcel for the density restriction (SDA Rules 2020, section 31(4)). list of laws: the dated list of the state and territory laws that apply to each dwelling, kept once in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register and cited by REG-SDA-01 and REG-SDA-02. defect: anything broken, unsafe, leaking, missing or not working in a dwelling. good state of repair: the structure is sound, the fixtures and services work, and every design feature works as it was designed to. SDA Manager: the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. In a small provider this may be the Chief Executive. Tenancy Officer: the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager. independent contact for concerns: in a provider with one owner, the outside person who hears concerns about the owner. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. This follows the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, section 2B; the SDA Rules 2020 do not define it themselves. SDA Rules 2020: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. SDA Conditions Rule: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018. The indicators call it "Rules".

t: Control
Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure
The result: every dwelling we enrol meets the requirements the NDIA enrolled it on. It sta
x: The result: every dwelling we enrol meets the requirements the NDIA enrolled it on. It stays within them. It is safe, secure, private and in good repair. This procedure gives effect to POL-SDA-04 Enrolment of SDA Properties Policy, C1 to C14.

t: Start this procedure when any of these happens: we think about enrolling a dwelling a pers
x: Start this procedure when any of these happens: we think about enrolling a dwelling a person is offered a home in an enrolled dwelling an inspection, a certificate or a service falls due a worker, a resident, the owner or another provider reports a defect something happens that the NDIA must be told about, or the NDIA writes to us the check of the list of laws falls due every 12 months, or the law changes; or the report to the governing body falls due every 3 months the sample re-inspection falls due every 12 months. Who acts: The SDA Manager opens each dwelling record, checks the dwelling, applies to the NDIA, inspects, rates and chases repairs, and tells the NDIA. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. They tell residents, give notice of entry and warn the SDA Manager of each planned move-in. In a small provider the SDA Manager is the Tenancy Officer. The Quality Manager checks the evidence before a certification, reviews the laws, re-inspects a sample and reports to the governing body. The Chief Executive signs each certification to the NDIA, answers NDIA notices and decides when an enrolment may end. Every worker reports each defect the same day. The on-call manager makes an urgent defect safe after hours. In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader names an independent contact for concerns in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. That person checks the evidence at step 11 before the sole trader signs at step 12. They do the sample at step 29 and hear any concern about the sole trader. Where a step says to tell the next role, a sole trader writes down the time and carries on.

t: The SDA Manager: You can open REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register and FRM-SDA-03 SDA Dwelling
x: The SDA Manager: You can open REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register and FRM-SDA-03 SDA Dwelling Inspection and Compliance Checklist. You hold the current NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation (the SDA Rules 2020 still call it the SDA Price Guide) and the current SDA Design Standard, and you know their versions and dates: [Pricing Arrangements version and date]; [SDA Design Standard edition]. You have the list of laws for the dwelling's state or territory from REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. You have access to the my NDIS provider portal (myID and RAM), where enrolment applications are lodged, and you know the NDIA contact for SDA enrolment: [NDIA contact for SDA]. Everyone who acts: You have each resident's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, so you know how they want to be told things. You know the repairs number, [repairs number], and the on-call number, [on-call number]. Workers: you know that any defect goes to the SDA Manager the same day (step 20).

t: If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. A gas smell, smoke, a fire alarm going off, live w
x: If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. A gas smell, smoke, a fire alarm going off, live wiring or flooding near power can kill. The defect report comes second. Providing SDA in a dwelling the NDIA has not enrolled breaks a condition of our registration. It can bring a civil penalty (SDA Conditions Rule, section 6(a); NDIS Act 2013, section 73J). Nobody moves in as an SDA resident until the enrolment is on the row. A signed certification must be true. Applying for a dwelling that does not meet the requirements also breaks that condition. The NDIA can cancel an enrolment after a notice of at least 14 days (SDA Rules 2020, section 27). The density count includes other people's dwellings. A count of our own dwellings alone can leave a parcel over its limit, and our dwelling out of its enrolment. The NDIA clock starts on the event, not on the day we find the paperwork. A late notice breaks a condition of enrolment (SDA Rules 2020, section 29). The NDIA can cancel an enrolment for that. A required design feature that stays out of use can change the dwelling's category. Residents lose the access the home was enrolled to give them. Fix it, and decide at once whether the NDIA must be told. A lock, gate or sensor that limits a resident's movement may be a restrictive practice. Fit none without the authorisation the law requires. PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies. Entering a resident's home without lawful notice breaks tenancy law and the resident's privacy. It also costs their trust in us. A repair is never a reason to move a resident, or to change their supports. Housing and supports stay separate.

t: Check whether the density restriction applies to the parcel, and whether we are inside its
x: Check whether the density restriction applies to the parcel, and whether we are inside its limit, using Decision table 3. A parcel's limit counts eligible participants in every dwelling on it. Where an answer is missing and the NDIA cannot confirm it, record the dwellings you observed, the bedrooms from the title plan and the written requests you sent, and write "not known" against the gap. The Chief Executive then decides whether to apply, with the section 25(3)(i) answer stated as "not exceeded on the information available" and the gaps listed. Count the eligible participants we plan to house, and add them to the count. The row shows whether the restriction applies, the limit, the count and the result. FRM-SDA-03 Q16 and Q20. t: Check the funding history of the dwelling.
x: Check the funding history of the dwelling. The SDA Manager Ask the owner for a written statement, and check our own records. Answer three questions. Has the NDIS funded or provided complex home modifications after 1 December 2016, within the 10 years before the application date? Has it funded other home modifications within the 5 years before? Does any government currently provide funding for the dwelling under a scheme unrelated to disability accommodation? A yes to any of them means we cannot certify the dwelling. Stop and take advice. Historic funding under an unrelated scheme that has ended is a "take advice" flag, not a bar. The funding history is on record, and every answer is no. FRM-SDA-03 Q17. x: Inspect the whole dwelling with FRM-SDA-03, and collect every certificate the law requires. A dwelling that does not meet the building and safety law cannot be certified. Ask the council, a building certifier or a licensed trade if you are not sure what the law of the state requires. Collect the certificate of occupancy or its equivalent. Collect any certificate for fire safety, electrical work, gas, hot water, lifts, hoists and pools. Collect any approval to use the building as disability accommodation. List each certificate, service and planned maintenance job the dwelling needs, with its due date, as rows in REG-SDA-01. Fix any defect that affects safety, security or a design feature before you apply. The dwelling has been inspected against the law and its category, and each certificate is on file. FRM-SDA-03 Q1 to Q44. REG-SDA-01 col AI and col AL Before the application is lodged (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 25(4)(d))

t: Check the evidence for every matter we must certify, using Decision table 4.

t: Decide whether to apply, and sign the certification.

t: Lodge the application with the signed certification through the my NDIS provider portal.

Add the owner's name where we do not own the dwelling. Say whether the density restriction applies to the parcel, and whether it would be exceeded. Say whether the NDIS has funded modifications. t: Send the NDIA what it asked for.

The decision can be reviewed (SDA Rules 2020, section 26(3)), and the Chief Executive decides whether to ask. Tell each person who was offered the home, in their format, the same day. We provide no SDA there. The row shows the decision, and nobody has moved in before enrolment. REG-SDA-01 col AE, col BI, col BK and col N The same day the decision arrives (our standard)

t: Check that a move-in keeps the dwelling inside its enrolled numbers and its density limit.
x: Check that a move-in keeps the dwelling inside its enrolled numbers and its density limit. Do the check once, here, and give the Tenancy Officer the limits check row number and date. Check nine things. (1) The dwelling was inspected in the last 30 days; if not, inspect it under step 19 before the person moves in, or do a "vacant room and shared areas" check under step 19 where the last full inspection is under 6 months old. PRO-SDA-05 step 3 books this when the vacancy is advertised. (2) The number of residents after the move is within the enrolled maximum. (8) Where a participant provides SDA to themselves in a dwelling enrolled for more than 5 residents, only their spouse or de facto partner and children live there with them. (9) No check is older than 30 days at the move-in date. If any check fails, the move-in does not go ahead. Tell the Chief Executive the same day. REG-SDA-01 col AF, col AG, col AH and col M Before the move-in is confirmed to the person (statutory: SDA Conditions Rule, section 11(a), and SDA Rules 2020, section 31)

Where the law requires more, the law applies. A resident may agree to less. Write down that they agreed. Say who is coming, why, when and which rooms. Ask which rooms they agree to and who they want there. Offer another time if they ask. A resident may say no to a room. Write it down. Never enter a bedroom or bathroom without the resident's agreement or lawful notice. Do not visit more often than tenancy law allows for routine inspections. Enter without notice only in an emergency, and only where the law allows it. Each resident knows who is coming and when, and has agreed. FRM-SDA-03 Q5 and Q6. Enter the rows within 2 business days; enter a repair row and its rating within 1 business day, and the same day for an emergency or urgent defect. REG-SDA-01 col A, col AL, col M and col L Every 6 months, or as often as the tenancy law of [state or territory] allows, if fewer. Within 5 business days of a change, an incident or an NDIA request. Residents told the result within 5 business days of the inspection (our standard)

t: Report the defect to the SDA Manager the same day.
x: Report the defect to the SDA Manager the same day. Any worker who sees or hears of a defect If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. A defect is anything broken, unsafe, leaking, missing or not working in the dwelling. A resident may tell any worker, in any way. A worker from another provider phones the repairs number. Phone the on-call manager at once for an emergency or an urgent defect. Emergency means a failure of power, backup power, water, a hoist, a call system or a way in and out for a resident whose support plan says they depend on it for breathing, feeding, suction, pressure care, medication or calling for help: call 000 if they are in danger, then the on-call manager at once, and the participant's medical emergency plan applies. Urgent means a fire or smoke alarm fault, exposed wiring, a gas smell, a door or window that cannot be locked, or no water or power. It also means a feature a resident relies on that is not working. Complete questions 1 to 4 and question 40 of FRM-SDA-03. Repair nothing yourself unless it is safe and you are trained. The SDA Manager knows about the defect and who reported it. FRM-SDA-03 Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 and Q40 Phone straight away for an emergency or urgent defect. Written report the same day (our standard)

t: Rate each defect using Decision table 5, and act on its rating.

For an urgent defect, make the home safe within 24 hours, or arrange another safe way for the resident to use their room, bathroom or way in. After hours the on-call manager does this. A defect that stops a resident using a feature their design category needs is never routine. Tell each affected resident the rating, what we will do and by when, in the format they chose. Where a resident stays at risk until the fix, offer a choice of interim measures. Never ask a resident to move out. Each defect has a rating, an owner and a due date, and each affected resident knows. FRM-SDA-03 Q40 and Q44. REG-SDA-01 col AU, col AV, col AW, col K and col L Acknowledge by the next business day. Rate within 1 business day of the report, and the same day for an emergency or urgent defect. Make an emergency defect safe the same day and an urgent defect within 24 hours (our standard)

Close the row only when it meets every closing condition in REG-SDA-01. The repair is checked, the resident has said it is fixed, and the row is closed. REG-SDA-01 col BI, col BJ, col BK, col BA, col L and col M Within 5 business days of the event (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2)). We aim for 3 business days; a notice sent after 3 and within 5 is an improvement trigger, not a breach

t: Answer the NDIA's notice by the date it sets.

Read it for its date and its conditions. For a certification request, engage a person who meets the notice's rules on qualifications and independence within 5 business days. Contractors are briefed under step 23. Every worker at our dwellings has been briefed in the last 12 months. REG-SDA-01 col BM. Put a risk to the whole organisation in REG-RSK-01 Risk Register. Send training gaps to PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure. The governing body has read the report and decided what to fix. REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register. The governing body's minutes Every 3 months (our standard)

t: SDA Dwelling Register
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] looks after each specialist
x: This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] looks after each specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwelling. It shows how we enrol it, keep it inside its enrolment, and keep it safe, secure, private and in good repair. Each row is one record about one dwelling. A row shows what was found or decided, who did it, which residents were told, and when the next action falls due. Indicators evidenced: s 71 (1), s 71 (2) and s 71 (3). The modification columns also evidence s 68 (1) and s 72 (5). FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling Modification and Adjustment Request sends its rows here. Legal basis: Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 6. SDA Conditions Rule, sections 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. SDA Rules 2020, sections 5 to 8, 15, 19 and 24 to 32. The SDA Rules 2020 are the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. The SDA Conditions Rule is the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018. No law sets the columns of this register. They are our standard, built from what the law makes us certify, notify and keep. Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded. Keep a dwelling row for 7 years after the dwelling stops being enrolled with us (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years; this register's rows support SDA claims, so 7 years is also the statutory floor. Other law can require a certificate or a safety record to be kept longer. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed. Roles and words: SDA Manager: the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. Tenancy Officer: the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. Business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. List of laws: the dated list of state and territory laws kept once in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. The register holds ten types of row. Column C names the type. Columns A to Q are the spine, and every row uses them. Each type then fills its own group of columns: dwelling: columns R to AE limits check: columns AF to AH certificate or service: columns AI to AK inspection: columns AL to AT repair: columns AU to BA modification record: columns BB to BG and BP to BT entry record: column BH NDIA matter: columns BI to BK compliance check: columns BL to BM house rules check: columns BN to BO Residents' names are not kept here. A row uses resident numbers. A resident number is the number we use in place of a name, for example the participant's record number in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register. Health details, behaviour support content and a resident's own words stay on their own file. Keep each row type on its own sheet, with the spine columns first. A provider with one dwelling has few rows: one dwelling row, two inspections a year, and a handful of certificate or service rows.

t: The SDA Manager adds every row. The Tenancy Officer adds entry records and modification re
x: The SDA Manager adds every row. The Tenancy Officer adds entry records and modification records, and may add a repair row from a resident's report. The Quality Manager adds compliance check rows, and inspection rows for a sample re-inspection. The person who enters a home records the entry the same day, and the Tenancy Officer adds the entry record. When the SDA Manager is away, the Tenancy Officer adds rows. Add the row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Add an NDIA matter row, a repair row and its rating within 1 business day, and an emergency or urgent repair row the same day. Use one row for each limits check, certificate or service due, inspection, defect, modification request, entry and NDIA matter. An inspection that finds 3 defects makes 4 rows, plus a limits check row. Link them at col P. A dwelling has one dwelling row in force at a time. When a dwelling fact changes, add a new version of the row with the date, your name and the reason. The old version becomes "superseded". Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason. Write resident numbers, not names. Leave out health details, behaviour support content and a resident's private words. Use one row each time a certificate or a service falls due. When it is done, close the row and open the next one. When someone was hurt or nearly hurt, the event is also an incident. Write its number from REG-INC-01 Incident Register at col P. A complaint goes in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register. A hazard to people while supports are given goes in REG-ENV-01 Hazard and Maintenance Register. Tenancy facts go in REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register. Link each one here. At any time, each enrolled dwelling must show a dwelling row with the status "enrolled". It must show an inspection row and a limits check row, each not older than 6 months. Its certificate or service rows must not be past their due dates, and no repair row may be past its due date. Reopen a closed row when the defect comes back. Set col N to "reopened" and write the reason. Which columns each row type fills: Row type Use it for Columns to fill Dwelling Each dwelling we enrol or plan to enrol. One row is in force at a time A to L, N to AE Limits check Each check of numbers and density: before we apply, before a move-in, and at an inspection A to H, K to Q, AF to AH Certificate or service Each certificate, approval, service or test that falls due A to H, K to Q, AI to AK Inspection Each inspection, with the residents A to Q, AL to AT Repair Each defect, from report to closing A to Q, AU to BA Modification record Each change a participant asks for, sent here from FRM-SDA-01 A to Q, BB to BG, BP to BT Entry record Each entry into a resident's home by us or a contractor A to I, M to Q, BH NDIA matter Each notice we send the NDIA, and each notice, request or decision we receive from it A to H, J to Q, BI to BK Compliance check Each 12-monthly check of the list of laws, each check when the law changes, and the briefing of people who work at our dwellings A to H, K to Q, BL and BM House rules check Each check of house rules, notices, forms and agreements against residents' rights, made under PRO-SDA-02 A to Q, BN and BO A row is closed only when all of these are true for its type: Dwelling: a new version has replaced it, or the dwelling is no longer enrolled with us and the NDIA has been told. Limits check: the result is recorded. If it was "over a limit", the Chief Executive has decided what happens. Certificate or service: the certificate or report is filed, and the next one has its own row. Inspection: every defect has its own row, each resident has been told the result, and the next inspection date is set. Repair: the work is done, someone other than the contractor has checked it, the resident says it is fixed, and the resident has been told. Any NDIA matter row for it is also closed. Modification record: FRM-SDA-01 question 37 is answered. Entry record: the visit is recorded, with the time out and any key used. NDIA matter: the notice or answer was sent, proof is filed, and the NDIA's reply is recorded. A notice we sent may close on "no reply" after 20 business days (our standard). An application for enrolment, a request from the NDIA and a notice from the NDIA stay open until the NDIA decides. Compliance check: every change found has an owner and a due date. House rules check: every limit found is removed, or has its lawful authority and the Chief Executive's decision on file. Each resident affected has been told. The SDA Manager approves closing. Its aim is that each participant can exercise choice and control over their home. It is for participants, their supporters, their supported independent living (SIL) providers, our workers and the people who check our work.

t: Every dwelling [Provider name] has enrolled for SDA, and every participant who lives in on
x: Every dwelling [Provider name] has enrolled for SDA, and every participant who lives in one. Every vacancy, tenancy notice and change in a participant's needs in those dwellings. Every arrangement with a participant's SIL providers. Every worker who manages, maintains or visits a dwelling for us: employees, contractors, agents and volunteers. Every complaint and incident that concerns a tenancy. Where [Provider name] also delivers SIL in a dwelling, this policy applies to us as the SDA provider. POL-SIL-05 Agreements about Tenancy, Housing and Support Arrangements Policy applies to us as the SIL provider. This policy does not cover the supports a SIL provider delivers. Each SIL provider answers for those under its own policies.

x: We will house a participant only in a dwelling that is enrolled, and never above the number of residents it is enrolled for. We start SDA only when the written service agreement is signed. We may also start when a proposed copy has been given and explained, and we provide SDA on its terms.

t: We will follow the landlord, tenancy, building, and health and safety law that applies to
x: We will follow the landlord, tenancy, building, and health and safety law that applies to each dwelling. We make sure everyone we employ or engage does the same. We keep the state or territory rules for tenancy notices in the register, built from the one dated list of laws in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register, and check each one against the law at least every 12 months and whenever the law changes.

x: We will declare, advertise and fill every vacancy in the same fair way. We tell the NDIA in writing within 5 business days. We advertise in at least 2 places for at least 10 business days. We ask each current resident before any offer, and we choose only on criteria we publish.

t: We will give each participant our vacancy process, their tenancy agreements and every tena
x: We will give each participant our vacancy process, their tenancy agreements and every tenancy notice. We use the language, mode of communication and terms which that participant is most likely to understand. We write down what they said back.

t: We will agree a documented arrangement with each participant and each of their SIL provide
x: We will agree a documented arrangement with each participant and each of their SIL providers. It names, for each matter, the party responsible, their role, a contact person and a response time. Where a participant does not agree or sign, we record it in their words, and nothing changes in their tenancy.

t: We will help residents settle conflict early and fairly. We meet each person affected, alo
x: We will help residents settle conflict early and fairly. We meet each person affected, alone, within 5 business days. We never move a person, or limit their access, to settle a conflict.

t: We will act on every allegation or incident of violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or d
x: We will act on every allegation or incident of violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination in or around a dwelling. We act on the day we learn of it. We support each person affected, record the details and the outcome of every review, and change something to stop a repeat. The person harmed keeps their home.

t: We will take every concern about a dwelling from anyone, and acknowledge it within 1 busin
x: We will take every concern about a dwelling from anyone, and acknowledge it within 1 business day. We record each concern, even one that is not a complaint or a repair. We give an answer, or a date for one, within 5 business days. We make an emergency safety problem safe the same day and an urgent one within 24 hours.

t: We will manage behaviours of concern that may put a tenancy at risk through the participan
x: We will manage behaviours of concern that may put a tenancy at risk through the participant's supports, not through the tenancy. We take no tenancy action about behaviour until we have asked the participant and offered an advocate. We also ask their SIL provider and behaviour support practitioner, with their agreement, what would help.

t: We will agree each change in a participant's needs or circumstances with them first. We pa
x: We will agree each change in a participant's needs or circumstances with them first. We pass it on, within 2 business days, only to the people they choose. We make reasonable adjustments, and we modify the dwelling where the new needs call for it, after asking each other resident affected.

t: We will tell a participant in person, within 2 business days of confirming it, when their
x: We will tell a participant in person, within 2 business days of confirming it, when their home cannot meet their needs. We tell the providers they choose and help them find another home. The participant decides whether and when to move. We do not serve a notice on that ground until the Chief Executive has reviewed every other option with them and an advocate.

t: We will agree with each participant and each SIL provider how supports and accommodation c
x: We will agree with each participant and each SIL provider how supports and accommodation continue in an emergency or a disaster. We give each SIL provider the dwelling's safety and emergency information before its first shift, and we keep the safety features tested. If the dwelling cannot be used, we arrange, with the participant's SIL provider and their emergency plan, safe temporary accommodation as soon as possible and within 24 hours, and a place that meets their access and equipment needs as soon as one can be found. We pay for or help fund it where the law or the agreement puts that on us.

t: We will give every tenancy notice as the law of the state or territory requires: on a grou
x: We will give every tenancy notice as the law of the state or territory requires: on a ground the law allows, in the form the law prescribes, with every prerequisite notice and third-party notification the law requires. A notice to vacate gives at least 90 days, and never because of the participant's choice of SIL provider, a complaint, or a refusal to sign an arrangement. A rent change gives the longer of what the law requires and 60 days. The Chief Executive approves each notice that would end a tenancy. We hear the participant first before any notice that would end or limit their tenancy. With every notice we tell them how to seek a review.

t: We will deal with every complaint and every incident about a tenancy through our complaint
x: We will deal with every complaint and every incident about a tenancy through our complaints system and our incident system. Both meet the NDIS rules, and both treat each person fairly.

t: SDA provider: the registered NDIS provider that owns or manages an enrolled dwelling and h
x: SDA provider: the registered NDIS provider that owns or manages an enrolled dwelling and houses participants in it. SIL provider: any other NDIS provider that delivers supported independent living supports to a participant in the dwelling. enrolled dwelling: a dwelling the NDIA has enrolled to provide SDA, for a set number of residents. resident: a person who lives in the dwelling, whether or not they use our services. arrangement: the written agreement between a participant, the SDA provider and each SIL provider that names who is responsible for each matter. tenancy notice: any notice about a participant's tenancy that the law of the state or territory regulates. Examples are an entry notice, a rent change and a notice to vacate. conflict: a disagreement between people who live in the home. It is not a conflict of interest. behaviours of concern: behaviour that puts the person or others at risk, or may put their tenancy at risk. restrictive practice: anything that limits a person's rights or freedom of movement. Five kinds are regulated: seclusion, and chemical, mechanical, physical and environmental restraint. reasonable adjustment: a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice or communicate. It lets a participant use their home on the same terms as anyone else. modification: a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. payback: treating a person worse for raising a concern, making a complaint or using a right. business day: a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. SDA Manager: the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. Tenancy Officer: the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager. concern: anything a participant, a resident, a supporter, a worker or another provider raises about a dwelling that is not yet a complaint, a repair or an incident. Each one gets a concern row in REG-SDA-02.

The result: each participant who lives in one of our specialist disability accommodation (
x: The result: each participant who lives in one of our specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwellings has a lawful, fair tenancy that they understand. A vacancy is filled with each resident's say. The participant's supported independent living (SIL) providers have agreed in writing who does what. A tenancy notice is served only as the law allows, and the participant knows they can ask for a review. t: Use this procedure for every dwelling [Provider name] has enrolled for SDA, and for every
x: Use this procedure for every dwelling [Provider name] has enrolled for SDA, and for every participant who lives in one. It starts at six points: a place becomes free, or is about to (steps 1 to 11) a participant moves in, a SIL provider starts or changes, or an arrangement is due for review (steps 12 to 14) day to day: a concern, a conflict, harm, a behaviour that may put a tenancy at risk, or an emergency (steps 15 to 21) a participant's needs or circumstances change (steps 22 and 23) we need to give a tenancy notice, or a tenancy ends (steps 24 to 28) the register is due for review (steps 29 and 30). A participant who already lives in a dwelling when you adopt this procedure starts at step 12. Who acts: The Tenancy Officer does the day-to-day tenancy work: advertising, applicants, residents, agreements, notices and records. The SDA Manager decides who is offered a place, takes charge of every response to harm, and owns the register. The Chief Executive reviews every notice that would end a tenancy and every decision that a home cannot meet a participant's needs. The Quality Manager samples the register and reports to the governing body. Every worker who sees, hears or is told of harm, a concern or a conflict passes it on. Workers include employees, contractors, agents and volunteers. Each SIL provider acts as the arrangement says. In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds them all. Where this procedure asks for a second person, the sole trader asks the independent contact for concerns, named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. If [Provider name] also delivers SIL in the dwelling, we are both parties at step 12. Two different people sign. PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) also applies. In this procedure: A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. "SDA Conditions Rule" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018. "SDA Rules 2020" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. "Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018. "Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager.

x: Each dwelling is enrolled. It has a row in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register with its design category, its building type and the number of residents it is enrolled for. You can open each participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form. If it is more than 12 months old, update it with the participant before anything else. You know whether each participant has agreed to share their information, and with whom. FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form shows it. In REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register, each kind of notice in [state or territory] has a notice rule row built from the dated list of laws in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. Each row was checked in the last 12 months and since the law last changed. If one is missing or old, do step 24 first. You hold the urgent line number [urgent line number], the NDIA contact for SDA notices [NDIA contact], and the independent contact for concerns. You hold STA-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancies: Plain Summary, AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement and a blank AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement.

t: Call 000 first if anyone is hurt, in danger or threatened with a weapon. A delay can cost
x: Call 000 first if anyone is hurt, in danger or threatened with a weapon. A delay can cost a life. A late notice to the NDIA breaks a condition of enrolment. The NDIA can then cancel the dwelling's enrolment. It must first give at least 14 days to put it right (SDA Rules 2020, sections 27 and 29). A tenancy never depends on a support choice. A notice given because a participant changed SIL provider, refused to sign an arrangement, complained or took a risk they chose is payback. It ends a home for the wrong reason. A notice that breaks the state rule may be invalid. The participant is then unsure whether they must leave. We may also face a tribunal. Locking, blocking access, taking belongings or limiting visitors is a restrictive practice. The Restrictive Practices Rules, section 6(e), call it environmental restraint. Without authorisation it can be a reportable incident. Private details about an applicant told to a resident, or the reverse, breach privacy. Share only what each person agreed to. A resident who feels unsafe cannot be talked round. Pushing a housemate on them can hurt them and ends their trust in us. The person harmed keeps their home. Moving or limiting the person who was hurt punishes them for another person's act. A concern about a manager can be buried if it goes only to that manager. Step 17 and If it goes wrong give another line.

t: Notify the NDIA in writing.
x: Notify the NDIA in writing. A late notice breaks a condition of enrolment. The NDIA can then cancel the dwelling's enrolment. a vacancy arises, a participant gives notice or is given notice to vacate, we propose rent above the limit, or an emergency may make the dwelling unsuitable for SDA The SDA Manager Use the channel the NDIA currently asks SDA providers to use. Write the dwelling, the event, the date it happened and, for a vacancy, that it is available to be filled. Keep a copy and the NDIA's reference. For rent above the limit, attach a certificate from a qualified property valuer that the rent is fair and reasonable. Work out the funding limit date for a dwelling enrolled for 2 to 5 residents. It applies when a participant dies, gives notice, or is given notice because of behaviour that might be a risk. The Rules then treat the participant as still living there until the vacancy is filled.
