REG-SDA-02 col AJ; REG-SDA-02 col AK; REG-SDA-02 col BD; REG-SDA-02 col T; REG-SDA-02 col BN Within 5 business days of the event (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2))

t: Advertise the vacancy.
x: Advertise the vacancy. A vacancy shown only to people we already know shuts out people with the same need. The Tenancy Officer Post a vacancy notice in at least 2 places that participants and support coordinators use. One must be open to the public without a login. Keep it open for at least 10 business days. State the suburb, the design category, the building type and the rooms. State the number of residents, with no personal detail. State the rent the participant would pay, how we choose using Decision table 1, the closing date, and how to ask for help to apply. Offer the notice in plain language, and in another format on request. Send it to each person on our list who may fit, and to each support coordinator who asked to hear of vacancies. Do not offer a gift, discount or reward to attract an applicant. While the notice is open, book the pre-move-in inspection, or the "vacant room and shared areas" check where the last full inspection is under 6 months old, under PRO-SDA-01 step 19, and ask each resident what matters to them in a housemate so steps 5 and 6 can run as applications arrive. Our target from step 1 to move-in is 30 business days, inside the 60-day funding limit. Law changing: from 20 November 2026 the NDIS Act 2013 bans inducements to provide supports (new section 73VA). Anyone who may fit can find the vacancy, in a form they can read, and knows how we choose. REG-SDA-02 col AL Within 5 business days of step 1 (our standard)

t: Help each applicant to apply.
x: Help each applicant to apply. The Tenancy Officer Take an application in any form: phone, email, letter, in person or through a supporter. Give each applicant a number. Do not write their name in the register. Ask how they want us to communicate. Offer help to apply and an independent advocate. Say how long the process takes, how we choose and when they will hear. Ask only what the criteria need. Get their consent on FRM-INF-01 before you ask anyone else about them. Every applicant has applied in a way they can, and knows how we choose and when they will hear. REG-SDA-02 col AM Acknowledge each application within 2 business days (our standard)

t: Check each applicant against Decision table 1.
x: Check each applicant against Decision table 1. The SDA Manager Read the part of the applicant's plan that says they are eligible for SDA. Check the design category and building type in it fit this dwelling. Check the applicant will have a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share. Count everyone who will live in the dwelling after the move. The count must not exceed the number it is enrolled for. Ask the applicant about their needs and wishes. With their consent, ask their support coordinator or SIL provider. Write the result for each criterion. Check for a conflict of interest of ours. Examples are a family or business tie, or a link between the vacancy and the applicant's choice of SIL provider. Declare it under PRO-SDA-03. Shortlist the applicants who meet criteria 1 and 2. Each applicant is checked on the same criteria and the SDA Manager has a shortlist. REG-SDA-02 col AN Within 5 business days of the closing date (our standard)

t: Ask each resident how they feel about a new person moving in.
x: Ask each resident how they feel about a new person moving in. A resident who is pushed to accept a housemate may stop raising concerns. the dwelling has other residents The Tenancy Officer Ask before any offer. Ask about the criteria while the vacancy is advertised (step 3) and about the shortlist here, so the two conversations run inside the advertising period. Ask each resident alone, in their own way of communicating, with a supporter or advocate if they want one. Say a place is free and a person may move in. Tell them only what the shortlisted applicants agreed to share. Ask what matters to them in a housemate and what they would like to know. Ask whether they want to meet the person and whether they have any worry. Say that their answer will be heard and never affects their tenancy. For a resident who does not use words, watch and ask a supporter who knows them. The SIL provider may already hold FRM-SIL-06 Co-Tenant Consultation and Matching Record for this vacancy. If so, ask for it with the resident's consent. Do not ask the same questions twice. Write each answer in a few words, without names. Use Decision table 2. Every resident has been heard before anyone is offered the place. REG-SDA-02 col AO Give each resident at least 5 business days to answer, unless they answer sooner (our standard)

t: Meet the resident to find a way through.
x: Meet the resident to find a way through. a resident says they are worried, do not feel safe, or do not want the person The SDA Manager Meet them alone, with an independent advocate or supporter if they want one. Ask what would make it work, such as meeting the person first or a trial visit. Use Decision table 2. Tell them nothing private about the applicant. Do not press them to agree. If they say they do not feel safe, do not offer the place to that applicant until they say the worry is settled. If it is not settled, offer the place to the next applicant and ask each resident again. Sometimes the worry is about who the applicant is, not how they would live together. Explain that we cannot refuse an applicant for that reason. Ask what worries them in daily life. Each worry has been heard and worked through, and nobody is pushed into a housemate they feel unsafe with. REG-SDA-02 col AP Meet within 2 business days of the resident's answer (our standard)

t: Decide which applicant to offer the place to.
x: Decide which applicant to offer the place to. The SDA Manager Use only the criteria in Decision table 1 and what each resident said. Choose between applicants who meet criteria 1 and 2 by the applicant's own wishes and the residents' views. Use the date they applied only to separate applicants who are equal. Write the reasons against each criterion, in plain words an applicant could test. If no applicant meets criteria 1 and 2, or a resident's safety worry is unresolved for every applicant, offer the place to nobody. Keep the vacancy open and go back to step 3. If the SDA Manager has a conflict of interest, the Chief Executive decides. The place is offered on stated reasons, with every resident's view taken into account. REG-SDA-02 col AQ Within 5 business days of the last resident's answer (our standard)

t: Offer the place to the chosen applicant.
x: Offer the place to the chosen applicant. The Tenancy Officer Offer in the applicant's way of communicating. Give them time to decide. Offer a visit to the dwelling, and a meeting with any resident who agrees. Give them the draft SDA service agreement (AGR-SDA-01), the rent they would pay, a draft AGR-SDA-02 and STA-SDA-02. Go through each in their way. Ask them to say back what it means. Offer an independent advocate and independent advice about the agreement. Say that the offer never depends on who delivers their other supports. Say that they can ask for this process in any format. If they decline, say that it counts for nothing against them. Then go back to step 8 and offer the place to the next applicant. The applicant chooses freely, with what they need to know in a form they understand. REG-SDA-02 col AR At least 5 business days to decide, and longer if they ask (our standard)

t: Tell each applicant who was not offered the place.
x: Tell each applicant who was not offered the place. The Tenancy Officer Say the result, and the reasons against each criterion, in plain words and in their way. Share nothing about any other applicant or resident. Tell them how to ask the Chief Executive for another look and how to complain to us. Give them the NDIS Commission's number, 1800 035 544. Offer an advocate. Keep them on our list for the next vacancy if they agree. Each applicant knows why, and how to challenge the decision. REG-SDA-02 col AS Within 5 business days of the chosen applicant's answer (our standard)

t: Confirm the move-in checks.
x: Confirm the move-in checks. The SDA Manager Obtain the limits check row number from PRO-SDA-01 step 16, dated within 30 days. It shows the dwelling is enrolled, the numbers and the density limit are met, and the room, bathroom and plan fit. Do not confirm the move-in without it. Check that the SDA service agreement is signed. If not, check that a proposed copy was given and explained, and that we will provide SDA on its terms. Check the participant has a copy, or write why not. Check the rent is no more than the NDIS amount plus the participant's reasonable rent contribution. If it is more, go to step 2. Write the bond: the amount, who holds it, and the receipt given. Tell each resident who agreed the move-in date. Tell each SIL provider the participant has chosen, with their consent. Make sure step 12 is booked and step 14 is ready. Open the tenancy row from AGR-SDA-01. Copy what you gave the applicant at step 9 into column V. Write the planned move-in date, and correct it on the day. The participant moves into a lawful, ready home, and the tenancy is on the record. REG-SDA-02 col P (the limits check row number and date); REG-SDA-02 col Q; REG-SDA-02 col R; REG-SDA-02 col S; REG-SDA-02 col T; REG-SDA-02 col U; REG-SDA-02 col V; REG-SDA-02 col AT Before the move-in day (statutory for the agreement: SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1); statutory for the limits check: SDA Conditions Rule, section 11(a), and SDA Rules 2020, section 31; our standard for the other checks)

t: Agree or review the arrangements.
x: Agree or review the arrangements. a participant moves in, a SIL provider starts or changes, an arrangement changes, no arrangement exists, or 12 months have passed since the last review The Tenancy Officer Open an arrangement row. If no SIL provider supports the participant in the dwelling, write "none in this dwelling" and a date within 6 months to check again. Then stop. Otherwise start with the participant alone, with a supporter or advocate if they want one. Go through STA-SDA-02 and each Term of AGR-SDA-02 in their way. Explain that it is separate from their other agreements and that they keep their home whatever they decide. Offer independent advice. Write how you explained it, who was there and what they said back. Complete Sections A and B with them. Then take the same draft to each SIL provider. Check on the NDIS Provider Register that it is registered for SIL. If it is not registered, still make the arrangement (SDA Conditions Rule, section 10(2)(a)), tell the participant plainly, and tell the Chief Executive, who decides whether to notify the NDIS Commission. Settle each matter with a party responsible, a role, a contact and a response time. At a review, ask the participant first what works and what does not, and change only what they want changed. For a participant who already lives there, also write what you gave them in column V. Every matter has a party responsible, a role, a contact and a response time, and the participant understands what was agreed. AGR-SDA-02 Q1; REG-SDA-02 col X; REG-SDA-02 col AA; REG-SDA-02 col AC; REG-SDA-02 col V Before move-in where the SIL provider is known. Otherwise within 10 business days of learning who it is. Reviewed at least every 12 months (our standard)

t: Record each party's decision about the arrangement.
x: Record each party's decision about the arrangement. The Tenancy Officer Give the participant the draft at least 5 business days before you ask for a decision. Ask each party to sign or to give its decision: agrees, agrees in part, does not agree, chose not to sign, or could not sign. A decision given aloud counts. Write who heard it and when. Write the participant's decision in their own words. If they do not agree or sign, write why, what stays in place and when you will offer again. After two refusals, record the participant's standing answer and ask again only at the 12-month review, or when the participant, the SIL provider or their needs change. Nothing changes in their tenancy or supports. If a SIL provider does not sign, write its reason and what we did to reach agreement. Give each party a copy, and give the participant theirs in the format they chose. Set the next review date. Each party's decision is on the record and each has a copy. A refusal is a record, not a gap. AGR-SDA-02 Q22; REG-SDA-02 col Y; REG-SDA-02 col Z; REG-SDA-02 col AD; REG-SDA-02 col AH Copies within 2 business days of each decision. Offer again within 28 days of a first refusal; after two refusals, at the 12-month review or when things change (our standard)

t: Give each SIL provider access and the dwelling's safety information.
x: Give each SIL provider access and the dwelling's safety information. The SDA Manager Give the keys or codes the participant agreed to. Never restrict a provider the participant chose from entering the dwelling to deliver their supports. The participant decides who enters their bedroom. Walk the provider's first worker through the dwelling. Show the alarms, extinguishers, exits and meeting point, and how to reach our urgent line. Say who maintains and tests each safety feature. Use the latest FRM-SDA-03 SDA Dwelling Inspection and Compliance Checklist for the test dates. The SIL provider tells its workers, and any other provider who works there. Write the test dates and the temporary accommodation arrangement. Each SIL provider can get in, and knows how to get everyone out safely. AGR-SDA-02 Q27; REG-SDA-02 col AB; REG-SDA-02 col AG Before the SIL provider's first shift in the dwelling (statutory for access: SDA Conditions Rule, section 10(2)(b); SDA Rules 2020, section 37, is the equivalent for registered providers of supports; our standard for the timing)

t: Acknowledge the concern.
x: Acknowledge the concern. A participant who fears losing their home may stop raising concerns. Silence is not satisfaction. The Tenancy Officer Anyone can raise a concern: the participant, a housemate, a supporter or a SIL worker. Any worker who hears one passes it to the Tenancy Officer the same day. Write it in the person's own words. Open a concern row in REG-SDA-02 for every concern, whatever it becomes, and sort it with Decision table 3. For an emergency matter, make it safe the same day; for an urgent matter, within 24 hours; phone the urgent line for both. Open a repair in REG-SDA-01 under PRO-SDA-01. If the person is unhappy with a decision, or with something we did or did not do, it is a complaint. Start PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. Enter it in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register as "housing or tenancy" and link it in the concern row. Offer an advocate. Give an answer, or a date for one. Tell the person the outcome in their way within 2 business days of closing it. Never treat a person worse for raising a concern. The person knows who has their concern, what happens next and by when. REG-SDA-02 col BP; REG-SDA-02 col BQ; REG-SDA-02 col BR; REG-SDA-02 col BS; REG-FBK-01 for a complaint; REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register for a repair Acknowledge within 1 business day of the day it was first raised. Answer, or give a date, within 5 business days. Make an emergency matter safe the same day and an urgent one within 24 hours (our standard)

t: Help the residents settle the conflict.
x: Help the residents settle the conflict. residents are in conflict and it affects the home or a tenancy, or someone asks us to help The SDA Manager A conflict here is a disagreement between people who live in the home. It is not a conflict of interest. The SIL provider and its workers respond first on shift and record it on FRM-SIL-04 Co-Tenant Conflict Record. We join when it affects the dwelling, a shared space, a house rule or a tenancy, or when a resident or the SIL provider asks. Meet each person affected alone, with an advocate or supporter if they want one. Ask what happened from their side, how safe they feel, and what they want. Agree a short written plan with each person: actions, owners and dates. Use mediation only if everyone agrees and nobody is afraid. Never move anyone, change a room or limit access to a shared area to settle it. Where anyone is hurt or afraid, go to step 17 as well. Open a home event row. Each person has been heard and the conflict is settled or has a plan, and nobody has lost their home. REG-SDA-02 col BI; REG-SDA-02 col BJ Meet each person within 5 business days of learning of the conflict. Review the plan at 28 days (our standard)

t: Respond to the incident.
x: Respond to the incident. Locking a person in or out, blocking their way, taking their things or holding them can injure and frighten them. It is a restrictive practice. a person is, or may have been, subjected to violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination in or around a dwelling, or is threatened with harm The worker who sees it, hears it or is told Follow WIN-INC-01 Responding to an Incident (frontline), which sets out steps 1 to 7 of PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. Make people safe. Call 000 first if anyone is hurt or in danger. Do not lock, block or hold anyone, and do not take anyone's things. Where a crime may have happened, do not question further and do not clean up. Phone the SDA Manager, or our urgent line after hours, as soon as people are safe. If the concern is about the SDA Manager, phone the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, phone the independent contact for concerns. You can also phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. Nobody may punish you for reporting. Write the incident report before your shift ends. Nobody is in immediate danger, a manager knows, and a first-hand account exists. FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form Straight away. The call as soon as people are safe, and the report before your shift ends (our standard). The law says as soon as possible (statutory: Incident Rules, section 19)

t: Manage our response to the harm.
x: Manage our response to the harm. the SDA Manager is told of harm, or an allegation of harm, in or around a dwelling The SDA Manager Check that PRO-INC-01 has started. The Quality Manager, as the authorised notifier, decides whether it is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission under PRO-INC-02 Reportable Incidents Notification Procedure. Where abuse, neglect or exploitation is alleged, also start PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure and FRM-SGD-01 Allegation Response and Investigation Record. Speak alone with each person affected. Offer an independent advocate. Ask what they want and what would help them feel safe. Tell the SIL provider the same day if the dwelling is unsafe or damaged, and within 1 business day in any other case. Do this with the participant's agreement unless the law or safety requires otherwise. Do not move or limit the person who was harmed. Open a home event row. Keep each person's account on their own file. Each person affected is supported, the right reports are made, and the record shows what was done. REG-SDA-02 col BI; REG-SDA-02 col BJ; REG-SDA-02 col BL The same day. The Commission is notified within 24 hours of becoming aware where the incident involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm; otherwise within 5 business days (statutory: Incident Rules, sections 20 and 21)

t: Put right the damage and its cause.
x: Put right the damage and its cause. The SDA Manager Check the dwelling with the participant's agreement. Make safe anything damaged: locks, doors, fittings and alarms. Open a repair in REG-SDA-01. Brief each contractor on the dwelling entry rules before they enter, with the entry and privacy briefing in PRO-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation), as PRO-SDA-01 step 23 does. Do not ask any participant to pay for damage until we know what caused it, we have offered support and step 25 is done. Never claim against a participant who was harmed. Ask the people affected what would stop it happening again. Ideas include lighting, a roster for shared spaces, a house rule agreed with residents, a talk with the SIL provider, or a lock that the affected resident controls on their own bedroom door after the SDA Manager confirms it limits nobody else. Any lock, gate, sensor, alarm or key restriction that would limit a resident's movement or access is not a remedy here: refer it to the behaviour support pathway under PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure first, and fit nothing until an authorised behaviour support plan covers every resident it affects. Enter each change in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date. Tell each person affected what changed. The dwelling is safe, and something real has changed to prevent a repeat. REG-SDA-02 col BK; REG-SDA-02 col BM Make safe the same day. Open the repair within 1 business day. Agree changes within 10 business days (our standard)

t: Manage the behaviour through support, not through the tenancy.
x: Manage the behaviour through support, not through the tenancy. Locking, blocking access, taking belongings or limiting visitors because of a person's behaviour is a restrictive practice. Only an authorised behaviour support plan can allow it. a participant's behaviour may put their tenancy at risk The SDA Manager Ask the participant what is happening and how they want to be supported. With their agreement, ask their SIL provider and behaviour support practitioner what would help, whether the plan needs review, and whether the behaviour is a disability-related need that a reasonable adjustment or a plan review could meet. No notice relying on behaviour starts until the practitioner has answered that question. Look at the dwelling and the house rules. A change to either may help. Consider a reasonable adjustment under FRM-SDA-01. Offer an independent advocate. Record each step. If anyone is in danger now, go to step 17. Step 24 may start only when every step here is done, the problem remains, and the law gives a ground. This procedure authorises no restrictive practice. Behaviour is managed through the participant's supports, and no tenancy action starts without these steps. REG-SDA-02 col AF Start within 2 business days of learning of it (our standard)

t: Keep each participant safe and housed.
x: Keep each participant safe and housed. a fire, flood, storm, power or water loss or other event makes the dwelling unsafe or unusable, or a disaster warning affects the area The SDA Manager, or the person on the urgent line Call 000 if anyone is in danger. The SIL workers on shift lead the move, as the arrangement says. Where no SIL worker is there, phone each participant and their emergency contact, and arrange help. Phone each SIL provider's contact. Use each participant's own plan in FRM-SUP-07 Participant Emergency and Disaster Plan and PLN-EDM-01 Emergency and Disaster Management Plan. With each participant's SIL provider and their emergency plan, arrange safe temporary accommodation as soon as possible and within 24 hours, and a place that meets their access and equipment needs (power for equipment, hoist, pressure care, medication storage, continence) as soon as one can be found. The participant must agree to it. Where a participant's life depends on a device, their medical emergency plan applies and the SIL provider and their practitioner decide the clinical steps. Nobody loses their home because the building is damaged. Check the dwelling is safe before anyone returns. Tell the NDIA at step 2 if it may no longer suit SDA. Open a home event row. Write each person's move and return. Each participant is safe the same day, housed within 24 hours, and keeps their tenancy. REG-SDA-02 col BN; REG-SDA-02 col BI; REG-SDA-02 col BJ Safe the same day. Temporary accommodation as soon as possible and within 24 hours. The NDIA within 5 business days (our standard; statutory for the NDIA: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2))

t: Record the change in the participant's needs or circumstances.
x: Record the change in the participant's needs or circumstances. The Tenancy Officer A change can come from the participant, a supporter, a SIL provider, a worker or a dwelling check. Ask the participant first whether they agree to us telling others. Write what changed in plain words, with no diagnosis. Tell the providers they chose. Ask what they want from the dwelling or from how we manage it. If a change to the dwelling or to how we manage it may help, start FRM-SDA-01 with them. FRM-SDA-01 asks each other resident affected. Tell the participant the outcome within 2 business days of the decision. If the home may not be able to meet their needs, tell the SDA Manager the same day. The change is agreed, recorded and passed only to the people the participant chose. REG-SDA-02 col BF; REG-SDA-02 col BG; FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling Modification and Adjustment Request Open the row within 2 business days of the report. Pass it on within 2 business days of the participant's agreement (our standard)

t: Tell the participant that the home cannot meet their needs.
x: Tell the participant that the home cannot meet their needs. Telling a participant their home may not suit them can feel like being sent away. It can leave them afraid for their home. FRM-SDA-01 decides the need cannot be met in the dwelling, or the participant's circumstances cannot be accommodated even with adjustments The SDA Manager The Chief Executive first reviews every adjustment, modification and alternative, and confirms in writing that none can work. Then tell the participant in person, in their way, with an advocate or supporter if they want one. Explain what was tried and why it cannot work. Say that they decide whether and when to move, and that no notice has been given. Ask who else they want told, such as their support coordinator and SIL providers. Tell them the same day. Offer help to find another home: the support coordinator, the NDIA, and other SDA providers. They keep their home while they look. Do not serve a notice on this ground unless the Chief Executive, after a second review with the participant and an advocate, decides that the risk to the participant or others cannot otherwise be managed and the law of [state or territory] provides the ground; only then does step 24 start. If they choose to leave, follow PRO-SUP-04 Transitions to or from a Provider Procedure and go to step 28. The participant and the providers they chose know early that another home is needed, and are helped to find one. REG-SDA-02 col BH Within 2 business days of the Chief Executive's confirmation (our standard)

t: Check the rule and the reason for the notice.
x: Check the rule and the reason for the notice. A notice given for the wrong reason ends a home unfairly, and is payback. we plan to give a tenancy notice of any kind The SDA Manager Find the notice rule row for this kind of notice in REG-SDA-02. If there is no row, or it is more than 12 months old, or the law has changed since it was checked, check the law of [state or territory] first, from the dated list in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. You can ask a tenancy advice service or a lawyer. Then enter a new rule row. Write, in this order: the ground the law requires and the evidence that must accompany the notice; the prescribed or approved form; any prerequisite notice; the least notice; how it must be served; who must receive it; the other parties the law requires to be told and by when; and the body that reviews it. Use Decision table 4. Check the reason. It must not be the participant's choice of SIL provider, a refusal to sign an arrangement, a complaint or concern, or a risk they chose. Write who decided and why. For any notice that would end the tenancy, the Chief Executive approves it in writing first. The second approver is never the person who decided. Open a notice row before you serve anything. The notice is lawful, has a real ground and has been checked by a second person. REG-SDA-02 col AU; REG-SDA-02 col AV; REG-SDA-02 col AW; REG-SDA-02 col AX; REG-SDA-02 col T Before any notice is served. The rule row checked inside the last 12 months and since the law last changed (our standard)

t: Hear the participant before you decide.
x: Hear the participant before you decide. the notice would end the tenancy, record a breach, or limit the participant's rights The SDA Manager Tell the participant in person, in their way, what is proposed and why. Give them at least 5 business days to answer, with an advocate, supporter or tenancy adviser if they want one. Show them what we hold. Ask for their account and what would help. Consider it and write how you did. Change the proposal if the facts change. Tell the participant the decision and the reasons in their way. If someone's safety is at risk now, go to step 17 first. Then record why a hearing was not possible, and give it as soon as it is safe. The participant has been heard before anything is decided, and the decision rests on what they said. REG-SDA-02 col AY At least 5 business days for the participant to answer (our standard)

t: Serve the notice as the rule says.
x: Serve the notice as the rule says. A notice that breaks the state rule may be invalid, and leaves the participant unsure whether they must leave. The Tenancy Officer Use the ground, form, method, time, prerequisite notice and recipients in the notice rule row. Give at least the notice the law requires, and any longer period our agreement or our standards promise: at least 90 days for a notice to vacate; the longer of the law and 60 days for a rent change; the longer of the law and 7 days for an inspection entry, 2 business days for a repair the participant asked for, and no notice only in an emergency the law allows. Serve it on the participant, and on their decision maker if there is one. Tell each other party the law requires, by its time limit. With the participant's consent, give a copy to their advocate and SIL provider. Give the participant a copy in the format they chose, and go through it in their way. Cover the date it takes effect, what it means and what they can do. Ask them to say it back. Write the date and time of service, and the date the law treats it as received. For a rent change, also write the new rent in column S. The notice is valid, and the participant understands it. REG-SDA-02 col AZ; REG-SDA-02 col BA; REG-SDA-02 col S On the date the rule row sets, and never with less notice than the law requires (statutory: tenancy law of [state or territory])

t: Tell the participant how to seek a review.
x: Tell the participant how to seek a review. The Tenancy Officer Do this with every notice, and with every decision about their tenancy, a modification or an application. Tell them in their way that they can ask the Chief Executive to look again, and that we answer within 10 business days. Tell them they can complain to us under PRO-FBK-01. They can contact the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. They can ask an independent advocate and get tenancy advice. They can apply to the tribunal or court for [state or territory] within the time in the notice rule row. Offer to help with any of these. Record which they chose. Say that using any of them never puts their home at risk. Where the notice ends the tenancy, offer help to find another home through their support coordinator and, with consent, their SIL providers. If the NDIA must be told, go to step 2. The participant knows they can seek a review, and how, and is helped to do it. REG-SDA-02 col BB; REG-SDA-02 col BC; REG-SDA-02 col BE With the notice, and within 2 business days of any other decision about the tenancy (our standard)

t: End the tenancy.
x: End the tenancy. a participant gives notice, a notice from us takes effect, a participant dies, or the agreement ends by its terms The Tenancy Officer Accept a participant's notice in any form. Open a notice row for it. Ask once, and without pressure, whether anything we did or did not do is behind it. Write the answer. Offer help with the move, through their support coordinator and, with consent, their SIL providers, under PRO-SUP-04. Do a final inspection with the participant. Return the bond, and any rent paid ahead, as the law of [state or territory] requires. Write any deduction and the reason. Tell the NDIA at step 2. Open a vacancy row at step 1. Where a participant has died, the incident process runs first under PRO-INC-01 and PRO-INC-02. Speak with their family or the person they named before anything in their room is moved. The tenancy ends fairly, the bond is settled, and the vacancy is on the record. REG-SDA-02 col W; REG-SDA-02 col U; REG-SDA-02 col BE Final inspection and bond return as the law requires (statutory: tenancy law of [state or territory]). The vacancy row within 1 business day (our standard)

t: Review the register.
x: Review the register. The SDA Manager Each week, read the open vacancy rows. Check the days since the event, the NDIA notices due and any funding limit date within 14 days. Each month, read the whole register. Look for tenancies with no arrangement row, arrangement reviews due within 60 days, and notice rows with no second approval, hearing or review rights. Look at REG-FBK-01 and REG-SDA-01 for each dwelling, for the days to acknowledge and to answer. Check that each incident at a dwelling in REG-INC-01 has a home event row. Check each notice rule row due for checking within 60 days, and enter a new row if the law changed. Give each gap an owner and a due date. Enter each in REG-QMS-01. Enter a review row. Gaps are found while there is still time to fix them, and each review leaves a dated record. REG-SDA-02 col BO; REG-SDA-02 col AV Every week for vacancies. Every month for the whole register (our standard)

t: Report on tenancy management to the Chief Executive and the governing body.
x: Report on tenancy management to the Chief Executive and the governing body. The Quality Manager Every 3 months, trace five rows of each record type to their source records. Show the days to tell the NDIA, the days each place stayed vacant, and whether every resident was asked before each offer. Show tenancies with no arrangement, and each decision. Show every notice that ended or limited a tenancy, with its hearing and review rights. Show concerns, conflicts, harm and changes, with the times met and missed. List the trends and the actions. The Chief Executive and the governing body record decisions in their minutes and in REG-QMS-01. Where there is no governing body, send the report to the independent contact for concerns. Every 12 months, also ask a sample of participants and applicants how clear and fair the vacancy and notice process was. Check every notice rule row. Recommend changes to POL-SDA-05 and to this procedure. The people who govern [Provider name] see how tenancies are managed and decide what to change. REG-SDA-02 col BO; REG-QMS-01 Every 3 months. The wider check every 12 months (our standard)

t: Decision table 1: how we choose (steps 3, 5 and 8). Every applicant is checked on the same
x: Decision table 1: how we choose (steps 3, 5 and 8). Every applicant is checked on the same criteria. No. Criterion What we check How it counts 1 SDA funding and fit The applicant's plan includes SDA funding. The dwelling has the design category and building type in their plan, or the NDIA has agreed in writing that this dwelling can be funded for them. The place is a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share. The residents after the move do not exceed the enrolled number Must be met 2 Needs The dwelling, and the supports that would be in place, can meet the applicant's needs. Ask the applicant and, with consent, their support coordinator or SIL provider Must be met 3 The applicant's own wishes Whether they want this home, its location and this household, as far as they know it. Location can mean nearness to family, work or community Weighs in favour 4 The residents' views What each resident said about living with a new person. A worry about safety is settled under Decision table 2 Weighs in favour 5 Order of application The date the applicant applied Used only between applicants who are equal on criteria 3 and 4 We never choose, or refuse, because of an applicant's age, diagnosis or type of disability alone, race, religion, sex or sexuality. We never choose because of who delivers their other supports, or whether they use our other services. We never choose because of a gift or reward. Decision table 2: what the resident says (steps 6 and 7). The resident says Then They have no worry, or no view Record it. Do not ask again unless the shortlist changes They want to meet the person first Offer a meeting at a time that suits both, with a supporter, if the applicant agrees. Record what each says afterwards They are worried about daily life together, such as noise, routines or shared spaces Meet them at step 7. Ask what would make it work. Pass any workable idea to the applicant before the offer They do not feel safe with the person Do not offer the place to that applicant until the resident says the worry is settled. c: AGR-SDA-02 What this agreement is for
t: This agreement sets out how a participant, their specialist disability accommodation (SDA)
w: SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement
x: This agreement sets out how a participant, their specialist disability accommodation (SDA) provider and each of their supported independent living (SIL) providers will work together. Its aim is that the participant's home works for them and for the people they live with. In this agreement "you" is the participant. "We" is [Provider name], the SDA provider, who owns or manages the dwelling. A "SIL provider" is any other NDIS provider that delivers supported independent living supports to you in the dwelling. It is one agreement with one copy for each party. A SIL provider can attach it to its own service agreement with you, and we can attach it to your SDA service agreement. Neither attachment changes either of those agreements. Nothing here limits your rights under your tenancy law or the NDIS rules. Complete it when you move in, when you get a new SIL provider, when something in it changes and at least every 12 months. The Tenancy Officer completes Sections A and B with you first, and then takes the same draft to each SIL provider. Where [Provider name] also provides your SIL, the SDA Manager signs for the home and the Service Manager signs for the supports; a sole trader signs once and the independent contact for concerns named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register countersigns. This agreement authorises no restrictive practice and no limit on your visitors, belongings or movement.

Each time in these Terms is our standard, and Section B of the Schedule can set a shorter time. A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where you live. "Provider party" means us and each SIL provider; the duties in these Terms that say "each provider party" are theirs, not yours.

t: If violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination happens or is alleged, each pr

Each provider party reports as the NDIS Incident Rules require for its own supports; question 9 says who notifies the NDIS Commission, whether both providers must, who leads the investigation, who tells you and the people you choose, and how the providers share findings with your consent. For us, our Quality Manager decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware where it involves death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm, and otherwise within 5 business days. A provider party who learns of it tells the other provider parties: the same day if the dwelling is unsafe or damaged, and within 1 business day in any other case. We support each person affected. The person harmed keeps their home. You have no reporting duty under this term.

x: Section B says whether behaviours of concern matter for you. Where they do, your behaviour support plan stays with the people who write it and carry it out; we do not hold or act on its content. We take no tenancy action about behaviour until we have spoken with you and offered you an advocate. We also ask your behaviour support practitioner and SIL provider, with your agreement, what would help. If we are ever asked to apply a lock, camera, gate or visitor limit, we would be an implementing provider and would need the state or territory authorisation and the NDIS Commission reporting the law requires; a SIL provider's request alone never allows it.

If you need a change to the dwelling, we decide it under FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling Modification and Adjustment Request, after asking each other resident affected. If the dwelling can no longer meet your needs, we tell you first, in person, within 2 business days of confirming it. We then help you look for another home.

Your SIL provider helps you take part if you ask.

If the dwelling cannot be used, we tell you the same day what we are doing and who is helping. We work with your SIL provider and the NDIA to find you a temporary place that meets your needs as soon as possible, and within 24 hours. We keep your tenancy, and you pay no rent for any time you cannot live in the dwelling.

t: SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] manages each tenancy in its
x: This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] manages each tenancy in its specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwellings. Each row is one record. It shows what was done, who took part, what the participant said and chose, and who checked. It holds nine kinds of record: tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, notice rule, notice, change, home event, concern and review. An arrangement is the agreement with the participant's supported independent living (SIL) providers. A concern is anything raised about a dwelling that is not yet a complaint, a repair or an incident. Complaints, incidents and repairs are not copied here. They stay in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register, REG-INC-01 Incident Register and REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register. A row here links to them in column O. In this register: "SDA Conditions Rule" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018. "SDA Rules 2020" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. "Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018. "Complaints Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Complaints Management and Resolution) Rules 2018. "Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018. "SDA Manager" means the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. "Tenancy Officer" means the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. "Business day" means a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. Indicators evidenced: s 72 (1) to (5), (8) and (9), including s 72 (3)(a) to (3)(h). Columns O and BL link to the complaints and incident records that evidence s 72 (6) and (7); those indicators are proved by the complaints and incident systems, not here. A SIL provider that signs an arrangement can use its arrangement row for Module 5A, sections 72A to 72E (from 1 July 2026). Legal basis: NDIS Act 2013, section 73F(2)(a) and (c). It makes compliance with the law and the NDIS Practice Standards a condition of registration. The SDA Conditions Rule (sections 6 and 8 to 11) and the SDA Rules 2020 (sections 24, 29 and 32) set duties; section 37 of the SDA Rules 2020 is the equivalent of Conditions Rule section 10(2)(b) for registered providers of supports. This register evidences them. No NDIS rule sets the columns. They are our standard, built from the indicators and those duties. Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years, so 7 years is also the statutory floor. An incident or complaint record has its own limit. It is 7 years from the day it is made (statutory: Incident Rules, section 12(4); Complaints Rules, section 10(3)). Other law can require longer, for example tenancy law about bonds. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed. Which columns apply: Every row fills columns A to O. These are the spine. A tenancy row also fills columns P to W. An arrangement row also fills columns X to AH. Every tenancy has an arrangement row. Where no SIL provider delivers supports in the dwelling to the participant, the row says so and sets a date to check again. A vacancy row also fills columns AI to AT. A notice rule row fills columns AU and AV. A notice row also fills columns AW to BE. A change row also fills columns BF to BH. A home event row also fills columns BI to BN. A review row also fills column BO. A concern row also fills columns BP to BS.

t: The SDA Manager owns the register and approves the closing of every row. The Tenancy Offic
x: The SDA Manager owns the register and approves the closing of every row. The Tenancy Officer adds tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, change and concern rows. The SDA Manager adds notice rows, notice rule rows, home event rows and monthly review rows. The Tenancy Officer completes the service and review rights columns of a notice row, and opens a notice row for a participant's own notice. The Quality Manager adds the 3-monthly and 12-monthly review rows. Add a row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Five rows are faster. Open a vacancy row within 1 business day of learning of the vacancy. Open a home event row within 1 business day. Open a concern row within 1 business day, when the concern is acknowledged. Open a notice rule row before the first notice of that kind. Enter a notice row before the notice is served. Use one row for each event. Where a record concerns several residents, columns AM, AO and AP hold one dated line for each person. Name participants by participant number. Name applicants by applicant number only. Never write an applicant's name in this register. Keep health details, diagnoses and behaviour support plan content out of the register. Put them on the participant's own file and give the file reference in column N. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason. A new SIL provider, or a change to who is responsible for a matter, is a new arrangement row. Set the old row to "superseded" on the same day. Nobody enters or approves a row about their own decision. The second approver in column AX is never the person who decided. When systems are down, write the record on paper. Enter the row within 2 business days of the system coming back. A row is closed only when all of these are true: every column required for its record type is filled each action in column J is done, or sits in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date the participant was told the outcome, and column K shows the date and way the SDA Manager has approved closing. A tenancy row stays "current" until column W is filled. An arrangement row stays "current" until a new row supersedes it. A vacancy row closes when column AT is filled, or when the SDA Manager records that the place is withdrawn. A notice rule row stays "current" until the law changes and a new row supersedes it. A notice row closes when column BE shows the result. A change row closes when column BG or column BH is filled and the participant was told. A home event row closes when the action in column BM is done, or is tracked in REG-QMS-01. A concern row closes when column BR is filled and column BS shows where it went and how the person was told.

x: The SDA Manager, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row. The Tenancy Officer can see every row, including review rows, which they read and cannot change, and adds the rows named in the entry rules. They can read, and cannot change, a row about their own decision. A participant can ask for any row about them or their home. We remove other people's details first. A SIL provider sees only the arrangement row for a participant who agreed to it in column AE, and only the columns that agreement covers. An applicant sees only their own lines in columns AM to AS. An auditor or the NDIS Commission sees rows only as the law allows or requires. Rows hold personal information about participants and applicants. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper record. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets the wider privacy rules.
